title: Book of Enoch — Restored Names Edition
front_matter:
Introduction

The Books of Enoch—primarily the Ethiopic 1 Enoch preserved in
full—stand as one of the most profound and misunderstood treasures of
ancient inspired literature. Attributed to Enoch, the seventh from Adam,
who “walked with Elohim (God), and he was not, for Elohim (God) took
him” (Genesis 5:24), this text unveils visions of the heavens, the fall
of the watchers, the secrets of creation, astronomical order, dream
prophecies, and eschatological judgment. Composed in stages between the
3rd century BCE and the 1st century CE, it circulated widely among the
righteous in the Second Temple period, influencing the Dead Sea Scrolls
community and echoing directly in the Renewed Covenant.

The Epistle of Yahudah (Jude) quotes Enoch explicitly: “And Enoch, the
seventh from Adam, prophesied about these men also, saying, ‘Behold,
Yahuah (God) comes with ten thousands of His set-apart ones, to execute
judgment on all, to convict all who are wicked of all their wicked works
which they have done in a wicked way, and of all the harsh things which
wicked sinners have spoken against Him’” (Jude 1:14-15, cf. Enoch 1:9).
This is no mere allusion—Yahudah (Judah) treats Enoch’s words as
authoritative prophecy. Hebrews 11:5 praises Enoch’s faith and
translation, while other New Testament passages (e.g., 2 Peter 2:4 on
angels in chains, Revelation’s apocalyptic imagery) bear clear marks of
Enochian influence. Far from irrelevant, these writings illuminate the
canonical narrative, filling in details about the sons of Elohim
(Genesis 6:1-4), the pre-flood world, and the coming Day of Yahuah
(God).

Yet lies have clouded this light for centuries. Some falsely claim Enoch
portrays Enoch himself as the Messiah—a distortion nowhere supported in
the text. Enoch is the righteous scribe and visionary who beholds the
Son of Man and the Elect One (Enoch 46–48, 71), pointing forward to the
true Messiah (Christ), not claiming the role. Others twist Enoch’s
364-day solar calendar (detailed in chapters 72–82) into endorsement of
a “false” system, ignoring how it aligns with Yahuah’s ordained feasts,
sabbaths, and creation order (cf. Jubilees 6; Genesis 1). Mainstream
traditions dismiss Enoch as non-canonical fringe, stripping its
prophetic weight to maintain control over interpretation. We reject
these deceptions. And we read this text as Scripture reads itself—as the
account of the seed of promise, the Adamic line and their history with
Yahuah (God). It is not a chronicle of all humanity or a world history,
but the record of the covenant family, told from inside the covenant
family, for those being gathered home.

One phrase in this book needs orienting before the reader meets it. “Son
of man” — in Hebrew “ben adam” — means son of Adam. It is a
seed-designation, marking a human as of the Adamic lineage. Scripture
uses it in two registers. In the creaturely register it addresses a
righteous prophet: Ezekiel hears it ninety-three times; Enoch hears it
in 60:10 and again in 71:14 as the Head of Days confirms his son-of-Adam
lineage. In the prophetic register it names the Messiah — the Formed of
the Formless coming to walk as a son of Adam — in the Parables’ visions
of the Elect One (chapters 46, 48, 62, 63, 69:30–33), in Daniel 7:13,
and in Yahusha’s (Jesus’s) own self-designation throughout the Gospels.
Yahusha (Jesus) was quoting Enoch’s usage. Enoch is the only other text
that calls the Messiah by that phrase, which is what gives the Gospels’
son-of-man sayings their Christological depth. Read both registers in
the Parables as they appear. The distinction holds through Chapter 71,
where Enoch is addressed in the creaturely register as the son of Adam
he was, while the Elect One — who has been the son of man throughout the
Parables — remains seated on the throne of glory.

This Sacred Name Edition restores what tradition obscured: the divine
Name Yahuah (God) (replacing “Lord”), Elohim (God) (for “God”), Elohanu
(“our Elohim (God)”), El Shaddai, and related titles, drawing from
faithful Hebrew-root restorations. No more substitutions that veil the
personal, covenant Name proclaimed forever (Exodus 3:15; Psalm 83:18;
Isaiah 42:8). We present the full 108 chapters, divided into its
traditional sections:

-   The Book of the Watchers (Chapters 1–36): The fall of the angels,
    their judgment, and Enoch’s heavenly journeys.
-   The Book of Parables (Chapters 37–71): Visions of the Elect One, the
    Son of Man, and final judgment.
-   The Book of the Heavenly Luminaries (Chapters 72–82): Yahuah’s
    ordered cosmos and calendar.
-   Dream Visions (Chapters 83–90): History in animal allegory, from
    creation to the Messianic kingdom.
-   The Epistle of Enoch (Chapters 91–108): Exhortations, the Apocalypse
    of Weeks, and birth of Noah.

Accompanying the text are canonical cross-references (linking to Torah,
Prophets, Writings, and Renewed Covenant) and commentary that exposes
myths, provides historical context (e.g., Qumran fragments confirming
antiquity), and encourages discernment. Unlike indoctrinating study
Bibles that reinforce traditions, our notes peel away scales—questioning
assumptions, highlighting Yahuah’s unchanging truth, and empowering you
to test all things (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

Enoch’s words were preserved for such a time as this—to awaken the
remnant, reveal hidden things (Daniel 12:4), and prepare for the
restoration of all things. May reading this ignite your spirit,
unindoctrinate your mind, and draw you closer to Yahuah (God), whose
Name we now proclaim without fear.

chapters.title: The Blessing and Prophecy of Enoch

verses.text: The words of the blessing of Enoch, wherewith he blessed the elect and righteous, who will be living in the day of tribulation, when all the wicked and godless are to be removed.

And he took up his parable and said—Enoch a righteous man, whose eyes were opened by Elohim (God), saw the vision of the Holy One in the heavens, which the angels showed me, and from them I heard everything, and from them I understood as I saw, but not for this generation, but for a remote one which is for to come.
Concerning the elect I said, and took up my parable concerning them: The Holy Great One will come forth from His dwelling,
And the eternal Elohim (God) will tread upon the earth, (even) on Mount Sinai, [And appear from His camp] And appear in the strength of His might from the heaven of heavens.
And all shall be smitten with fear And the Watchers shall quake, And great fear and trembling shall seize them unto the ends of the earth.
And the high mountains shall be shaken, And the high hills shall be made low, And shall melt like wax before the flame
And the earth shall be wholly rent in sunder, And all that is upon the earth shall perish, And there shall be a judgement upon all (men).

But with the righteous He will make peace. And will protect the elect, And mercy shall be upon them. And they shall all belong to Elohim (God), And they shall be prospered, And they shall all be blessed. And He will help them all, And light shall appear unto them, And He will make peace with them.

And behold! He cometh with ten thousands of His set-apart ones To execute judgement upon all, And to destroy all the ungodly: And to convict all flesh Of all the works of their ungodliness which they have ungodly committed, And of all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against Him.

chapters.commentary: This chapter functions as the superscription and opening oracle for the entire Book of the Watchers (Chapters 1–36), framing the visions to follow as a prophetic blessing for the righteous elect amid coming tribulation. Enoch is presented as a faithful recipient of divine revelation—his eyes “opened by Elohim (God)”—who speaks not for his own time but for a distant future generation facing judgment and deliverance. - Verses 1–2: The blessing targets the elect righteous enduring a “day of tribulation,” when the wicked are removed. Enoch’s vision comes via angels from the Holy One, emphasizing prophetic foresight for end-times encouragement rather than immediate application. - Cross-refs: Genesis 5:24 (Enoch walked with Elohim (God) and was taken); Hebrews 11:5 (by faith Enoch was translated, that he should not see death… he pleased Elohim (God)). - Verses 3–4: A majestic theophany—Yahuah (the Holy Great One, eternal Elohim (God)) coming forth from His dwelling, treading on earth (Mount Sinai imagery), appearing in heavenly might. - Cross-refs: Deuteronomy 33:2 (Yahuah (God) came from Sinai… with ten thousands of set-apart ones); Habakkuk 3:3–6 (Elohim (God) came from Teman… mountains shook before Him); Psalm 68:17–18 (chariots of Elohim (God)… Sinai in holiness). - Verses 5–7: Cosmic terror at Yahuah’s approach—the Watchers (angelic beings) quake, mountains shake and melt, earth rends, signaling universal judgment on humanity. - Cross-refs: Isaiah 24:19–20 (the earth is utterly broken… reels like a drunkard); Micah 1:4 (mountains melt under Him like wax before fire); Revelation 6:14 (sky receded as a scroll… every mountain and island moved out of its place). - Verse 8: Contrast—peace, protection, mercy, prosperity, blessing, and light for the righteous elect, who belong to Elohim (God). - Cross-refs: Psalm 37:11 (the meek shall inherit the earth and delight in abundant peace); Isaiah 57:19 (“Peace, peace, to the far and to the near,” says Yahuah (God)); Romans 5:1 (peace with Elohim (God) through our Master Yahusha (Jesus) Messiah). - Verse 9: Climax—Yahuah (God) comes with ten thousands of His set-apart ones to judge, destroy the ungodly, and convict all flesh of wicked deeds and blasphemous words. - Cross-refs: Jude 1:14–15 (direct quotation: “Behold, Yahuah (God) comes with ten thousands of His set-apart ones, to execute judgment on all, to convict all the ungodly of all their deeds…”); Zechariah 14:5 (Yahuah (God) my Elohim (God) will come, and all the set-apart ones with Him); Matthew 25:31 (the Son of Man comes in His glory… with all the holy angels); 1 Thessalonians 3:13 (at the coming of our Master Yahusha (Jesus) with all His set-apart ones); Deuteronomy 33:2 (He came with ten thousands of set-apart ones). Key Insight for Discernment: Chapter 1 establishes an eschatological framework of judgment and salvation, rooted in Sinai theophany traditions but projected forward to ultimate divine intervention. The direct citation in Jude treats this as prophetic truth, showing early believers drew from such writings for insight into Yahuah’s coming judgment—without requiring full canonization. This invites testing: compare with Torah promises of blessing for obedience and curse for rebellion (Deuteronomy 28–30), and hold fast to what aligns with the full counsel of Scripture (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Orderly Works of Elohim (God) in Creation

verses.text: Observe ye everything that takes place in the heaven, how they do not change their orbits, and the luminaries which are in the heaven, how they all rise and set in order each in its season, and transgress not against their appointed order.

Behold ye the earth, and give heed to the things which take place upon it from first to last, how steadfast they are, how none of the things upon earth change, but all the works of Elohim (God) appear to you.
Behold the summer and the winter, how the whole earth is filled with water, and clouds and dew and rain lie upon it.

chapters.commentary: This brief chapter serves as a transitional exhortation, urging observation of the created order to highlight Elohim’s sovereignty and reliability. It builds on Chapter 1’s prophetic judgment by presenting nature’s perfect obedience as a silent testimony against future disobedience (from humanity and the Watchers in subsequent chapters). Enoch calls for attentive looking (“observe,” “behold,” “give heed”)—a call to discernment through creation itself, revealing Elohim’s unchanging faithfulness. - Verse 1: The heavenly bodies (sun, moon, stars) maintain fixed orbits, rising and setting precisely in their seasons without deviation or transgression. - Cross-refs: Genesis 1:14–18 (Elohim (God) set lights in the firmament for signs, seasons, days, years… to rule day and night); Psalm 104:19 (He appointed the moon for seasons; the sun knows its going down); Jeremiah 31:35 (Yahuah (God) who gives the sun for light by day… the ordinances of the moon and stars… do not fail). - Verse 2: The earth and its processes remain steadfast from beginning to end; nothing changes, and all works of Elohim (God) are evident and reliable. - Cross-refs: Psalm 93:1 (the world is established, so that it cannot be moved); Psalm 104:5 (He laid the foundations of the earth, that it should not be removed forever); Ecclesiastes 1:4–7 (one generation passes… the earth abides forever… the sun rises and sets… the wind goes… rivers run into the sea); Romans 1:20 (the invisible attributes of Elohim (God)… are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made). - Verse 3: Seasonal cycles (summer/winter) bring water, clouds, dew, and rain to cover the earth—illustrating provision and renewal in Elohim’s design. - Cross-refs: Genesis 8:22 (while the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter… shall not cease); Job 37:6–13 (He says to the snow, ‘Be on the earth’… He causes it to come… for correction, or for His land, or for mercy); Psalm 147:8 (He covers the heavens with clouds, prepares rain for the earth); Joel 2:23 (be glad… for He has given you the former rain faithfully). Key Insight for Discernment: Chapter 2 uses creation as a mirror of Elohim’s character—orderly, faithful, transgressing nothing. This sets up a stark contrast with the chaos introduced by rebellious angels and sinful humanity later in the book. It invites readers to “behold” the evidence of Elohim’s handiwork as a foundation for trusting His judgments (from Ch. 1) and promises. Scripture repeatedly echoes this: the heavens declare Elohim’s glory (Psalm 19:1), and ignoring creation’s testimony hardens hearts (Romans 1:20–21). Test all things by observing what Elohim (God) has established unchangingly (1 Thessalonians 5:21; Acts 17:11).

chapters.title: The Trees and Their Seasons

verses.text: Observe and see how (in the winter) all the trees seem as though they had withered and shed all their leaves, except fourteen trees, which do not lose their foliage but retain the old foliage from two to three years till the new comes.

And again, observe the days of summer how the sun is above the earth over against it. And you seek shade and shelter by reason of the heat of the sun, and the earth also is burning with growing heat, and so you cannot tread on the earth, or on a rock by reason of its heat.

chapters.commentary: This short chapter continues Enoch’s call to “observe” creation, now turning to the trees as living examples of Elohim’s designed cycles. It contrasts the apparent “death” of most trees in winter (shedding leaves) with the evergreen persistence of fourteen specific trees, which hold old foliage until new growth arrives. The summer description then highlights the sun’s intense heat, making shade necessary and the ground itself scorching—illustrating both provision (evergreens, shade) and the power of Elohim’s ordinances. - Verse 1: Most trees appear lifeless in winter, losing leaves, yet fourteen retain foliage for two or three years until renewal. This points to Elohim’s preservation amid seasonal change—orderly dormancy followed by revival. - Cross-refs: Psalm 1:3 (the righteous… is like a tree planted by streams of water that yields its fruit in its season; its leaf does not wither); Jeremiah 17:8 (blessed is the man who trusts in Yahuah (God)… like a tree planted by water… its leaves remain green); Psalm 104:16–17 (the trees of Yahuah (God) are full of sap, the cedars of Lebanon which He planted… where the birds make their nests); Job 14:7–9 (there is hope for a tree, if it is cut down, that it will sprout again… at the scent of water it will bud). - Verse 2: Summer’s blazing sun scorches the earth, driving people to seek shade and making bare ground untreadable—showing the intensity of Elohim’s created forces and the need for His provision (shade, shelter). - Cross-refs: Genesis 8:22 (while the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat… shall not cease); Psalm 121:5–6 (Yahuah (God) is your keeper… the sun shall not strike you by day); Isaiah 25:4 (You have been a shelter from the storm, a shade from the heat); Jonah 4:6–8 (Yahuah (God) appointed a plant… to give shade… then a scorching east wind); Revelation 7:16 (they shall neither hunger anymore nor thirst anymore; the sun shall not strike them). Key Insight for Discernment: Chapter 3 reinforces the message of Chapters 1–2: creation obeys Elohim (God) without fail—trees follow their appointed cycles, the sun governs heat and seasons precisely. This steadfastness testifies to Elohim’s faithfulness and invites reflection on human responsibility to align with His order. Scripture uses similar imagery to describe the blessed life (evergreen, fruitful trees) and warns against straying from Yahuah’s ways, which leads to withering (Jeremiah 17:5–6). Observe creation, as Enoch urges, and let it point you back to the Creator who sustains it all (Romans 1:20; Psalm 19:1–4). Hold fast to what is unchanging and true (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Heat of Summer

verses.text: And again, observe ye the days of summer how the sun is above the earth over against it. And you seek shade and shelter by reason of the heat of the sun, and the earth also burns with growing heat, and so you cannot tread on the earth, or on a rock by reason of its heat.

chapters.commentary: This single-verse chapter (often seen as an extension of Chapter 3’s summer description) intensifies the call to observe Elohim’s created order, now emphasizing the scorching power of the sun in summer. The relentless heat forces people to seek shade and makes the ground itself untreadable—illustrating both the might of Elohim’s ordinances and humanity’s dependence on His provisions (like shade or relief). It underscores the theme of unchanging natural laws: the sun dominates without deviation, mirroring the reliability seen in previous chapters. - Verse 1: The sun’s position high overhead brings oppressive heat; earth and rocks become scorching, compelling shelter-seeking and limiting movement. - Cross-refs: Genesis 8:22 (while the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat… shall not cease); Psalm 121:5–6 (Yahuah (God) is your keeper; Yahuah (God) is your shade at your right hand. The sun shall not strike you by day); Isaiah 25:4 (You have been a refuge for the poor… a shade from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall); Jonah 4:6–8 (Yahuah (God) appointed a plant… to give shade over his head… but when the sun arose… a scorching east wind); Revelation 7:16 (they shall neither hunger anymore nor thirst anymore; the sun shall not strike them, nor any heat). Key Insight for Discernment: Chapter 4 keeps the focus on creation’s faithful obedience—the sun fulfills its role precisely, providing both life-giving light/heat and a test of endurance. This reliability points to Elohim’s sovereignty: He who commands the seasons does not waver (Psalm 104:19–23; Jeremiah 33:20–21). Enoch urges us to “observe” these patterns as evidence of divine faithfulness, encouraging alignment with Elohim’s ways rather than rebellion. Scripture uses heat/shade imagery to contrast judgment (scorching for the wicked) and mercy (shade for the righteous)—let creation’s testimony draw you to trust Yahuah’s unchanging character (Romans 1:20; Psalm 19:1–4). Test and hold fast (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: Creation’s Obedience vs. Human Rebellion

verses.text: Observe ye how the trees cover themselves with green leaves and bear fruit: wherefore give ye heed and know with regard to all His works, and recognize how He that liveth for ever hath made them so.
And all His works go on thus from year to year for ever, and all the tasks which they accomplish for Him, and their tasks change not, but according as Elohim (God) hath ordained so is it done.
And behold how the sea and the rivers in like manner accomplish and change not their tasks from His commandments.

But ye—ye have not been steadfast, nor done the commandments of Yahuah (God), but ye have turned away and spoken proud and hard words with your impure mouths against His greatness. Oh, ye hard-hearted, ye shall find no peace.
Therefore shall ye execrate your days, and the years of your life shall perish, and the years of your destruction shall be multiplied in eternal execration; and ye shall find no compassion.

And in those days ye shall make your names an eternal execration unto all the righteous, and by you shall the godless be cursed, and all the sinners and godless shall imprecate by you, saying: “May the godless be far away from us, and their deeds be far from us.”

But to the righteous and holy He will grant peace, and He will protect the elect, and compassion shall be upon them; and they shall all belong to Elohim (God), and they shall be prospered, and they shall all be blessed. And He will help them all, and light shall appear unto them, and He will make peace with them.

And behold! He cometh with ten thousands of His set-apart ones to execute judgement upon all, and to destroy all the ungodly: and to convict all flesh of all the works of their ungodliness which they have ungodly committed, and of all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against Him.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 5 concludes the introductory exhortation section (chs. 1–5), contrasting creation’s perfect obedience with humanity’s rebellion. Nature (trees fruiting yearly, seas/rivers flowing per command) testifies to Elohim’s unchanging sovereignty, while humans speak proud words, disobey commandments, and face curses—no peace, eternal execration. The righteous receive peace, protection, blessing, light, and ultimate deliverance. The chapter echoes Ch. 1’s judgment theophany, bridging to the Watchers’ fall in Ch. 6. - Verses 1–3: Trees, seas, and rivers fulfill ordained tasks without deviation—evidence of Elohim’s eternal life and design. - Cross-refs: Psalm 104:5–9 (earth set on foundations… boundaries for waters… they do not transgress); Jeremiah 5:22 (fear Yahuah (God)… who set the sand as boundary for the sea… waves toss but cannot prevail); Job 38:8–11 (Yahuah (God) shut in the sea… “Thus far shall you come, and no farther”); Psalm 148:8 (fire, hail, snow, clouds… fulfilling His word); Genesis 1:11–12, 20–22 (creation produces after its kind by Elohim’s command). - Verses 4–6: Humanity’s rebellion—disobedience, proud/hard/impure words against Yahuah’s greatness—leads to no peace, cursed days/years, eternal execration, and becoming a curse-word among the righteous. - Cross-refs: Isaiah 57:20–21 (“The wicked are like the tossing sea… there is no peace,” says Yahuah (God)); Deuteronomy 28:15–20 (curses for disobedience: confusion, rebuke in all undertakings); Psalm 109:17–18 (curses return on the wicked); Romans 3:13–14 (throats open graves… mouths full of cursing and bitterness); James 3:5–6 (tongue sets on fire… a world of evil). - Verse 7: Contrast—peace, protection, compassion, belonging to Elohim (God), prosperity, blessing, help, light, and peace for the righteous/elect/holy. - Cross-refs: Psalm 37:11 (meek inherit earth, delight in abundant peace); Isaiah 57:19 (“Peace, peace, to the far and near,” says Yahuah (God)); Romans 5:1 (peace with Elohim (God) through Master Yahusha (Jesus) Messiah); Numbers 6:24–26 (Yahuah (God) bless/keep/make face shine/give peace); Matthew 5:9 (peacemakers called sons of Elohim (God)). - Verse 8: Climax—Yahuah (God) comes with ten thousands of set-apart ones for universal judgment, destroying ungodly, convicting all flesh of ungodly works and hard/blasphemous words. - Cross-refs: Jude 1:14–15 (direct quote: “Behold, Yahuah (God) comes with ten thousands of His set-apart ones, to execute judgment… convict all the ungodly”); Deuteronomy 33:2 (Yahuah (God) came from Sinai… with ten thousands of set-apart ones); Zechariah 14:5 (Yahuah (God) my Elohim (God) will come, all set-apart ones with Him); Matthew 25:31 (Son of Man comes in glory with all holy angels); 1 Thessalonians 3:13 (coming of Master Yahusha (Jesus) with all His set-apart ones). Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 5 uses creation’s flawless obedience as a mirror to expose human sin and pride—nature never rebels, but we do, speaking against Yahuah (God) and earning curses. Yet hope shines for the elect: peace, light, and ultimate vindication at Yahuah’s coming judgment. This sets up the Watchers’ fall (chs. 6–16) as cosmic rebellion’s consequence. Test traditions that downplay these texts—Jude quotes Enoch authoritatively, Hebrews praises Enoch’s walk, and Revelation echoes apocalyptic imagery. Compare to Torah’s obedience/blessing vs. rebellion/curse (Deuteronomy 28–30), and hold fast to what aligns with Scripture’s full counsel (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21). Yahuah’s order is unchanging—align with it, reject pride, and find peace in Him.

chapters.title: The Descent of the Watchers

verses.text: And it came to pass when the children of men had multiplied that in those days were born unto them beautiful and comely daughters.
And the angels, the children of the heaven, saw and lusted after them, and said to one another: ‘Come, let us choose us wives from among the children of men and beget us children.’
And Shemyaza, who was their leader, said unto them: ‘I fear ye will not indeed agree to do this deed, and I alone shall have to pay the penalty of a great sin.’
And they all answered him and said: ‘Let us all swear an oath, and all bind ourselves by mutual imprecations not to abandon this plan but to do this thing.’
Then sware they all together and bound themselves by mutual imprecations upon it.

And they were in all two hundred; who descended in the days of Yered (Jared) on the summit of Mount Hermon, and they called it Mount Hermon, because they had sworn and bound themselves by mutual imprecations upon it.

And these are the names of their leaders: Shemyaza, who was their leader, Arakiba, Rameel, Kokabiel, Tamiel, Ramiel, Danel, Ezeqeel, Baraqijal, Asael, Armaros, Batarel, Ananel, Zaqiel, Shamsiel, Sathariel, Turiel, Yomiel, Sariel.
These are their chiefs of tens.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 6 introduces the core narrative of the Book of the Watchers: the fall of angelic beings (the “Watchers”) who abandon their heavenly station to pursue forbidden unions with human women. This act of rebellion—driven by lust—sets in motion the corruption that leads to the pre-flood judgment (echoing Genesis 6:1–4). The chapter names the leaders and describes their solemn oath on Mount Hermon, emphasizing deliberate, collective defiance against Elohim’s order. The Sons of Elohim (God) and the Question of Origin The existing commentary on Chapter 6 correctly identifies the sons of Elohim (God) as heavenly beings and rightly dismisses the Sethite interpretation. But it leaves the reader at that door without walking them through it. A deeper question waits on the other side. - Verses 1–2: Human population growth produces beautiful daughters; the angels (“children of heaven”) see, lust, and conspire to take wives and beget offspring. - Cross-refs: Genesis 6:1–2 (“When men began to multiply… the sons of Elohim (God) saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives”); Job 1:6, 2:1 (sons of Elohim (God) present themselves before Yahuah (God)); Job 38:7 (morning stars sang together, and all the sons of Elohim (God) shouted for joy—pre-fall angelic state). - Verses 3–5: Shemyaza (leader) fears the sin’s penalty but the group swears a binding oath of mutual imprecation to ensure none back out—highlighting willful, unified rebellion. - Cross-refs: 2 Peter 2:4 (Elohim (God) did not spare the angels who sinned, but cast them down to hell and delivered them into chains of darkness); Jude 1:6 (the angels who did not keep their proper domain… He has reserved in everlasting chains under darkness for the judgment of the great day). - Verses 6–8: The 200 descend in the days of Yered (Jared, Enoch’s father) onto Mount Hermon; their oath names the mountain (“Hermon” from “oath/curse”). List of 20 named chiefs (of tens), with Shemyaza as overall leader. - Cross-refs: Genesis 5:18–20 (Yered lived… begot Enoch); Deuteronomy 3:8–9 (Mount Hermon… called Sirion by the Sidonians, Senir by the Amorites—geographic note); Psalm 133:3 (dew of Hermon… life forevermore—ironic contrast to its use here as site of rebellion). Key Insight for Discernment: This chapter explains the “sons of Elohim (God)” in Genesis 6 not as mere humans or Sethites (a common traditional interpretation), but as heavenly beings who transgressed boundaries set by Elohim (God). Their oath and descent mark intentional rebellion, leading to hybrid offspring (Nephilim/giants in later verses) and widespread corruption. Scripture affirms angelic sin and judgment (2 Peter, Jude), using Enoch’s account to provide detail without contradicting Torah. Observe how Elohim’s order—upheld by creation (Ch. 2–5)—is violated here by those who should have known better. Let this warn against crossing divine boundaries and pursuing forbidden desires. Test interpretations against the full witness of Scripture (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21). Now I have everything. Here are the four supplemental commentary sections, written in MTM’s existing style but upgraded with your theological framework: Supplemental Commentary Sections The “daughters of men” in verse 1 require a question the text itself demands: whose daughters, and from whom descended? Genesis does not record one creation event. It records two distinct ones. Genesis 1 records the creation of male and female humanity — the peoples of the earth, created on the sixth day. Genesis 2 records something separate: Adam, formed specifically from the dust, animated by the direct breath of Elohim (God), placed in a garden, given a priestly calling and a covenant charge. Adam was not the first human on earth in the general sense. He was the first of a specific appointed seed — set apart with a distinct lineage, a distinct vocation, and a distinct covenant relationship with Yahuah (God). When the Watchers descended and took wives from among the children of men, the resulting hybrid offspring — the Nephilim, the giants, the mighty ones — introduced a seed into the human story that was neither fully of heaven nor fully of the Adamic covenant line. Their bodies died. But Chapter 15 will establish that their spirits did not go to the place appointed for Adamic seed. They remained on earth. Disembodied. Hostile. The origin of what Scripture calls evil spirits and what the New Testament confronts as the demonic realm. But the seed war does not end there. It has been running since Genesis 3:15 — enmity between the seed of the woman and the seed of the serpent. That war did not conclude at the flood. The tares were sown into the field of the wheat, and they grew alongside it. This is what Yahusha (Jesus) described in Matthew 13 — not a metaphor about bad behavior but a precise statement about seed. The enemy came and sowed. The tares look like wheat in the field. They are not wheat. They cannot become wheat. No amount of teaching, preaching, or discipleship converts serpent seed into Adamic seed. The nature is in the origin, not the behavior. This is why Yahuah (God) said of Esau — before he had done good or evil, while still in the womb — “Jacob I loved, but Esau I have hated” (Romans 9:13, Malachi 1:2–3). The hatred precedes the deed because the seed precedes the choice. Esau’s works confirmed what was already true of his origin. He is not a prodigal. He is not a backslider who could have gone differently. He is what he is from seed. Nimrod is the same pattern after the flood — the first post-flood builder of counterfeit kingdom, the original type of the beast system, operating not as a deceived son of Adam who wandered but as serpent seed expressing its nature in dominion and idolatry. This is critical for how the Watcher narrative is read. The sons of Adam corrupted by the Watchers’ forbidden knowledge — the humanity that was led astray by enchantments, metallurgy for war, sorcery, and astrology — these are not tares. They are wheat carrying chaff. Deceived Adamic seed. Damaged but not converted into something other than what they are. The flood preserves Noah and his line — clean grain carried through the water — while removing what had corrupted the earth around them. The tares and the chaff are not the same thing. Chaff is the outer husk on genuine wheat — the inherited deception, the religious corruption, the Babylonian overlay that has accumulated on Adamic seed across generations. It comes off under threshing. The wilderness produces it. Refinement removes it. That is who Jeremiah 16:19 addresses — our fathers have inherited lies, the chaff of accumulated deception covering genuine seed that was always wheat underneath. Tares are not redeemable into wheat because they were never wheat. The father does not run toward a tare. There is no lost sheep dynamic with a son of Belial. They are left in the field until harvest because uprooting them prematurely damages the wheat growing beside them (Matthew 13:29). The separation belongs to Yahuah (God) of Spirits and His appointed reapers — not to us, not now, not by our judgment. Understanding this distinction is the difference between writing off the deceived as irredeemable and wasting the harvest season trying to convert what was never convertible. The remnant cannot afford either error. Cross-refs: Genesis 1:26–27 (general humanity created); Genesis 2:7 (Adam specifically formed — distinct appointment); Genesis 3:15 (enmity of seeds — the war declared); Matthew 13:24–30, 37–43 (tares sown by enemy, harvest separates — not our work to uproot); Romans 9:11–13 (Esau hated before birth — seed not behavior); Genesis 10:8–10 (Nimrod — mighty one, builder of Babel, post-flood serpent seed expression); 1 Samuel 2:12 (sons of Eli were sons of Belial — inside the covenant priestly line); John 8:44 (your father the devil — sons of Belial identified within the community); Jeremiah 16:19 (our fathers inherited lies — chaff language, Adamic seed under deception).

chapters.title: The Unions, Giants, Forbidden Knowledge, and Corruption

verses.text: And all the others together with them took unto themselves wives, and each chose for himself one, and they began to go in unto them and to defile themselves with them, and they taught them charms and enchantments, and the cutting of roots, and made them acquainted with plants.
And they became pregnant, and they bare great giants, whose height was three thousand ells:
Who consumed all the acquisitions of men. And when men could no longer sustain them, the giants turned against them and devoured mankind.
And they began to sin against birds, and beasts, and reptiles, and fish, and to devour one another’s flesh, and drink the blood.
Then the earth laid accusation against the lawless ones.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 7 unfolds the immediate fallout from the Watchers’ rebellion (Ch. 6): illicit unions lead to defilement, the transmission of secret knowledge, the birth of monstrous giants, and escalating violence that consumes creation. This narrative expands on Genesis 6:4–5 (“the Nephilim were on the earth… the wickedness of man was great”), portraying hybrid offspring as agents of chaos and the Watchers as corrupters who reveal heavenly secrets improperly. - Verse 1: The 200 Watchers take human wives, defiling themselves (crossing divine boundaries); they teach sorcery (“charms and enchantments”), herbology (“cutting of roots”), and pharmacology (“plants”)—forbidden arts that pervert Elohim’s natural order. - Cross-refs: Genesis 6:2, 4 (sons of Elohim (God) took daughters of men… Nephilim were on the earth); Exodus 22:18 (You shall not permit a sorceress to live); Deuteronomy 18:10–12 (no one who practices divination, sorcery, or interprets omens… abomination to Yahuah (God)); Galatians 5:19–20 (works of the flesh include sorcery… those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of Elohim (God)). - Verses 2–3: Women bear giants (“Nephilim”) of enormous size (hyperbolic “three thousand ells” ≈ impossible height, emphasizing monstrosity); giants consume human resources, then turn cannibalistic against mankind when supplies fail. - Cross-refs: Genesis 6:4 (Nephilim… mighty men of renown); Numbers 13:33 (we saw the Nephilim there… we were like grasshoppers); Deuteronomy 3:11 (Og king of Bashan… bedstead of iron… nine cubits long—giant remnant echo); Amos 2:9 (I destroyed the Amorite… whose height was like the height of the cedars). - Verse 4: Giants sin against all creation (birds, beasts, reptiles, fish), devouring flesh and drinking blood—total violation of Elohim’s boundaries for life and diet. - Cross-refs: Genesis 9:4 (flesh with its lifeblood you shall not eat); Leviticus 17:10–14 (no eating of blood… life is in the blood); Deuteronomy 12:23 (do not eat the blood… the blood is the life); Acts 15:20, 29 (abstain from blood… things strangled). - Verse 5: The earth itself “cries out” against the lawlessness—personifying creation’s groan under corruption. - Cross-refs: Genesis 4:10 (blood of Abel cries out from the ground); Job 31:38–40 (if my land cries out against me… let thistles grow instead of wheat); Romans 8:19–22 (creation waits… groans… subjected to futility… in bondage to corruption); Revelation 6:9–10 (souls under the altar cry out, “How long?”). Key Insight for Discernment: Chapter 7 reveals how angelic rebellion corrupted humanity at its root: forbidden knowledge fueled idolatry and violence; hybrid giants accelerated chaos; bloodshed defiled the land. Elohim’s response will be just judgment (foreshadowed in later chapters). This account deepens Genesis 6’s “wickedness of man” by showing supernatural origins of pre-flood evil, without excusing human responsibility. Scripture condemns such abominations (sorcery, blood consumption) and promises restoration when creation is freed from corruption. Observe how transgression multiplies—let this warn against pursuing hidden or forbidden things outside Yahuah’s revealed will (Deuteronomy 29:29; Colossians 2:18). Test all teachings and practices against Torah and the Renewed Covenant (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Forbidden Teachings of the Watchers

verses.text: And Azâzêl taught men to make swords, and knives, and shields, and breastplates, and made known to them the metals of the earth and the art of working them, and bracelets, and ornaments, and the use of antimony, and the beautifying of the eyelids, and all kinds of costly stones, and all colouring tinctures.

And there arose much godlessness, and they committed fornication, and they were led astray, and became corrupt in all their ways. Semjâzâ taught enchantments, and root-cuttings, Armârôs the resolving of enchantments, Barâqîjâl taught astrology, Kôkabêl the constellations, Ezêqêêl the knowledge of the clouds, Araqiêl the signs of the earth, Shamsiêl the signs of the sun, and Sariêl the course of the moon. And as men perished, they cried, and their cry went up to heaven.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 8 amplifies the corruption introduced in Chapter 7 by itemizing the heavenly secrets the Watchers illicitly revealed to humanity. Azâzêl (a chief Watcher) focuses on metallurgy and adornment (leading to weapons of war and vanity/cosmetics), while others teach sorcery, astrology, meteorology, and celestial signs—arts that pervert Elohim’s natural wisdom into tools of idolatry, violence, and deception. The result: rampant godlessness, sexual immorality, and total moral decay, with humanity’s outcry ascending to heaven (setting up Elohim’s response in coming chapters). - Verse 1: Azâzêl reveals metalworking (for weapons/armor) and beautification (jewelry, makeup, dyes, stones)—transforming Elohim’s gifts in the earth into instruments of war and vanity. - Cross-refs: Genesis 4:22 (Tubal-Cain forged all instruments of bronze and iron—pre-flood metallurgy echo); Isaiah 2:4 (swords into plowshares—reversal of corruption); 1 Timothy 2:9–10 (women adorn themselves modestly… not with braided hair or gold or pearls… but with good works); Exodus 32:2–4 (golden calf from earrings—adornment linked to idolatry); Deuteronomy 29:29 (secret things belong to Yahuah (God)… revealed things to us and our children). - Verse 2: The teachings spawn godlessness, fornication, delusion, and corruption in every way. Semjâzâ (overall leader) teaches basic sorcery/root-cutting; others specialize in enchantments, astrology (Barâqîjâl, Kôkabêl), weather signs (Ezêqêêl), earth omens (Araqiêl), solar signs (Shamsiêl), and lunar courses (Sariêl). Humanity’s cry reaches heaven amid perishing. - Cross-refs: Deuteronomy 18:9–14 (no divination, sorcery, interpreting omens, astrology… abomination to Yahuah (God)); Isaiah 47:12–13 (astrologers, star-gazers fail to save you); Jeremiah 10:2 (do not be dismayed at signs of the heavens… nations are dismayed); Acts 19:19 (many who practiced magic brought books and burned them… value fifty thousand pieces of silver); Galatians 5:19–21 (sorcery… those who practice such will not inherit the kingdom of Elohim (God)); Revelation 9:21 (they did not repent of their sorceries); Genesis 6:5 (wickedness great… every intent evil continually); Romans 1:21–25 (exchanged truth for lie… worshiped creation over Creator). Key Insight for Discernment: These “secrets” were heavenly knowledge meant for angelic stewardship, not human exploitation. Their revelation fueled violence (weapons), vanity/idolatry (adornments), and occult practices (astrology/sorcery)—direct violations of Elohim’s boundaries (Deuteronomy 18). Humanity’s corruption is not just internal but supernaturally accelerated, yet responsibility remains ours (as in Genesis 6). The cry to heaven shows Elohim (God) hears injustice (even from the corrupt). This warns against seeking “hidden knowledge” outside Yahuah’s revealed Torah and Renewed Covenant—true wisdom comes from fearing Yahuah (Proverbs 1:7; James 3:17). Test all sources of knowledge: does it lead to righteousness or corruption? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Archangels’ Intercession

verses.text: And then Michael, Uriel, Raphael, and Gabriel looked down from heaven and saw much blood being shed upon the earth, and all lawlessness being wrought upon the earth.
And they said one to another: ’The earth lost through those who dwell upon her! The voice of their crying has reached unto the gates of heaven.
And now to you, O holy ones of heaven, the souls of men make their suit, saying, “Bring our cause before the Most High.”

And they said to Yahuah (God) of the ages: "Yahuah (God) of lords, Elohim (God) of elohiym, King of kings, and Elohim (God) of the ages, the throne of Thy glory (standeth) unto all the generations of the world, and Thy Name is holy and glorious and blessed unto all the ages!
Thou hast made all things, and power over all things hast Thou: and all things are naked and open in Thy sight, and Thou seest all things, and nothing can hide itself from Thee.
Thou seest what Azâzêl hath done, who hath taught all unrighteousness on earth and revealed the eternal secrets which were (preserved) in heaven, which men were striving to learn:
And what Shemyaza hath done, to whom Thou hast given authority to bear rule over his associates.
And they have gone to the daughters of men upon the earth, and have slept with the women, and have defiled themselves, and revealed to them all kinds of sins.
And the women have borne giants, and the whole earth has thereby been filled with blood and unrighteousness.

And now, behold, the souls of those who have died are crying and making their suit to the gates of heaven, and their lamentations have ascended: and cannot cease because of the lawless deeds which are wrought on the earth.
And Thou knowest all things before they come to pass, and Thou seest these things and Thou dost suffer them, and Thou dost not say to us what we are to do to them in regard to these."

chapters.commentary: Chapter 9 shifts perspective from earth’s chaos (caused by the Watchers’ rebellion in Ch. 6–8) to the heavenly realm: the four archangels witness the bloodshed, lawlessness, and cries of the oppressed (including souls of the slain). They intercede with a doxology and petition to Yahuah (God), blaming Azâzêl primarily for teaching forbidden secrets and Shemyaza for leading the unions that produced giants and filled the earth with violence. This highlights Elohim’s omniscience—He sees all yet allows events to unfold—while affirming the archangels’ role as mediators and executors of divine justice. - Verses 1–3: The archangels see widespread bloodshed and lawlessness; the earth “cries out” through the voices/souls of victims, reaching heaven’s gates—echoing creation’s groan. - Cross-refs: Genesis 4:10 (blood of Abel cries from the ground); Genesis 18:20–21 (outcry against Sodom and Gomorrah great… Yahuah (God) will go down and see); Romans 8:22 (creation groans… in travail); Revelation 6:9–10 (souls under the altar cry, “How long, O Master?”). - Verses 4–5: Praise to Yahuah (God) as Lord of lords, Elohim (God) of elohiym, eternal King—Creator who sees all nakedly, nothing hidden. - Cross-refs: Deuteronomy 10:17 (Yahuah (God) your Elohim (God) is Elohim (God) of elohiym and Lord of lords); Psalm 90:2 (from everlasting to everlasting You are Elohim (God)); Hebrews 4:13 (no creature hidden from His sight… all things naked and open); Psalm 139:1–4 (Yahuah (God) searches and knows… before a word on my tongue). - Verses 6–10: Specific accusation against Azâzêl (teaching unrighteousness/secrets) and Shemyaza (authority over associates, unions with women → giants, blood/unrighteousness filling earth); souls of the dead cry without ceasing. - Cross-refs: Genesis 6:11–13 (earth filled with violence… Elohim (God) saw… all flesh corrupted); Leviticus 17:11 (life of the flesh in the blood); 2 Peter 2:4 (angels who sinned… cast down to hell); Jude 1:6 (angels who did not keep their domain… reserved in chains); Revelation 18:24 (blood of prophets and saints… found in her). - Verse 11: Elohim (God) knows all beforehand yet permits it; archangels ask for guidance on response. - Cross-refs: Psalm 94:9–11 (He who planted the ear… sees… knows thoughts of man); Isaiah 46:10 (declaring the end from the beginning); Habakkuk 1:2–4 (how long… violence… no justice?); Romans 11:33–36 (depth of riches… who has known mind of Yahuah (God)?). Key Insight for Discernment: The archangels’ cry shows heaven is not indifferent—Elohim (God) hears injustice and will act justly (as in coming chapters). Azâzêl’s revelation of “eternal secrets” underscores the danger of forbidden knowledge leading to corruption. This chapter bridges human/angelic sin to divine intervention, affirming Yahuah’s sovereignty and omniscience. Let the outcry of the oppressed remind us: Elohim (God) sees, hears, and judges (Psalm 9:7–8; James 5:4). Test events and teachings: do they increase righteousness or lawlessness? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: Yahuah’s Judgments and the Cleansing of the Earth

verses.text: Then said the Most High, the Holy and Great One spake, and sent Uriel to the son of Lamech,

And said to him: ’Go to Noah and tell him in My Name “Hide thyself!” and reveal to him the end that is approaching: that the whole earth will be destroyed, and a deluge is about to come upon the whole earth, and will destroy all that is on it.
And now instruct him that he may escape and his seed may be preserved for all the generations of the world.’
And again Yahuah (God) said to Raphael: ’Bind Azâzêl hand and foot, and cast him into the darkness: and make an opening in the desert, which is in Dûdâêl, and cast him therein.
And place upon him rough and jagged rocks, and cover him with darkness, and let him abide there for ever, and cover his face that he may not see light.
And on the day of the great judgement he shall be cast into the fire.

And heal the earth which the angels have corrupted, and proclaim the healing of the earth, that they may heal the plague, and that all the children of men may not perish through all the secret things that the Watchers have disclosed and have taught their sons.
And the whole earth has been corrupted through the works that were taught by Azâzêl: to him ascribe all sin.’

And to Gabriel said Yahuah (God): ’Proceed against the bastards and the reprobates, and against the children of fornication: and destroy [the children of fornication and] the children of the Watchers from amongst men [and cause them to go forth]: send them one against the other that they may destroy each other in battle: for length of days shall they not have.

And no request that they (i.e. their fathers) make of thee shall be granted unto their fathers on their behalf; for they hope to live an eternal life, and that each one of them will live five hundred years.’
And Yahuah (God) said unto Michael: ’Go, bind Semjâzâ and his associates who have united themselves with women so as to have defiled themselves with them in all their uncleanness.

And when their sons have slain one another, and they have seen the destruction of their beloved ones, bind them fast for seventy generations in the valleys of the earth, till the day of their judgement and of their consummation, till the judgement that is for ever and ever is consummated.
In those days they shall be led off to the abyss of fire: and to the torment and the prison in which they shall be confined for ever.
And whosoever shall be condemned and destroyed will from thenceforth be bound together with them to the end of all generations.
And destroy all the spirits of the reprobate and the children of the Watchers, because they have wronged mankind.

Destroy all wrong from the face of the earth and let every evil work come to an end: and let the plant of righteousness and truth appear: and it shall prove a blessing; the works of righteousness and truth’ shall be planted in truth and joy for evermore.
And then shall all the righteous escape, and shall live until they beget thousands of children, And all the days of their youth and their old age Shall they complete in peace.
And then shall the whole earth be tilled in righteousness, and shall all be planted with trees and be full of blessing.

And all desirable trees shall be planted on it, and they shall plant vines on it: and the vine which they plant upon it shall yield wine in abundance, and as for all the seed which is sown upon each measure (of it) shall bear a thousand, and each measure of olives shall yield ten presses of oil.
And cleanse thou the earth from all oppression, and from all unrighteousness, and from all sin: and all the uncleanness that is wrought upon the earth destroy from off the earth.
And all the children of men shall become righteous, and all nations shall offer adoration and shall praise Me, and all shall worship Me.

And the earth shall be cleansed from all defilement, and from all sin, and from all punishment: and all the children of men shall become righteous, and all nations shall offer adoration and shall praise Me, and all shall worship Me. And the earth shall be cleansed from all defilement, and from all sin, and from all punishment: and all the children of men shall become righteous, and all nations shall offer adoration and shall praise Me, and all shall worship Me. [And the earth shall be cleansed from all defilement, and from all sin, and from all punishment:]

chapters.commentary: Chapter 10 delivers Yahuah’s authoritative decrees in response to the archangels’ petition—specific punishments for the Watchers and their offspring, instructions for the flood, and a vision of ultimate restoration. It expands Genesis 6–9 (Noah’s flood, cleansing judgment) with heavenly details: binding of Azâzêl and Semjâzâ, destruction of giants, evil spirits from giants’ bodies, and post-judgment renewal where the righteous inherit a fruitful, peaceful earth. - Verses 1–3: Uriel sent to Noah (son of Lamech) to warn of the deluge and preserve his seed. - Cross-refs: Genesis 6:13–14, 17–18 (Elohim (God) said to Noah… I will destroy them with the earth… make an ark); Genesis 7:1 (Yahuah (God) said to Noah… come into the ark); 2 Peter 2:5 (Noah, a preacher of righteousness… preserved); Hebrews 11:7 (by faith Noah… prepared an ark… became heir of righteousness). - Verses 4–8: Raphael binds Azâzêl in darkness (Dûdâêl desert) until final fire judgment; he bears chief blame for corrupting earth with forbidden teachings—command to heal earth and proclaim cleansing. - Cross-refs: Leviticus 16:8–10 (scapegoat for Azâzêl in wilderness—atonement ritual echo); Isaiah 24:21–22 (Yahuah (God) will punish the host of the high ones… shut up in prison); Revelation 20:1–3 (angel binds Satan… casts into bottomless pit… shut up… thousand years); Romans 8:20–21 (creation subjected to futility… will be delivered). - Verses 9–10: Gabriel destroys giants (bastards/reprobates) by mutual slaughter; no mercy for their long-life hopes. - Cross-refs: Genesis 6:4 (Nephilim… mighty men); Numbers 13:33 (Nephilim remnants); Genesis 6:3 (man’s days 120 years—limiting lifespan). - Verses 11–15: Michael binds Semjâzâ and associates for 70 generations in valleys until final judgment/consummation in fire abyss; destroy evil spirits and wrong from earth. - Cross-refs: 2 Peter 2:4 (cast angels into hell… chains of darkness); Jude 1:6 (reserved in everlasting chains under darkness); Revelation 20:10 (devil cast into lake of fire… tormented day and night forever). - Verses 16–22: Vision of restoration—righteous plant of truth flourishes; earth tilled in righteousness, abundant blessing (trees, vines, yields); cleansed from sin; all nations worship Yahuah (God); complete righteousness. - Cross-refs: Isaiah 11:6–9 (wolf with lamb… earth full of knowledge of Yahuah (God)); Isaiah 65:17–25 (new heavens and new earth… no more weeping… build houses, plant vineyards… wolf and lamb feed together); Revelation 21:1–4 (new heaven and new earth… no more death, sorrow… former things passed away); Hosea 2:18 (covenant with beasts… bow, sword… break… make them lie down safely); Psalm 72:3–7 (mountains bring peace… righteous flourish… abundance of peace); Zechariah 14:9 (Yahuah (God) shall be King over all the earth). Key Insight for Discernment: Yahuah’s response shows perfect justice: immediate restraint of evil (binding Watchers/giants), catastrophic cleansing (flood), and long-term hope (renewal for the righteous). Azâzêl’s scapegoat-like punishment echoes Leviticus atonement, pointing to ultimate removal of sin. The chapter affirms Elohim (God) hears cries, judges rebellion, yet promises blessing to the faithful remnant. Let this encourage endurance: judgment on corruption is certain, but restoration follows for those who align with Yahuah (Romans 8:18–23; 2 Peter 3:13). Test all things by His unchanging word (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Cleansing and the Record of the Visions

And when their sons have slain one another, and they have seen the destruction of their beloved ones, bind them fast for seventy generations in the valleys of the earth, till the day of their judgement and of their consummation, till the judgement that is for ever and ever is consummated.
In those days they shall be led off to the abyss of fire: and to the torment and the prison in which they shall be confined for ever.
And whosoever shall be condemned and destroyed will from thenceforth be bound together with them to the end of all generations.
And destroy all the spirits of the reprobate and the children of the Watchers, because they have wronged mankind.

Destroy all wrong from the face of the earth and let every evil work come to an end: and let the plant of righteousness and truth appear: and it shall prove a blessing; the works of righteousness and truth shall be planted in truth and joy for evermore.
And then shall all the righteous escape, and shall live until they beget thousands of children, and all the days of their youth and their old age shall they complete in peace.
And then shall the whole earth be tilled in righteousness, and shall all be planted with trees and be full of blessing.

And all desirable trees shall be planted on it, and they shall plant vines on it: and the vine which they plant thereon shall yield wine in abundance, and as for all the seed which is sown thereon each measure (of it) shall bear a thousand, and each measure of olives shall yield ten presses of oil.
And cleanse thou the earth from all oppression, and from all unrighteousness, and from all sin: and all the uncleanness that is wrought upon the earth destroy from off the earth.
And all the children of men shall become righteous, and all nations shall offer adoration and shall praise Me, and all shall worship Me.

And the earth shall be cleansed from all defilement, and from all sin, and from all punishment: and all the children of men shall become righteous, and all nations shall offer adoration and shall praise Me, and all shall worship Me.

And the earth shall be cleansed from all defilement, and from all sin, and from all punishment: and all the children of men shall become righteous, and all nations shall offer adoration and shall praise Me, and all shall worship Me.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 11 largely repeats and reinforces the restoration vision from the end of Chapter 10, emphasizing the total eradication of evil (spirits of the reprobate, wrong works, uncleanness) and the flourishing of righteousness on a renewed earth. It underscores Yahuah’s ultimate purpose: a cleansed creation where the righteous live long, peaceful lives, the land yields abundantly, and all nations worship Him in truth. This chapter acts as a summary of the judgment-and-renewal theme before shifting to Enoch’s personal involvement in the revelations. - Verses 1–5: Reiteration of Michael’s binding of Semjâzâ and associates (70 generations in valleys → abyss of fire), destruction of evil spirits and wrongdoers. - Cross-refs: 2 Peter 2:4 (Elohim (God) spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell); Jude 1:6 (angels… reserved in everlasting chains under darkness); Revelation 20:1–3, 10 (binding Satan… lake of fire… tormented day and night forever). - Verses 6–13: Vision of post-judgment renewal—plant of righteousness blossoms; righteous beget thousands in peace; earth tilled fruitfully (abundant yields of vines, olives); complete cleansing from oppression, sin, defilement; universal righteousness and worship of Yahuah (God). - Cross-refs: Isaiah 65:17–25 (new heavens and new earth… no more weeping… build houses, plant vineyards… wolf and lamb feed together); Isaiah 11:6–9 (earth full of knowledge of Yahuah (God) as waters cover the sea); Revelation 21:1–5 (new heaven and new earth… former things passed away… no more death, sorrow); Hosea 2:18–23 (covenant with beasts… earth shall answer… I will say to them, “You are My people”); Psalm 72:16 (abundance of grain in the earth… fruit thereof shake like Lebanon); Zechariah 14:9, 16 (Yahuah (God) shall be King over all the earth… all nations shall come up to worship); Romans 8:19–23 (creation waits… delivered from bondage of corruption into glorious liberty). Key Insight for Discernment: The repetition here drives home Elohim’s unwavering commitment to justice followed by restoration. Judgment on rebellion (Watchers, giants, sin) is thorough, but the goal is not mere destruction—it’s the flourishing of righteousness, abundance, and universal worship. This eschatological hope aligns with prophetic promises of a renewed creation under Yahuah’s rule. It encourages the righteous to endure: the current corruption will end, and peace will prevail for those who remain faithful. Let this vision inspire alignment with Yahuah’s ways now (2 Peter 3:13; Revelation 21:3–4). Test all things by His word (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: Enoch Commissioned to Deliver Judgment to the Watchers

verses.text: Before these things Enoch was hidden, and no one of the children of men knew where he was hidden, and where he abode, and what had become of him.
And his activities had to do with the Watchers, and his days were with the holy ones.
And I Enoch was blessing Yahuah (God) of majesty and the King of the ages, and lo! the Watchers called me—Enoch the scribe—and said to me:

’Enoch, thou scribe of righteousness, go, declare to the Watchers of the heaven who have left the high heaven, the holy eternal place, and have defiled themselves with women, and have done as the children of earth do, and have taken unto themselves wives: "Ye have wrought great destruction on the earth:
And ye shall have no peace nor forgiveness of sin: and inasmuch as they delight themselves in their children,
The murder of their beloved ones shall they see, and over the destruction of their children shall they lament, and shall make supplication unto eternity, but mercy and peace shall ye not attain."’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 12 transitions from the divine decrees (Ch. 10–11) to Enoch’s prophetic role. He is described as “hidden” (alluding to his translation in Genesis 5:24), dwelling among heavenly beings. The fallen Watchers, aware of impending judgment, summon Enoch—the “scribe of righteousness”—to petition Yahuah (God) for mercy on their behalf. Instead, Enoch is commissioned to deliver an unyielding message of condemnation: no peace, no forgiveness, only grief over their offspring’s destruction. - Verses 1–2: Enoch’s hidden state and association with the holy ones (angels/Watchers in pre-fall context) emphasize his unique position as a bridge between earth and heaven. - Cross-refs: Genesis 5:24 (“Enoch walked with Elohim (God): and he was not; for Elohim (God) took him”); Hebrews 11:5 (by faith Enoch was translated… he pleased Elohim (God)); Sirach 44:16 (Enoch pleased Yahuah (God) and was taken up… a pattern of repentance to all generations—apocryphal echo). - Verses 3–6: The Watchers appeal through Enoch, but Yahuah’s word through him is final: their defilement (unions with women) caused great destruction; they will witness their children’s slaughter, lament eternally, yet receive no mercy or peace. - Cross-refs: Genesis 6:11–13 (earth filled with violence… Elohim (God) said, “I will destroy them”); 2 Peter 2:4–5 (angels who sinned… reserved unto judgment… Noah preserved); Jude 1:6 (angels… kept not their first estate… reserved in everlasting chains); Isaiah 59:2 (your iniquities have separated you from your Elohim (God)… no peace for the wicked); Jeremiah 11:11 (Yahuah (God) says: “I will bring evil upon them… they shall cry unto Me, but I will not hearken”). Key Insight for Discernment: Enoch functions as a faithful messenger, not an intercessor for the rebellious—he delivers Yahuah’s unalterable judgment without softening it. This underscores the gravity of crossing divine boundaries: angelic sin brings irreversible consequences, even for those who once held heavenly status. Mercy is extended to the repentant righteous (as in Ch. 10–11’s promises), but persistent rebellion meets justice. Let this warn against presuming on grace or seeking loopholes in Yahuah’s commands (Hebrews 10:26–31; Romans 6:1–2). Test all appeals and teachings: do they align with Yahuah’s revealed will, or seek to evade accountability? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: Enoch Delivers Judgment; The Watchers’ Petition

verses.text: And Enoch went and said: ’Azâzêl, thou shalt have no peace: a severe sentence has gone forth against thee to put thee in bonds:

And thou shalt not have toleration nor request granted to thee, because of the unrighteousness which thou hast taught, and because of all the works of godlessness and unrighteousness and sin which thou hast shown to men.’
Then I went and spoke to them all together, and they were all afraid, and fear and trembling befell them.
And they besought me to write out for them the record of a petition, that they might have forgiveness, and to take their petition into the presence of Yahuah (God) of heaven.
For from thenceforward they could not speak (with Him) nor lift up their eyes to heaven for shame of their sins for which they had been condemned.
Then I wrote out their petition, and the prayer in regard to their spirits and their deeds individually and in regard to their requests that they should have forgiveness and forbearance.
And I went off and sat down at the waters of Dan, in the land of Dan, to the south of the west of Hermon: I read their petition till I fell asleep.
And behold a dream came to me, and visions fell upon me, and I saw visions of chastisement, and a voice came to me saying: ‘Speak to the sons of heaven, and reprimand them.’

And when I awaked, I came unto them, and they stood together, and they were weeping and their eyes were full of tears; and they besought me to write out for them a petition, that forgiveness might be granted to them.
And I took their petition and read it before Yahuah (God) of heaven.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 13 intensifies the personal confrontation: Enoch confronts the Watchers face-to-face with Yahuah’s irrevocable judgment (no peace, no mercy for Azâzêl and the group). Overwhelmed by shame and fear, they beg Enoch to record and present their petition for forgiveness. He does so, reading it before Yahuah (God)—yet the dream-vision confirms only reprimand and chastisement await. This underscores the finality of divine justice: repentance after willful, high-level rebellion comes too late. - Verses 1–2: Enoch directly proclaims Azâzêl’s sentence—no tolerance, no granted requests—due to teaching unrighteousness and godlessness. - Cross-refs: Isaiah 59:2 (your iniquities have separated between you and your Elohim (God)… He will not hear); Jeremiah 7:16 (do not pray for this people… I will not hear them); 1 John 5:16 (sin leading to death… I do not say he should pray for that). - Verses 3–6: The Watchers tremble in fear; they ask Enoch (scribe of righteousness) to draft their petition for forgiveness and present it to Yahuah (God), as shame prevents them from approaching heaven directly. - Cross-refs: Genesis 3:8–10 (Adam and Eve hid from Yahuah (God)… afraid because naked); Hebrews 12:17 (Esau sought blessing with tears but found no place for repentance); Revelation 6:16–17 (hide us from the face of Him… great day of His wrath has come). - Verses 7–10: Enoch reads the petition at Dan (near Hermon, site of descent); falls asleep, receives a dream-vision of chastisement and a command to reprimand the sons of heaven; awakes to find them still weeping and begging; he presents the petition before Yahuah (God). - Cross-refs: Genesis 28:10–19 (Jacob’s dream at Bethel near Dan—ladder to heaven, angels ascending/descending); Daniel 7:9–10 (Ancient of Days… books opened); Revelation 20:12 (books opened… judged according to works); Psalm 50:21 (these things you did, and I kept silent; you thought I was like you… I will reprove you). Key Insight for Discernment: Enoch faithfully records and delivers the Watchers’ plea, yet the vision confirms judgment stands—no intercession alters it. This illustrates the seriousness of rebellion against Yahuah (God): once boundaries are crossed with full knowledge (as heavenly beings), consequences are binding. Mercy is real for the repentant on earth (as seen in Noah’s preservation), but presumption after deliberate sin meets justice. Let this caution against delaying repentance or assuming late pleas will be heard (Hebrews 3:7–15; 2 Corinthians 6:2—“now is the day of salvation”). Test all spirits and petitions by Yahuah’s unchanging word (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: Enoch’s Ascent and Vision of the Throne

verses.text: The book of the words of righteousness, and of the reproof of the Watchers, who belong to the world, according to that which He, who is blessed and righteous, commanded in the vision.
Enoch also saw the vision, the ends of all things, and all things did he see, even to the ends of the earth, and no one spoke a word to him.
And I Enoch was carried off in a whirlwind, with a chariot of fire, and the wind lifted me up and bore me into the ends of heaven.
And I went into the heavens, and the holy ones came forth to meet me, and they showed me the place of the righteous and the place of the holy.
And I saw the dwellings of the holy ones, and the resting-places of the righteous.
And my spirit longed for that dwelling-place, and my soul desired it exceedingly.
Then I entered into the houses of the holy ones, and they showed me the place of the righteous.
And I saw the foundations of the house of heaven, and the pillars of fire, and the pillars of light, and the pillars of ice, and the pillars of snow, and the pillars of hail.
And I saw the winds which turn the heaven, and cause the disc of the sun and all the stars to set.
And I saw the winds which support the clouds.
And I saw the paths of the angels.
And I saw at the end of the earth the firmament of the heaven above.
And I went towards the south, and it was burning day and night, where there were seven mountains of precious stones, three towards the east, and three towards the south.
And as for those towards the east, one was of coloured stone, and one of pearl, and one jacinth, and those towards the south of red stone.
But the middle one reached to heaven, like the throne of Yahuah (God), of stibium, and the top of the throne was of sapphire.
And I saw a flaming fire, and beyond that fire I saw a mountain whose summit reached to heaven.
And I saw there a deep abyss, with columns of heavenly fire, and among them I saw columns of fire fall, which were beyond measure alike towards the height and towards the depth.

And beyond that abyss I saw a place which had no firmament of the heaven above, and no firmly founded earth beneath it: there was no water upon it, and no birds, but it was a waste and horrible place.

I saw there seven stars like great burning mountains, and to me, when I inquired regarding them, the angel said: ’This place is the end of heaven and earth: this has become a prison for the stars and the host of heaven.
And the stars which roll over the fire are they which have transgressed the commandment of Yahuah (God) in the beginning of their rising, because they did not come forth at their appointed times.
And He was wroth with them, and bound them till the time when their guilt should be consummated (even) for ten thousand years.’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 14 launches Enoch’s heavenly journey and throne vision, a high point of apocalyptic literature. It describes his ascent in a whirlwind/chariot of fire, entry into celestial realms, and approach to Yahuah’s throne amid dazzling phenomena (pillars of fire/light/ice, winds, mountains of precious stones). The vision culminates in the prison of rebellious stars (symbolizing fallen angels/Watchers) bound for 10,000 years—reinforcing the irreversible judgment on those who transgressed divine order. - Verses 1–7: Enoch’s visions of righteousness/reproof; ascent in whirlwind/fire chariot; encounter with holy ones showing dwellings of the righteous. - Cross-refs: 2 Kings 2:11 (Elijah taken up by whirlwind in chariot of fire); Genesis 5:24 (Enoch taken by Elohim (God)); Hebrews 11:5 (Enoch translated… did not see death); Psalm 68:17 (chariots of Elohim (God)… thousands of angels). - Verses 8–17: Description of heavenly architecture (foundations, pillars, winds, paths of angels); journey south to burning region with seven jewel mountains; central throne-like mountain of stibium/sapphire; abyss of fire and waste place. - Cross-refs: Exodus 24:10, 17 (under Elohim’s feet… sapphire pavement… devouring fire); Ezekiel 1:26–28 (throne appearance like sapphire… rainbow… glory of Yahuah (God)); Revelation 4:2–6 (throne in heaven… appearance like jasper and carnelian… sea of glass like crystal); Isaiah 6:1–4 (Yahuah (God) high and lifted up… seraphim… house filled with smoke). - Verses 18–21: Prison for transgressing stars/host of heaven—bound 10,000 years for failing appointed times. - Cross-refs: Job 38:7 (morning stars sang… sons of Elohim (God) shouted); Isaiah 24:21 (Yahuah (God) punishes host of high ones… shut up in prison); 2 Peter 2:4 (angels who sinned… cast down to hell… chains of darkness); Jude 1:6 (angels… reserved in everlasting chains under darkness); Revelation 20:1–3 (Satan bound… thousand years—echo of long-term restraint). Key Insight for Discernment: The throne vision reveals Yahuah’s unmatched majesty and justice—creation’s order (stars keeping times) is sacred; violation brings binding judgment. Enoch’s ascent shows privileged revelation to the righteous scribe, contrasting the Watchers’ fall. This affirms Elohim’s sovereignty over heavenly and earthly realms—nothing escapes His order or wrath. Let the splendor draw awe and the prison warn against rebellion (Psalm 19:1; Romans 1:20). Test visions/teachings: do they glorify Yahuah (God) and uphold His commandments? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: Yahuah’s Rebuke and the Origin of Evil Spirits

verses.text: And He answered and said to me, and I heard His voice: ’Fear not, Enoch, thou righteous man and scribe of righteousness: approach hither and hear my voice.
And go, say to the Watchers of heaven, who have sent thee to intercede for them: "You should intercede for men, and not men for you:

Wherefore have ye left the high, holy, and eternal heaven, and lain with women, and defiled yourselves with the daughters of men and taken to yourselves wives, and done like the children of earth, and begotten giants (as your) sons?

And though ye were holy, spiritual, living the eternal life, you have defiled yourselves with the blood of women, and have begotten (children) with the blood of flesh, and, as the children of men, have lusted after flesh and blood as those also do who die and perish.
Therefore have I given them wives also that they might impregnate them, and beget children by them, that thus the earth might be filled with their children.
And now, the giants, who are produced from the spirits and flesh, shall be called evil spirits upon the earth, and on the earth shall be their dwelling.

Evil spirits have proceeded from their bodies; because they are born from men and from the holy Watchers is their beginning and primal origin; evil spirits they will be upon earth and evil spirits will they be called.
As for the spirits of heaven, in heaven shall be their dwelling, but as for the spirits of the earth which were born upon the earth, on the earth shall be their dwelling.

And the spirits of the giants afflict, oppress, destroy, attack, do battle, and work destruction on the earth, and cause trouble: they take no food, but nevertheless hunger and thirst, and cause offences.
And these spirits shall rise up against the children of men and against the women, because they have proceeded from them.

From the days of the slaughter and destruction and death of the giants, from the souls of whose flesh the spirits, having gone forth, shall destroy without incurring judgement—thus shall they destroy until the day of the consummation, the great judgement in which the age shall be consummated, over the Watchers and the godless, yea, shall be wholly consummated."’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 15 records Yahuah’s authoritative rebuke delivered through Enoch—no forgiveness is offered to the Watchers. It explains the theological reason for their condemnation (abandoning spiritual nature for fleshly lust), the hybrid origin of the giants, and the post-death fate of their spirits: becoming disembodied evil spirits that afflict humanity. This chapter provides one of the clearest ancient explanations for the existence and activity of demons/evil spirits in pre-flood and ongoing contexts. The Origin of Demons and the Persistence of the Tares - Verses 1–2: Yahuah (God) comforts Enoch and commands him to rebuke the Watchers—the proper order is angels interceding for humans, not vice versa. - Cross-refs: Hebrews 1:14 (ministering spirits sent to minister for those who will inherit salvation); Hebrews 2:16 (He does not give aid to angels, but to the seed of Abraham). - Verses 3–5: Rebuke for leaving their heavenly station to defile themselves with women, begetting giants—contrasting their eternal spiritual nature with fleshly corruption. - Cross-refs: Jude 1:6 (angels who did not keep their proper domain… left their own abode); 2 Peter 2:4 (angels who sinned… cast down to hell); Genesis 6:2–4 (sons of Elohim (God) took daughters of men… Nephilim on earth). - Verses 6–10: Giants’ spirits become evil spirits on earth after death—afflicting, oppressing, and causing trouble; they hunger/thirst yet consume nothing, rising against men and women (their origin). - Cross-refs: Mark 5:1–13 (Legion—demons begging not to be sent out of the country); Luke 8:30–33 (unclean spirits enter swine); Ephesians 6:12 (wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities… spiritual hosts of wickedness); James 2:19 (demons believe and tremble); Revelation 16:13–14 (unclean spirits like frogs… spirits of demons working signs). - Verse 11: Evil spirits continue their destructive work until the final consummation—the great judgment on Watchers and godless. - Cross-refs: Matthew 8:29 (demons cry, “Have You come here to torment us before the time?”); Revelation 20:10–15 (devil… cast into lake of fire… great white throne judgment); 2 Peter 3:7 (heavens and earth… reserved for fire… day of judgment and perdition of ungodly men). Key Insight for Discernment: Yahuah (God) clarifies that evil spirits are not pre-existent or independent creations but the disembodied result of angelic-human transgression—explaining their malice toward humanity (their source). This underscores the consequences of crossing Elohim’s boundaries: eternal spiritual beings become agents of ongoing affliction until final judgment. Mercy is for repentant humans (Noah’s line), not rebellious angels. Let this affirm spiritual warfare is real (Ephesians 6:12) yet bound by Yahuah’s timeline—victory belongs to the righteous through Him (Romans 16:20; 1 John 4:4). Test spirits: do they oppose Yahuah’s order or lead to righteousness? (1 John 4:1–3; Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21). Evil Spirits, Disembodied Seed, and What This Means for Spiritual Warfare Yahuah’s explanation to Enoch here is precise: evil spirits are not an eternal parallel opposition to Elohim (God). They are a consequence. The disembodied spirits of the giants — born of Watcher fathers and human mothers, belonging fully to neither realm — have no appointed place in the order Yahuah (God) established. Heaven is not their home. The Adamic Sheol is not fitted for them. They remain on earth between the worlds, afflicting the children of men from whom their physical nature was drawn, until the day of final consummation. The Watchers themselves receive no mercy here.
