Enoch is explicitly told not to intercede for them. The proper order — angels interceding for men, not men for angels — is stated and the reversal is condemned. There is no redemptive arc for the Watchers. No repentance offered. No path back. Their judgment is set and their binding is certain. This is not cruelty. It is the nature of what they chose: beings of eternal spiritual nature who traded that nature for the flesh, and in doing so placed themselves beyond the provisions made for Adamic seed. For the scattered seed reading this: you are not fighting an eternal enemy on equal footing with Yahuah (God). You are dealing with the wreckage of a rebellion that has already been sentenced, already been bound in its leadership, and is already running out of time. The Watchers are in chains. The giants are dead. Their spirits rage because they have no home and no hope — and they know it. “Have You come to torment us before the time?” (Matthew 8:29). They know there is a time. They are counting down to it, not toward anything. This does not make spiritual warfare casual. Ephesians 6:12 is true and the affliction is real. But it is warfare from inside a victory already secured, not a battle whose outcome is uncertain. Walk accordingly — with authority, not with fear. Cross-refs: Matthew 8:29 (demons know the timeline — before the time); Luke 10:19 (authority over all the power of the enemy); Colossians 2:15 (principalities disarmed — past tense, already accomplished); Ephesians 6:12 (wrestle against spiritual hosts — the warfare is real); 1 John 4:4 (greater is He in you than he in the world); Revelation 20:10 (final sentencing — the timeline closes).

chapters.title: Final Rejection of the Watchers’ Petition

verses.text: And from the beginning thus have I been shown concerning you, and written concerning you:
With the spiritual ones have ye had union, with the women have ye defiled yourselves, and with the blood of women have ye lusted, and with the flesh and blood of men have ye drunk wine.
And these things have ye shown to women, and through these mysteries women and men work much destruction on earth.
Say to them therefore: “You have no peace.”’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 16 serves as the emphatic conclusion to Yahuah’s response to the Watchers (continuing from Ch. 15). It reiterates the core sins—union with women, defilement through blood/lust, and revealing heavenly mysteries that lead to widespread destruction—and pronounces the final, irrevocable sentence: no peace. No further intercession, no forgiveness, no reversal. This seals the judgment announced earlier (binding, imprisonment, eventual fire) and transitions the narrative away from the Watchers’ plea toward Enoch’s ongoing visions. - Verses 1–3: Yahuah (God) recalls the revelation shown to Enoch from the beginning: the Watchers’ spiritual corruption through fleshly unions, drinking blood/wine (symbolizing violence and excess), and teaching forbidden mysteries that multiplied evil on earth. - Cross-refs: Genesis 6:5, 11–12 (wickedness great… earth filled with violence… all flesh corrupted); Leviticus 17:10–14 (blood prohibition… life in the blood); Deuteronomy 32:32–33 (vine of Sodom… wine of fury); Galatians 5:19–21 (works of flesh: fornication, uncleanness… those who practice such will not inherit the kingdom of Elohim (God)); Revelation 18:23 (sorceries deceived all nations—echo of revealed mysteries). - Verse 4: The ultimate decree, repeated for emphasis: “You have no peace.” - Cross-refs: Isaiah 57:21 (“There is no peace,” says my Elohim (God), “for the wicked”); Isaiah 48:22 (“There is no peace,” says Yahuah (God), “for the wicked”); Ezekiel 13:10–16 (false prophets say “Peace” when there is no peace); Romans 3:17 (the way of peace they have not known); Jude 1:13 (wandering stars… blackness of darkness forever—Watchers’ fate). Key Insight for Discernment: The repeated “no peace” is not cruelty but justice—Yahuah’s boundaries are holy, and deliberate, high-level rebellion (especially by spiritual beings) forfeits mercy. The mysteries they revealed caused irreversible harm, showing how forbidden knowledge multiplies sin. This chapter warns that some choices carry permanent consequences, yet it contrasts sharply with the hope offered to the righteous (Ch. 10–11’s renewal). Let it remind us: true peace comes only through alignment with Yahuah (God), not through rebellion or late pleas (Isaiah 26:3; Romans 5:1; Philippians 4:7). Test all things: does a path lead to peace with Elohim (God) or perpetuate destruction? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: Enoch’s Journey to the Ends of the Earth

verses.text: And they took me to a place in which people were like flaming fire, and, when they wished, they appeared as men.
And they brought me to a place of darkness, and to a mountain the point of whose summit reached to heaven.

And I saw the places of the luminaries and the treasuries of the stars and of the thunder and in the uttermost depths, where were a fiery bow, arrows and their quiver, a fiery sword and all the lightnings.
And they took me to the river of fire in which the fire flows like water and discharges itself into the great sea towards the west.
I saw all the great rivers and came to the great darkness, and went to the place where no flesh walks.
I saw the mountains of darkness of winter and the place whence all the waters of the deep flow.
I saw the mouths of all the rivers of the earth and the mouth of the deep.
I saw the treasuries of all the winds: I saw how He has ordered all creation by His wisdom, and how He has founded the world upon them.
And I saw the cornerstone of the earth: then I saw the four winds which bear the earth and the firmament of the heaven.
And I saw how the winds stretch out the vaults of heaven, and have their station between heaven and earth: these are the pillars of the heaven.
I saw the winds of heaven which turn and bring the circumference of the sun and all the stars to their setting.
I saw the winds on the earth carrying the clouds: I saw the paths of the angels. I saw at the end of the earth the firmament of the heaven above.
And I proceeded to the south, and it was burning day and night, where there were seven mountains of precious stones, three towards the east, and three towards the south.
And as for those towards the east, one was of coloured stone, and one of pearl, and one jacinth, and those towards the south of red stone.
But the middle one reached to heaven like the throne of Yahuah (God), of stibium, and the top of the throne was of sapphire.
And I saw a flaming fire, and beyond that fire I saw a mountain whose summit reached to heaven.
And I saw there a deep abyss, with columns of heavenly fire, and among them I saw columns of fire fall, which were beyond measure alike towards the height and towards the depth.

And beyond that abyss I saw a place which had no firmament of the heaven above, and no firmly founded earth beneath it: there was no water upon it, and no birds, but it was a waste and horrible place.

I saw there seven stars like great burning mountains, and to me, when I inquired regarding them, the angel said: ’This place is the end of heaven and earth: this has become a prison for the stars and the host of heaven.
And the stars which roll over the fire are they which have transgressed the commandment of Yahuah (God) in the beginning of their rising, because they did not come forth at their appointed times.
And He was wroth with them, and bound them till the time when their guilt should be consummated (even) for ten thousand years.’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 17 launches Enoch’s cosmic journey through the “ends of the earth” and the lower heavenly realms, guided by angels. He witnesses the treasuries and mechanisms of creation (winds, luminaries, rivers of fire, mountains of jewels) that uphold Elohim’s ordered universe, then arrives at the prison for rebellious stars and the heavenly host—symbolizing fallen angels/Watchers bound in a desolate abyss. The vision reinforces the theme from earlier chapters: creation obeys perfectly (winds, stars keep their paths), but transgression (failing appointed times) brings eternal restraint. - Verses 1–7: Fiery beings, darkness mountain, treasuries of thunder/lightnings/stars, river of fire flowing into the western sea, great darkness, winter mountains, sources of earth’s waters/deep. - Cross-refs: Job 38:4–7 (Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth?… morning stars sang together); Psalm 104:5–9 (foundations of the earth… boundaries for waters); Revelation 21:1 (new heaven and new earth… no more sea—contrast to current order); Jeremiah 5:22 (sand as boundary for the sea). - Verses 8–12: Treasuries of winds supporting creation, cornerstone/four winds bearing earth/firmament, winds turning sun/stars, paths of angels, firmament at earth’s end. - Cross-refs: Job 26:7 (He stretches out the north over the void… hangs the earth on nothing); Psalm 148:8 (fire and hail, snow and clouds, stormy wind fulfilling His word); Isaiah 40:22 (He sits above the circle of the earth… stretches out heavens like a curtain). - Verses 13–21: Seven jewel mountains (east/south), central throne-like peak of sapphire/stibium, flaming fire, fiery abyss, desolate waste place, prison for seven transgressing stars/host of heaven—bound 10,000 years for failing appointed times. - Cross-refs: Exodus 24:10 (sapphire pavement under Elohim’s feet); Ezekiel 1:26 (throne like sapphire); Isaiah 24:21–22 (host of high ones punished… shut up in prison); 2 Peter 2:4 (angels who sinned… reserved unto judgment); Jude 1:6 (chains under darkness); Revelation 20:1–3 (binding for a thousand years—long-term restraint motif). Key Insight for Discernment: The vision contrasts Elohim’s perfect cosmic order (winds, luminaries, mountains fulfilling roles) with the punishment for rebellion—even among heavenly beings. The prison of stars/angels shows transgression disrupts harmony and incurs binding until full judgment. Enoch’s tour reveals hidden realities to affirm Yahuah’s sovereignty: creation testifies to His wisdom (Romans 1:20), yet free will allows rebellion—with consequences. Let this inspire awe at the Creator’s design and vigilance against straying from appointed paths (Psalm 19:1–4; Colossians 1:16–17). Test all things: does a teaching uphold Elohim’s order or lead to chaos? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Prisons of the Fallen and the Pillars of Heaven

verses.text: I saw the treasuries of all the winds: I saw how He has ordered all creation by His wisdom, and how He has founded the world upon them.
And I saw the cornerstone of the earth: then I saw the four winds which bear the earth and the firmament of the heaven.
And I saw how the winds stretch out the vaults of heaven, and have their station between heaven and earth: these are the pillars of the heaven.
I saw the winds of heaven which turn and bring the circumference of the sun and all the stars to their setting.
I saw the winds on the earth carrying the clouds: I saw the paths of the angels. I saw at the end of the earth the firmament of the heaven above.
And I proceeded to the south, and it was burning day and night, where there were seven mountains of precious stones, three towards the east, and three towards the south.
And as for those towards the east, one was of coloured stone, and one of pearl, and one jacinth, and those towards the south of red stone.
But the middle one reached to heaven like the throne of Yahuah (God), of stibium, and the top of the throne was of sapphire.
And I saw a flaming fire, and beyond that fire I saw a mountain whose summit reached to heaven.
And I saw there a deep abyss, with columns of heavenly fire, and among them I saw columns of fire fall, which were beyond measure alike towards the height and towards the depth.

And beyond that abyss I saw a place which had no firmament of the heaven above, and no firmly founded earth beneath it: there was no water upon it, and no birds, but it was a waste and horrible place.

I saw there seven stars like great burning mountains, and to me, when I inquired regarding them, the angel said: ’This place is the end of heaven and earth: this has become a prison for the stars and the host of heaven.
And the stars which roll over the fire are they which have transgressed the commandment of Yahuah (God) in the beginning of their rising, because they did not come forth at their appointed times.
And He was wroth with them, and bound them till the time when their guilt should be consummated (even) for ten thousand years.’

And from thence I went to another place, which was still more horrible than the former, and I saw a horrible thing: a great fire there which burnt and blazed, and the place was cleft as far as the abyss, being full of great descending columns of fire: neither its extent or magnitude could I see, nor could I conjecture.
Then I said: ‘How fearful is the place and how terrible to look upon!’

Then Uriel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered and said unto me: ‘Enoch, why hast thou such fear and affright?’ And I answered: ‘Because of this fearful place, and because of the spectacle of the pain.’
And he said unto me: ‘This place is the prison of the angels, and here they will be imprisoned for ever.’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 18 deepens the cosmic tour from Chapter 17, focusing on the mechanics of creation (winds as pillars supporting earth/heaven) and then shifting to the terrifying prisons: one for transgressing stars (fallen angels failing their courses), and another even more dreadful abyss of descending fire columns for the Watchers themselves. The desolate, birdless, waterless waste underscores the horror of eternal separation from Yahuah’s order. Uriel explains the finality: this is their everlasting prison. - Verses 1–5: Treasuries of winds, cornerstone/four winds bearing earth/firmament, winds stretching vaults and turning sun/stars, paths of angels at earth’s end. - Cross-refs: Job 26:7–11 (He hangs the earth on nothing… pillars of heaven tremble); Psalm 104:2–5 (stretches out heavens like a tent… foundations of the earth); Isaiah 40:22 (circle of the earth… stretches heavens like curtain); Job 38:4–7 (foundations of the earth… corner stone… morning stars sang). - Verses 6–14: Seven jewel mountains, central throne-like sapphire peak, flaming fire, deep fiery abyss, prison for seven stars/host of heaven—bound 10,000 years for failing appointed times. - Cross-refs: Exodus 24:10 (sapphire under Elohim’s feet); Ezekiel 1:26 (throne like sapphire); Isaiah 24:21–22 (host of high ones punished… shut in prison); 2 Peter 2:4 (angels… reserved in chains of darkness); Jude 1:6 (everlasting chains under darkness). - Verses 15–18: Even worse prison—great blazing fire, cleft abyss full of descending fire columns, extent unimaginable; Enoch’s fear; Uriel declares it the eternal prison of the angels. - Cross-refs: Matthew 25:41 (everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels); Revelation 20:10, 14–15 (lake of fire… devil cast in… tormented day and night forever); Revelation 14:10–11 (tormented with fire and brimstone… smoke of their torment ascends forever); Isaiah 66:24 (their worm shall not die, their fire not quenched). Key Insight for Discernment: The vision reveals Yahuah’s meticulous order—winds, stars, luminaries all serve precisely—yet rebellion (even among heavenly hosts) leads to terrifying, eternal confinement in fire and desolation. The dual prisons (stars/host, then angels/Watchers) show graduated judgment for cosmic transgression. Enoch’s fear is natural before such holiness and justice; Uriel’s explanation comforts the righteous while warning the rebellious. This affirms Elohim’s sovereignty: creation glorifies Him (Psalm 19:1), but defiance meets irreversible consequence. Let it inspire reverence and obedience—peace is for those who keep their appointed place (Romans 1:20; Colossians 1:16–17). Test all things: does a path honor Yahuah’s order or invite chaos? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Binding of the Watchers and the Spirits of the Giants

verses.text: And Uriel said to me: ’Here shall stand the angels who have connected themselves with women, and their spirits assuming many different forms are defiling mankind and shall lead them astray into sacrificing to demons as gods, here shall they stand, till the day of the great judgement in which they shall be judged till they are made an end of.
And the women also of the angels who went astray shall become sirens.’
And I, Enoch, alone saw the vision, the ends of all things: and no man shall see as I have seen.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 19 provides Uriel’s concise explanation of the prisons seen in Chapters 17–18: the fallen Watchers (who united with women) are bound here until the great judgment, when they face final end. Their disembodied giant offspring become evil spirits/demons that defile humanity, leading people into idolatry and demon worship. The women involved are transformed into sirens (seductive spirits in some traditions). Enoch alone witnesses this full cosmic vision—emphasizing his unique role as scribe and visionary. - Verse 1: The angels who defiled themselves with women are imprisoned; their spirits (from giants) take various forms, defile mankind, and incite demon/sacrifice worship until the great judgment destroys them. - Cross-refs: Deuteronomy 32:17 (they sacrificed to demons, not to Elohim (God)); Psalm 106:37 (sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons); 1 Corinthians 10:20 (what pagans sacrifice they sacrifice to demons); Revelation 9:20 (did not repent of worshiping demons); 2 Peter 2:4 (angels who sinned… reserved for judgment); Jude 1:6 (angels… reserved in everlasting chains under darkness for the judgment of the great day). - Verse 2: The women who went astray with the angels become sirens (in some ancient interpretations: seductive, destructive spirits luring men to ruin). - Cross-refs: Isaiah 13:21–22 (wild beasts and owls/satyrs haunt desolate places—echo of unclean spirits in waste lands); Revelation 18:2 (Babylon become habitation of demons… unclean spirits… unclean birds); Proverbs 7:10–27 (seductive woman leading to death—parallel imagery); 1 Timothy 4:1 (departing from faith, giving heed to deceiving spirits and doctrines of demons). - Verse 3: Enoch alone beholds the full vision of “the ends of all things”—no other human sees as he has. - Cross-refs: Genesis 5:24 (Enoch walked with Elohim (God) and was not); Hebrews 11:5 (by faith Enoch was translated… had testimony he pleased Elohim (God)); 2 Corinthians 12:2–4 (man caught up to third heaven… heard inexpressible words not lawful for man to utter); Revelation 1:1 (revelation of Yahusha (Jesus) Messiah… signified to His servant John). Key Insight for Discernment: This chapter links the Watchers’ sin directly to the origin and activity of demons/evil spirits: disembodied giants continue their fathers’ work by deceiving humanity into idolatry and defilement. The binding until “the great judgment” shows Yahuah’s justice is patient yet certain—evil is restrained but not yet eradicated. Enoch’s exclusive vision highlights privileged revelation for the righteous to warn and instruct. Let this affirm spiritual realities: idolatry is demon-linked (1 Corinthians 10:19–20), and deception persists until final consummation. Test spirits and teachings rigorously—do they lead to worship of Yahuah (God) alone or to compromise? (1 John 4:1; Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Seven Holy Archangels and Their Duties

verses.text: And these are the names of the holy angels who watch.
Uriel, one of the holy angels, who is over the world and over Tartarus.
Raphael, one of the holy angels, who is over the spirits of men.
Raguel, one of the holy angels who takes vengeance on the world of the luminaries.
Michael, one of the holy and honoured angels, who is set over the best part of mankind and over chaos.
Saraqâêl, one of the holy angels, who is set over the spirits of those who sin in the spirit.
Gabriel, one of the holy angels, who is over Paradise and the serpents and the Cherubim.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 20 functions as a transitional catalog, naming seven prominent archangels (holy watchers) and assigning each a domain of oversight in Yahuah’s ordered creation. This list highlights the structured hierarchy of heaven: angels appointed to govern natural forces, human spirits, judgment, chaos, sin, and sacred realms. It contrasts the faithful holy angels with the fallen Watchers (Ch. 6–19), showing Yahuah’s faithful administration amid rebellion. - Uriel — Oversees the world and Tartarus (the abyss/prison realm, linking to the fiery prisons in Ch. 17–19). - Cross-refs: 2 Esdras 4:1 (Uriel sent to instruct Ezra); Revelation 9:1–2 (angel with key to bottomless pit—abyss imagery); Revelation 20:1–3 (angel binds Satan in abyss). - Raphael — Oversees the spirits of men (healing, binding evil spirits; see Tobit tradition). - Cross-refs: Tobit 12:15 (Raphael one of seven angels who present prayers); Revelation 8:2–5 (seven angels with trumpets—prayers ascending). - Raguel — Takes vengeance on the world of the luminaries (judging rebellious stars/angels, cf. Ch. 18). - Cross-refs: Isaiah 24:21 (Yahuah (God) punishes host of high ones); Revelation 12:7–9 (Michael and angels war against dragon and stars swept down). - Michael — Set over the best part of mankind and over chaos (protector of Israel, warrior against disorder). - Cross-refs: Daniel 10:13, 21; 12:1 (Michael, great prince who stands for children of your people); Jude 1:9 (Michael the archangel contending with devil); Revelation 12:7 (Michael and his angels fought against the dragon). - Saraqâêl (or Sariel) — Set over spirits who sin in the spirit (oversight of spiritual transgressions). - Cross-refs: 1 Chronicles 21:1 (Satan stands against Israel—spiritual opposition); Ephesians 6:12 (spiritual forces of evil in heavenly places). - Gabriel — Over Paradise, serpents, and Cherubim (messenger, guardian of sacred spaces). - Cross-refs: Daniel 8:16; 9:21 (Gabriel explains visions); Luke 1:19, 26 (Gabriel stands in presence of Elohim (God), sent to Mary); Genesis 3:24 (cherubim guard Eden); Ezekiel 10:1–22 (cherubim under throne). Key Insight for Discernment: The seven archangels illustrate Yahuah’s delegated order—faithful angels maintain creation, judge rebellion, protect the righteous, and oversee spiritual realms. This contrasts sharply with the fallen Watchers’ anarchy. The list affirms heaven’s hierarchy serves Elohim’s purposes: justice, protection, and restoration. It encourages trust in Yahuah’s administration—even chaos and evil are under oversight until final judgment. Let this remind us: spiritual warfare exists, but victory belongs to Yahuah (God) and His faithful servants (Daniel 12:1; Revelation 12:11). Test all things: align with His appointed order, not rebellion (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Fiery Prison of the Fallen Stars and Angels

verses.text: And I proceeded to where things were chaotic.

And I saw there something which was like a cloud of fire, and when I looked, I saw a deep abyss with columns of heavenly fire, and among them I saw columns of fire fall, which were beyond measure alike towards the height and towards the depth.

And beyond that abyss I saw a place which had no firmament of the heaven above, and no firmly founded earth beneath it: there was no water upon it, and no birds, but it was a waste and horrible place.
I saw there seven stars like great burning mountains, and to me, when I inquired regarding them, the angel said:
’This place is the end of heaven and earth: this has become a prison for the stars and the host of heaven.
And the stars which roll over the fire are they which have transgressed the commandment of Yahuah (God) in the beginning of their rising, because they did not come forth at their appointed times.
And He was wroth with them, and bound them till the time when their guilt should be consummated (even) for ten thousand years.’

And from thence I proceeded to another place, which was still more horrible than the former, and I saw a horrible thing: a great fire there which burnt and blazed, and the place was cleft as far as the abyss, being full of great descending columns of fire: neither its extent or magnitude could I see, nor could I conjecture.
Then I said: ‘How fearful is the place and how terrible to look upon!’

Then Uriel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered and said unto me: ‘Enoch, why hast thou such fear and affright?’ And I answered: ‘Because of this fearful place, and because of the spectacle of the pain.’
And he said unto me: ‘This place is the prison of the angels, and here they will be imprisoned for ever.’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 21 intensifies the horror of the cosmic prisons introduced in Chapters 17–19. Enoch is led to two terrifying abysses: one for the seven transgressing stars (fallen angels who failed their ordained courses), bound for 10,000 years; and a deeper, more dreadful chasm of descending fire columns for the Watchers themselves—their eternal prison. The utter desolation (no firmament, no earth, no water, no birds) and unimaginable fire emphasize complete separation from Yahuah’s ordered creation. Enoch’s fear is met with Uriel’s calm explanation: this is the everlasting holding place for the rebellious angels. - Verses 1–7: First abyss—chaotic fire clouds, deep pit with falling fire columns; prison for stars/host of heaven who disobeyed appointed times—bound until guilt consummated (10,000 years). - Cross-refs: Job 38:31–33 (can you bind chains of Pleiades or loose cords of Orion?… ordinances of heaven); Isaiah 24:21–22 (Yahuah (God) punishes host of high ones… shut up in prison… after many days they shall be visited); 2 Peter 2:4 (angels who sinned… cast down to hell… chains of darkness reserved for judgment); Jude 1:6 (angels… kept not their first estate… reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day). - Verses 8–11: Second, worse prison—great blazing fire, cleft abyss with descending fire pillars (extent unmeasurable); Enoch’s terror; Uriel declares it the eternal prison of the angels. - Cross-refs: Matthew 25:41 (everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels); Revelation 20:10 (devil… cast into lake of fire and brimstone… tormented day and night for ever and ever); Revelation 14:10–11 (tormented with fire and brimstone… smoke of their torment ascends up for ever and ever); Isaiah 66:24 (their worm shall not die, their fire shall not be quenched); Mark 9:43–48 (hell, where their worm does not die and fire is not quenched). Key Insight for Discernment: The double prison vision reveals graduated judgment—Yahuah’s order is so precise that even stars/angels failing their “appointed times” face binding; willful defilement (Watchers) merits deeper, eternal torment. The desolation contrasts sharply with the flourishing renewal promised to the righteous (Ch. 10–11). Enoch’s fear is human and appropriate before divine justice; Uriel’s response reassures that Yahuah’s ways are just. This warns against any rebellion—cosmic or personal—while affirming hope for the faithful: judgment is final for the unrepentant, but mercy endures for those who walk in righteousness (Psalm 19:1–4; Romans 1:20). Test all things: does a path keep Yahuah’s ordinances or lead to the abyss? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Four Hollow Places for the Spirits of the Dead

verses.text: And thence I proceeded to another place, where I saw a great and glorious device at the ends of the whole earth.
Here I saw a deep abyss with columns of heavenly fire, and among them I saw columns of fire fall, which were beyond measure alike towards the height and towards the depth.

And beyond that abyss I saw a place which had no firmament of the heaven above, and no firmly founded earth beneath it: there was no water upon it, and no birds, but it was a waste and horrible place.
And there I saw seven stars of the heaven bound together like great mountains and burning with fire.
Then I said: ‘For what sin are they bound, and on what account have they been cast in hither?’

Then Uriel, one of the holy angels, who was with me, answered and said unto me: ‘Enoch, why hast thou such fear and affright?’ And I answered: ‘Because of this fearful place, and because of the spectacle of the pain.’
And he said unto me: ‘This place is the prison of the angels, and here they will be imprisoned for ever.’
And I proceeded to another place, and he showed me in the west another great and glorious mountain of hard rock.
And there was in it four hollow places, deep and wide and very smooth. How smooth are the hollow places and deep and dark to look at.

Then Raphael, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered and said unto me: ’These hollow places have been created for this very purpose, that the spirits of the souls of the dead should assemble therein, yea that all the souls of the children of men should assemble here.
And these places have been made for them until the day of their judgement and until their appointed period, till the great judgement comes upon them.’
I saw (the spirits of) the dead making suit, and their petition went forth to heaven, but they received no answer.
And I inquired of Raphael, the angel who was with me, saying: ‘Whose is this spirit whose suit is thus presented?’

And he answered me saying: ‘This is the spirit which went forth from Abel, whom his brother Cain slew, and he makes his suit against him till his seed is destroyed from the face of the earth, and his seed is annihilated from amongst the seed of men.’
Then I asked regarding it, and regarding all the hollow places: ‘Why is one separated from the other?’

And he answered me and said unto me: ’These three have been made that the spirits of the dead might be separated. And such a division has been made (for) the spirits of the righteous, in which there is the bright spring of water.
And such has been made for sinners when they die and are buried in the earth and judgement has not been executed on them in their lifetime.

Here their spirits shall be set apart in this great pain till the great day of judgement and punishment and torment of those who curse for ever and retribution for their spirits. There He shall bind them for ever.
And this division has been made for the spirits of those who make their suit, who make disclosures concerning their destruction, when they died in the days of the sinners.

Such has been made for the spirits of men who were not righteous but sinners, and of the transgressors: they shall be with criminals and transgressors, but their spirits shall not be slain on the day of judgement nor shall they be raised from thence.’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 22 introduces the intermediate state of human souls after death, before the final resurrection and judgment. Enoch sees four hollow places (compartments) in a great mountain, each designated for different categories of departed spirits: the righteous (with a bright spring of water, implying refreshment); sinners who died without earthly punishment (in great pain, bound until judgment); the victims/slaughtered (making suit for justice, like Abel’s spirit crying out); and a fourth for certain sinners/transgressors whose spirits remain in separation but are not raised. Raphael explains these divisions preserve order until Yahuah’s great judgment. - Verses 1–7: Transition from previous prison vision; reaffirms the angelic prison of fire and desolation. - Cross-refs: Revelation 20:13–14 (death and hades gave up the dead… judged according to works); Luke 16:19–31 (rich man in hades in torment, Lazarus in Abraham’s bosom—parallel compartments). - Verses 8–11: Four hollow places created for assembling souls of the dead until the day of judgment. - Cross-refs: Daniel 12:2 (many who sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, some to shame and everlasting contempt); John 5:28–29 (all in graves shall hear His voice and come forth… resurrection of life or condemnation). - Verses 12–14: Abel’s spirit petitions against Cain’s seed—justice delayed but not forgotten. - Cross-refs: Genesis 4:10 (voice of your brother’s blood cries to Me from the ground); Hebrews 11:4 (Abel… being dead yet speaks); Revelation 6:9–10 (souls under the altar cry, “How long, O Master?”). - Verses 15–20: Divisions explained—righteous in light/refreshment; unpunished sinners in pain until judgment; victims seeking vindication; some sinners separated but not resurrected (debated fate in ancient views). - Cross-refs: Luke 16:22–26 (great gulf fixed between righteous and torment); 2 Peter 2:9 (Yahuah (God) knows how to deliver the godly out of temptations and to reserve the unjust under punishment for the day of judgment); Revelation 20:4–6 (first resurrection—blessed and holy); Psalm 9:17 (wicked shall be turned into hell… all nations that forget Elohim (God)). Key Insight for Discernment: The four compartments show Yahuah’s justice is meticulous—souls are separated according to deeds and circumstances, preserved until the great judgment. No immediate universal reward or punishment; the righteous rest in hope, the wicked await torment, victims cry for vindication (heard by Elohim (God)). This bridges Old Testament Sheol concepts with New Testament teachings on intermediate state and resurrection. It affirms accountability: earthly impunity does not mean eternal escape. Let this encourage righteous living and trust in Yahuah’s perfect timing (Ecclesiastes 12:14; Romans 2:5–11). Test all things: does a doctrine align with Scripture’s witness on judgment and resurrection? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Fiery Luminaries and Their Lawful Courses

verses.text: And I proceeded to another place, to the west of the ends of the earth.
And I saw there a burning fire which ran without resting, and paused not from its course day or night but (ran) regularly.
And I asked saying: ‘What is this which never rests?’

Then Raguel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered me and said unto me: ‘This course of fire which thou hast seen is the fire which surrounds the sun, and which the sun rolls round upon the whole earth, and which the sun sets.’
And I saw chariots in the heaven, running in the world above to the right and to the left of the sun.

And I saw six portals out of which the sun rises, and six portals in which the sun sets and the moon rises and sets in those portals, and the leaders of the stars and those whom they lead: six in the east and six in the west following them, and also many other chariots and their leaders.
And the greatness of them all is as the greatness of the sun, and their chariots are like the chariots of the sun.
And all the stars rise and set in their own order, and they do not change their course.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 23 returns to the theme of creation’s perfect obedience (echoing Chapters 2–5), now through the sun, moon, stars, and their chariots/portals. Enoch observes the ceaseless, fiery circuit of the sun (surrounded by fire that never rests), six eastern rising portals and six western setting portals for sun, moon, and stars, each following precise, unchanging paths led by appointed leaders. This vision reinforces Yahuah’s wisdom in establishing fixed laws for the luminaries—no deviation, no transgression—standing in stark contrast to the fallen Watchers and stars who abandoned their appointed times (Ch. 18, 21). - Verses 1–4: Fiery, ever-running course surrounding the sun, rolling around the earth without pause—Raguel explains it as the sun’s encircling fire. - Cross-refs: Psalm 19:4–6 (sun’s circuit from end of heaven… nothing hidden from its heat); Psalm 104:19 (appointed the moon for seasons; sun knows its going down); Ecclesiastes 1:5 (sun rises and sun sets, hastens to place where it rises). - Verses 5–8: Chariots running right/left of sun; six portals east/west for rising/setting of sun, moon, stars; leaders guide them; all maintain greatness/order like the sun—no change in course. - Cross-refs: Genesis 1:14–18 (lights in firmament for signs, seasons, days, years… to rule day/night); Job 38:31–33 (bind Pleiades… loose Orion… know ordinances of heavens?); Jeremiah 31:35 (Yahuah (God) gives sun for light by day, ordinances of moon/stars… do not fail); Psalm 148:3–6 (sun, moon, stars… praise Yahuah (God)… established them forever… gave decree not to pass away). Key Insight for Discernment: The luminaries’ flawless obedience testifies to Yahuah’s sovereign design—fixed portals, leaders, unchanging courses declare His glory and reliability. This contrasts sharply with rebellious beings (Watchers, transgressing stars) who abandoned their stations. The vision calls us to emulate creation’s faithfulness: keep our appointed paths in obedience to Yahuah (God). Let the sun’s daily circuit remind us of His steadfast covenant and coming judgment on disorder (Malachi 4:2; Romans 1:20; Psalm 19:1–4). Test all things: does a way align with Elohim’s unchanging order or lead to deviation? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Seven Mountains and the Fragrant Tree of Life

verses.text: And from thence I proceeded to another place of the earth, and he showed me a mountain of fire which burnt day and night.

And I went beyond it and saw seven magnificent mountains all differing from each other, and the stones thereof were magnificent and beautiful, and their form was glorious, and their appearance was beautiful. Three towards the east, one founded on the other, and three towards the south, one upon the other, and deep rough ravines, no one of which joined with any other.
And the seventh mountain was in the midst of them, and it excelled them in height, resembling the seat of a throne: and fragrant trees encircled the mountain.

And amongst them was a tree such as I had never yet smelt, neither was any amongst them nor were others like it: it had a fragrance beyond all fragrance, and its leaves and blooms and wood wither not for ever: and its fruit is beautiful, and its fruit resembles the dates of a palm.
Then I said: ‘Behold this beautiful tree, and what is its name?’
Then answered Michael, one of the holy and honoured angels who was with me, and was their leader.
And he said unto me: ‘Enoch, why dost thou ask me regarding the fragrance of the tree, and why dost thou wish to learn the truth?’
Then I answered him saying: ‘I wish to know about everything, but especially about this tree.’

And he answered saying: ’This high mountain which thou hast seen, whose summit is like the throne of Yahuah (God), is His throne, where the Holy Great One, Yahuah (God) of Glory, the Eternal King, will sit, when He shall come down to visit the earth with goodness.
And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when His righteousness and His majesty shall be punished for ever in its fruit to the righteous and humble.
To the righteous it shall be given for food, and its fruit shall be for life to the elect; it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (God), the Eternal King.

Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, and into the holy place shall they enter; and its fragrance shall be in their bones, and they shall live a long life on earth, such as thy fathers lived: and in their days shall no sorrow or plague or torment or calamity touch them.’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 24 builds on the seven jewel mountains (from Ch. 18, 23) but centers on the central, exalted mountain resembling Yahuah’s throne and the unique, eternally fragrant tree at its heart—widely understood as the tree of life (Genesis 2–3; Revelation 22). Michael explains its guarded status until the great judgment, when its fruit will be given to the righteous and humble for eternal life, joy, and healing. The tree will be transplanted to the holy place (temple of Yahuah (God)), bringing longevity and freedom from sorrow—foreshadowing the restored Edenic paradise for the elect. - Verses 1–3: Fiery mountain transition; seven magnificent mountains (three east, three south, one central towering like a throne), encircled by fragrant trees. - Cross-refs: Ezekiel 28:13–14 (Eden… every precious stone… anointed cherub on holy mountain of Elohim (God)); Revelation 21:10–11 (holy city… glory of Elohim (God)… radiance like jasper and crystal). - Verses 4–8: Unique tree—fragrance beyond all, unfading leaves/fruit like palm dates; Enoch’s awe and inquiry. - Cross-refs: Genesis 2:9 (tree of life in midst of garden); Genesis 3:22–24 (lest he take also of tree of life… cherubim guard way); Proverbs 3:18 (wisdom is a tree of life to those who lay hold of her); Revelation 22:2 (tree of life… leaves for healing of nations). - Verses 9–12: Central mountain as Yahuah’s throne for His coming in goodness; tree untouchable until judgment—then fruit given to righteous for life; transplanted to holy place/temple; eternal joy, no sorrow/plague/calamity, long life like ancestors. - Cross-refs: Revelation 22:1–5 (river of water of life… tree of life… no more curse… they shall reign for ever); Isaiah 65:17–25 (new heavens/new earth… no more weeping… long life… wolf/lamb feed together); Ezekiel 47:12 (trees by river… leaves not fade… fruit not fail… leaves for medicine); Psalm 92:12–14 (righteous flourish like palm tree… bear fruit in old age); Revelation 21:4 (no more death, sorrow, crying, pain—former things passed away). Key Insight for Discernment: The tree of life—guarded since Eden—symbolizes restored access to eternal life for the righteous after judgment. Its fruit brings healing, joy, longevity, and freedom from affliction, pointing to the ultimate renewal of creation under Yahuah’s throne-rule. This vision contrasts the desolation of rebellion (prisons earlier) with the abundance awaiting the faithful. It encourages perseverance: the humble/righteous inherit the promise (Revelation 2:7—“to him who overcomes I will give to eat from the tree of life”). Let this hope anchor you—Yahuah (God) preserves what is holy and restores what sin marred (Romans 8:19–23). Test all things: does a teaching lead toward this promised restoration or away from Yahuah’s order? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: Michael Explains the Throne Mountain and the Tree of Life

verses.text: And he answered and said unto me, and I heard his voice: ’Fear not, Enoch, thou righteous man and scribe of righteousness: approach hither and hear my voice.
And go, say to the Watchers of heaven, who have sent thee to intercede for them: "You should intercede for men, and not men for you:

Wherefore have ye left the high, holy, and eternal heaven, and lain with women, and defiled yourselves with the daughters of men and taken to yourselves wives, and done like the children of earth, and begotten giants (as your) sons?

And though ye were holy, spiritual, living the eternal life, you have defiled yourselves with the blood of women, and have begotten (children) with the blood of flesh, and, as the children of men, have lusted after flesh and blood as those also do who die and perish.
Therefore have I given them wives also that they might impregnate them, and beget children by them, that thus the earth might be filled with their children.
And now, the giants, who are produced from the spirits and flesh, shall be called evil spirits upon the earth, and on the earth shall be their dwelling.

Evil spirits have proceeded from their bodies; because they are born from men and from the holy Watchers is their beginning and primal origin; evil spirits they will be upon earth and evil spirits will they be called.
As for the spirits of heaven, in heaven shall be their dwelling, but as for the spirits of the earth which were born upon the earth, on the earth shall be their dwelling.

And the spirits of the giants afflict, oppress, destroy, attack, do battle, and work destruction on the earth, and cause trouble: they take no food, but nevertheless hunger and thirst, and cause offences.
And these spirits shall rise up against the children of men and against the women, because they have proceeded from them.

From the days of the slaughter and destruction and death of the giants, from the souls of whose flesh the spirits, having gone forth, shall destroy without incurring judgement—thus shall they destroy until the day of the consummation, the great judgement in which the age shall be consummated, over the Watchers and the godless, yea, shall be wholly consummated."’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 25 continues Michael’s explanation from Chapter 24, emphasizing the central mountain as Yahuah’s future throne for His visitation in goodness (judgment and blessing). The tree of life—untouchable by mortals until the great judgment—is reserved for the righteous and humble: its fruit grants life, healing, and joy; it will be transplanted to the holy place (temple of Yahuah (God)), bringing eternal blessing. The elect will live long, sorrow-free lives, echoing pre-fall longevity and Edenic peace. This vision closes the mountain/tree sequence with hope for restoration after judgment. - Verses 1–4: The high mountain as Yahuah’s throne for His coming in goodness; tree untouchable until judgment—then fruit given to righteous/humble. - Cross-refs: Isaiah 66:1 (heaven is My throne, earth My footstool); Revelation 22:1–2 (throne of Elohim (God) and the Lamb… tree of life bearing twelve fruits); Ezekiel 47:12 (trees by river… fruit not fail… leaves for healing). - Verses 5–9: Tree’s fruit for food/life to the elect; transplanted to holy place/temple of Yahuah (God); fragrance in bones, long life, no sorrow/plague/torment/calamity. - Cross-refs: Revelation 2:7 (to him who overcomes I will give to eat from the tree of life in paradise of Elohim (God)); Revelation 22:14 (blessed are those who wash robes… right to tree of life); Isaiah 65:20–23 (no more infant of days… sinner accursed at 100… elect enjoy work of hands); Psalm 92:12–14 (righteous flourish… bear fruit in old age); Hosea 14:5–7 (like lily… fragrance like Lebanon… dwell under his shadow). Key Insight for Discernment: The tree of life—guarded since Eden—symbolizes restored immortality and healing for the righteous after the great judgment. Yahuah’s throne on the central mountain signifies His direct rule and visitation in goodness (blessing the faithful, punishing evil). This contrasts the fiery prisons of rebellion with the fragrant, life-giving future for the elect—long life, joy, no affliction. It points forward to the renewed creation where access to life is open to the humble/righteous (Revelation 22:14). Let this vision strengthen endurance: judgment separates the wicked from the blessed, but the humble inherit eternal good (James 4:10; 1 Peter 5:6). Test all things: does a path lead toward this promised restoration or echo the Watchers’ fall? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Holy Mountain Zion and Its Blessed Valley

verses.text: And I proceeded to the middle of the earth, and saw there a blessed and fertile place, and there were many trees in it.
And there was a holy mountain, and under the mountain to the east there was a stream flowing, and to the south another stream.
And on the mountain there was a tree, the colour of whose fragrance was like the mastic tree.
And on the sides of those streams I saw fragrant trees, and the fragrance of them was beyond all fragrance.
And I said: ‘What is this fragrant tree?’
And Michael, one of the holy and honoured angels who was with me, answered and said unto me:

’This high mountain which thou hast seen, whose summit is like the throne of Yahuah (God), is the throne of Yahuah (God), the Holy Great One, the Eternal King, when He shall come down to visit the earth with goodness.

And as for this fragrant tree, no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when His righteousness and His majesty shall be avenged on the sinners in its fruit to the righteous and humble.
To the righteous it shall be given for food, and its fruit shall be for life to the elect; it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (God), the Eternal King.

Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, and into the holy place shall they enter; and its fragrance shall be in their bones, and they shall live a long life on earth, such as thy fathers lived: and in their days shall no sorrow or plague or torment or calamity touch them.’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 26 presents a vision of the holy mountain—identified as Zion/Jerusalem in its eschatological glory—surrounded by fertile land, flowing streams, and fragrant trees. The central fragrant tree (again evoking the tree of life from Ch. 24–25) is guarded until the great judgment, when its fruit will nourish the righteous, granting long life, joy, and freedom from affliction. The mountain serves as Yahuah’s throne for His visitation in goodness, blending present geography with future restoration: the holy city renewed, the elect dwelling in blessing. - Verses 1–4: Blessed fertile place in earth’s middle; holy mountain with east/south streams; fragrant trees beyond all fragrance. - Cross-refs: Psalm 46:4–5 (river whose streams make glad the city of Elohim (God), the holy place of the tabernacle of the Most High); Psalm 48:1–2 (great King… beautiful for situation, joy of the whole earth, mount Zion); Isaiah 33:20–21 (Zion… place of broad rivers and streams); Ezekiel 47:1–12 (water flowing from under the threshold of the temple… trees on both sides… leaves for medicine, fruit not fail). - Verses 5–10: Michael explains the mountain as Yahuah’s throne for visitation in goodness; tree of life untouchable until judgment—then fruit for righteous/elect, transplanted to temple of Yahuah (God); joy, entry to holy place, fragrance in bones, long life without sorrow/plague/torment/calamity. - Cross-refs: Revelation 22:1–5 (river of water of life from throne of Elohim (God) and Lamb… tree of life… no more curse… they shall reign forever); Isaiah 65:17–25 (new heavens and new earth… no more weeping… long life… elect enjoy work of hands); Ezekiel 47:12 (trees by river… leaves not fade… fruit not fail); Revelation 21:3–4 (tabernacle of Elohim (God) with men… no more death, sorrow, crying, pain); Zechariah 14:8–11 (living waters flow from Jerusalem… Yahuah (God) shall be king over all the earth… Jerusalem inhabited safely). Key Insight for Discernment: The holy mountain/Zion vision merges present reality (Jerusalem’s location) with future glory: Yahuah’s throne descends in goodness to bless the righteous, the tree of life restores Edenic life, and the elect inherit a sorrow-free existence. Streams and fragrant trees symbolize abundance, healing, and divine presence. This contrasts the prisons of rebellion with the promised paradise for the humble/elect—judgment purges evil, renewal follows. It encourages faithfulness: Zion’s future belongs to those who endure (Hebrews 12:22–24; Revelation 3:12). Let this hope strengthen you—Yahuah (God) visits to redeem and dwell with His people (Revelation 21:3). Test all things: does a path lead toward this holy restoration or echo the Watchers’ corruption? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Cursed Valley and the Final Judgment of the Wicked

verses.text: And I proceeded to the middle of the earth, and saw there a blessed and fertile place, and there were many trees in it.
And there was a holy mountain, and under the mountain to the east there was a stream flowing, and to the south another stream.
And on the mountain there was a tree, the colour of whose fragrance was like the mastic tree.
And on the sides of those streams I saw fragrant trees, and the fragrance of them was beyond all fragrance.
And I said: ‘What is this fragrant tree?’

And Michael, one of the holy and honoured angels who was with me, answered and said unto me: ’This high mountain which thou hast seen, whose summit is like the throne of Yahuah (God), is the throne of Yahuah (God), the Holy Great One, the Eternal King, when He shall come down to visit the earth with goodness.
And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when His righteousness and His majesty shall be punished for ever in its fruit to the righteous and humble.
To the righteous it shall be given for food, and its fruit shall be for life to the elect; it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (God), the Eternal King.

Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, and into the holy place shall they enter; and its fragrance shall be in their bones, and they shall live a long life on earth, such as thy fathers lived: and in their days shall no sorrow or plague or torment or calamity touch them.’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 27 presents a stark contrast to the blessed holy mountain of Chapter 26: a deep, accursed valley (likely Gehenna/Hinnom imagery) designated as the place of final gathering and eternal judgment for the wicked, the godless, and the cursed. It is a desolate ravine where the unrighteous are collected for condemnation—no fragrance, no life, only separation from Yahuah’s goodness. The chapter underscores the binary outcome at the great judgment: blessing and life for the elect on the holy mountain, curse and torment for the wicked in the valley. - Verses 1–4: Transition to the cursed valley—deep, hollow, accursed, separated from the holy mountain; no trees or fragrance, only desolation. - Cross-refs: Isaiah 66:24 (they shall go forth and look on the corpses of the men who have rebelled against Me; their worm shall not die, their fire shall not be quenched); Jeremiah 7:31–32 (valley of Hinnom… Topheth… slaughter until no place left); Mark 9:43–48 (Gehenna, where their worm does not die and fire is not quenched). - Verses 5–9: The valley is for the accursed, the godless, those who will be gathered for final judgment and eternal curse; no blessing, no entry to the holy place—contrast to the righteous’ fate. - Cross-refs: Matthew 25:41, 46 (Depart from Me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels… eternal punishment); Revelation 20:11–15 (great white throne… dead judged according to works… death and hades cast into lake of fire… anyone not found in book of life cast into lake of fire); Daniel 12:2 (some to everlasting life, others to shame and everlasting contempt); Matthew 13:49–50 (angels separate wicked from righteous… cast into furnace of fire… weeping and gnashing of teeth). Key Insight for Discernment: The juxtaposition of the holy mountain (life, fragrance, throne of blessing) and the cursed valley (death, desolation, eternal judgment) illustrates Yahuah’s perfect justice: the righteous inherit restoration and peace, while the unrepentant face separation and torment. This is not arbitrary—Yahuah’s visitation brings goodness to the humble but condemnation to the rebellious. The vision warns of final accountability: deeds determine destiny (Romans 2:6–11). It encourages turning from sin to righteousness while hope remains—mercy for the repentant, but no peace for the wicked (Isaiah 57:21). Let this binary outcome sharpen discernment: choose the path to the holy mountain (Hebrews 12:22–24). Test all things: does a way lead to life with Yahuah (God) or to the cursed valley? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Fragrant Paradise in the East

verses.text: And from thence I proceeded to another place in the east of the earth.
And I saw there sweet-smelling trees, and trees of the mastic, and myrrh, and trees whose fragrance was beyond all fragrance.
And the trees of the mastic exuded gum like the almond, and the myrrh trees exuded myrrh like the bark of the almond.
And beyond these trees I proceeded to the east, and I saw another place, a valley full of water.
And there was a tree which had fragrance such as the mastic tree, and its fruit was like the clusters of the vine, very beautiful; and the fragrance of that tree penetrated far beyond the valley.
And I said: ‘This fragrant tree is beautiful, and its fruit is beautiful to behold.’
Then answered Michael, one of the holy and honoured angels who was with me, and said unto me:
‘Enoch, why dost thou ask me regarding the fragrance of this tree and why dost thou wish to learn the truth?’
And I answered him saying: ‘I wish to know about everything, but especially about this tree.’

And he answered saying: ’This high mountain which thou hast seen, whose summit is like the throne of Yahuah (God), is His throne, where the Holy Great One, Yahuah (God) of Glory, the Eternal King, will sit, when He shall come down to visit the earth with goodness.

And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when His righteousness and His majesty shall be avenged on the sinners in its fruit to the righteous and humble.
To the righteous it shall be given for food, and its fruit shall be for life to the elect; it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (God), the Eternal King.

Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, and into the holy place shall they enter; and its fragrance shall be in their bones, and they shall live a long life on earth, such as thy fathers lived: and in their days shall no sorrow or plague or torment or calamity touch them.’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 28 expands the eastward journey into a paradise region filled with aromatic trees (mastic, myrrh, pepper-like spices, vine clusters)—their overwhelming fragrance and unfading beauty symbolize the abundance of the renewed creation. The central fragrant tree (again the tree of life motif) is highlighted for its penetrating scent and beauty, with Michael reiterating its guarded status until the great judgment. After judgment, its fruit nourishes the righteous/elect, granting life, joy, and long, affliction-free existence when transplanted to Yahuah’s temple/holy place. - Verses 1–5: Eastward progression to sweet-smelling trees, mastic (gum like almond), myrrh (bark exuding), and a valley tree with vine-like fruit whose fragrance fills the region. - Cross-refs: Genesis 2:9 (tree of life in garden… pleasant to sight and good for food); Song of Solomon 4:13–14 (paradise of pomegranates with pleasant fruits, henna with spikenard, spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with all trees of frankincense, myrrh and aloes); Revelation 22:2 (tree of life… leaves for healing of nations—fragrance implied in life-giving abundance). - Verses 6–13: Enoch’s inquiry; Michael’s explanation repeats the throne-mountain and tree-of-life promise—untouchable until judgment, then fruit for the righteous/elect, transplanted to temple, bringing joy, entry to holy place, fragrance in bones, long life without sorrow/plague/torment/calamity. - Cross-refs: Revelation 2:7 (to him who overcomes I will give to eat from the tree of life in paradise of Elohim (God)); Isaiah 35:1–2, 10 (wilderness glad… desert rejoice and blossom… ransomed of Yahuah (God) return… everlasting joy upon their heads… sorrow and sighing flee away); Ezekiel 47:12 (trees by river… fruit not fail… leaves not fade); Psalm 16:11 (in Your presence is fullness of joy… pleasures forevermore); Revelation 21:4 (no more death, sorrow, crying, pain). Key Insight for Discernment: The eastward paradise of fragrance and life contrasts the cursed valley (Ch. 27) and fiery prisons—Elohim’s creation holds both judgment for the wicked and overflowing blessing for the elect. The tree of life’s promise (guarded now, accessible later) points to ultimate restoration: Yahuah’s visitation in goodness brings healing, longevity, and joy to the humble/righteous in His holy place. This vision encourages pursuit of righteousness—fragrance in bones signifies deep, abiding life from Elohim (John 10:10; Romans 8:11). Let it inspire hope: judgment separates, but renewal reunites the faithful with Yahuah’s presence (Hebrews 12:22–24). Test all things: does a path lead toward this fragrant paradise or toward desolation? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Fragrant Trees of Paradise

verses.text: And from thence I proceeded to another place in the east of the earth.
And I saw there sweet-smelling trees, and trees of the mastic, and myrrh, and trees whose fragrance was beyond all fragrance.
And the trees of the mastic exuded gum like the almond, and the myrrh trees exuded myrrh like the bark of the almond.
And beyond these trees I proceeded to the east, and I saw another place, a valley full of water.
And there was a tree which had fragrance such as the mastic tree, and its fruit was like the clusters of the vine, very beautiful; and the fragrance of that tree penetrated far beyond the valley.
And I said: ‘This fragrant tree is beautiful, and its fruit is beautiful to behold.’

Then answered Michael, one of the holy and honoured angels who was with me, and said unto me: ‘Enoch, why dost thou ask me regarding the fragrance of this tree and why dost thou wish to learn the truth?’
And I answered him saying: ‘I wish to know about everything, but especially about this tree.’

And he answered saying: ’This high mountain which thou hast seen, whose summit is like the throne of Yahuah (God), is His throne, where the Holy Great One, Yahuah (God) of Glory, the Eternal King, will sit, when He shall come down to visit the earth with goodness.

And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when His righteousness and His majesty shall be avenged on the sinners in its fruit to the righteous and humble.
To the righteous it shall be given for food, and its fruit shall be for life to the elect; it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (God), the Eternal King.

Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, and into the holy place shall they enter; and its fragrance shall be in their bones, and they shall live a long life on earth, such as thy fathers lived: and in their days shall no sorrow or plague or torment or calamity touch them.’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 29 deepens the eastward paradise depiction, cataloging additional fragrant trees—frankincense (resin), myrrh (gum), aloe (bitter-sweet aroma), and others—whose scents surpass all earthly fragrance. These trees grow in a watered valley, their beauty and perfume symbolizing the overflowing purity, healing, and divine pleasure of the renewed earth. The vision reinforces the theme of guarded abundance: the central tree of life (repeated from prior chapters) remains inaccessible until the great judgment, after which its fruit sustains the righteous/elect with eternal life, joy, and freedom from affliction when transplanted to Yahuah’s temple. - Verses 1–5: Eastward continuation; sweet-smelling trees, mastic (almond-like gum), myrrh (exuding bark), valley of water with vine-cluster tree whose penetrating fragrance fills far beyond. - Cross-refs: Song of Solomon 4:13–15 (paradise of pomegranates… henna with spikenard, spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon… fountain of gardens… flowing streams from Lebanon); Exodus 30:23–25 (fragrant spices for holy anointing oil—myrrh, cinnamon, calamus, cassia); Revelation 22:1–2 (river of water of life… tree of life on either side—life-giving fragrance implied). - Verses 6–12: Enoch’s admiration; Michael’s explanation reiterates the throne-mountain as Yahuah’s seat for visitation in goodness; tree of life untouchable until judgment—then fruit for righteous/elect, transplanted to temple, bringing joy, holy entry, fragrance in bones, long life without sorrow/plague/torment/calamity. - Cross-refs: Revelation 22:14 (blessed are those who wash their robes… right to tree of life and enter by gates into city); Isaiah 35:10 (ransomed of Yahuah (God) return… everlasting joy upon their heads… sorrow and sighing flee away); Ezekiel 47:12 (trees by river… leaves not fade… fruit not fail… leaves for healing); Psalm 133:2 (precious ointment upon head… runs down beard… dew of Hermon—fragrance imagery); Revelation 21:3–4 (Elohim’s tabernacle with men… no more death, sorrow, crying, pain). Key Insight for Discernment: The paradise of fragrance and life contrasts every form of desolation seen earlier (fiery prisons, cursed valley)—Elohim’s restored creation overflows with beauty, healing, and divine presence for the righteous. The guarded tree of life promises access only after judgment: humility and righteousness open the way to eternal sustenance and joy in Yahuah’s holy place. This vision fuels hope—affliction ends, long life returns, fragrance permeates the faithful (symbolizing deep inner renewal). It calls us to pursue the path that leads here: obedience, humility, and trust in Yahuah’s visitation (James 4:10; 1 Peter 5:6). Test all things: does a doctrine or way carry the fragrance of life or the stench of corruption? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: More Fragrant Trees in the Paradise Valley

verses.text: And beyond these, I proceeded to the east, and I saw other mountains, and trees out of which flowed the resin called styrax and the gum called galbanum, and onycha, and the trees which produce stacte, and the balsam tree.
And beyond these mountains I saw another mountain, and the trees of that mountain were like the almond tree, and their fragrance was sweet and strong.
And when I smelled the fragrance of those trees, I was amazed, and I said: ‘What is the fragrance of these trees?’
And the angel who was with me answered and said unto me: ‘These are the trees whose fragrance ascends to Yahuah (God), and their scent is acceptable before Him.’

And I saw another tree in the midst of them, whose fragrance was more excellent than all the others, and its leaves and its flowers were like the flowers of the vine, and its fruit was like clusters of grapes.
And I said: ‘This tree is beautiful beyond all trees, and its fragrance surpasses all fragrance.’

Then answered the angel who was with me, and said unto me: ‘This is the tree of wisdom, of which thy father old (in years) and thy aged mother, who were before thee, have eaten, and they learnt wisdom, and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked, and they were driven out of the garden.’
And from that time forward no one has been permitted to touch it until the great judgment, when His righteousness shall be avenged upon the sinners, and its fruit given to the righteous and humble.
Then shall it be given to the righteous and humble, and its fruit shall be for life to the elect; it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (God), the Eternal King.

Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, and into the holy place shall they enter; and its fragrance shall be in their bones, and they shall live a long life on earth, such as thy fathers lived: and in their days shall no sorrow or plague or torment or calamity touch them.’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 30 further enriches the paradise imagery with specific aromatic resins and trees—storax (styrax), galbanum, onycha (a mollusk-derived incense ingredient), stacte (sweet myrrh), balsam, and almond-like trees—whose scents rise acceptably to Yahuah (God). The central tree is explicitly identified as the tree of wisdom (from Eden), whose fruit opened Adam and Eve’s eyes but led to expulsion. It remains guarded until the great judgment, when its fruit will again be given to the righteous and humble for life, joy, and healing, transplanted to Yahuah’s temple in the renewed holy place. - Verses 1–4: Eastward mountains with storax, galbanum, onycha, stacte, balsam; their fragrance ascends to Yahuah (God) and is acceptable. - Cross-refs: Exodus 30:34–38 (Yahuah’s incense recipe: stacte, onycha, galbanum, pure frankincense—sweet aroma); Leviticus 2:1–2 (frankincense on grain offering… memorial portion… sweet aroma to Yahuah (God)); Psalm 141:2 (let my prayer be set before You as incense). - Verses 5–10: Central tree of wisdom—vine-like flowers, grape clusters; fragrance supreme; guarded until judgment—then fruit for righteous/elect, transplanted to temple; joy, holy entry, fragrance in bones, long life without sorrow/plague/torment/calamity. - Cross-refs: Genesis 2:17; 3:6–7, 22–24 (tree of knowledge of good and evil… eyes opened… knew they were naked… lest he take also of tree of life); Proverbs 3:18 (wisdom is a tree of life to those who lay hold of her); Revelation 22:2, 14 (tree of life… leaves for healing… right to tree of life); Isaiah 35:10 (ransomed return… everlasting joy… sorrow and sighing flee); Ezekiel 47:12 (trees… fruit not fail… leaves for healing). Key Insight for Discernment: The tree of wisdom—source of the fall—is redeemed in the end: guarded now, but its fruit will restore life and insight to the righteous after judgment. The fragrant resins ascending to Yahuah (God) symbolize acceptable worship and purity in the renewed creation. This vision transforms Eden’s loss into future gain—the humble/elect inherit what was forfeited, with joy, longevity, and divine presence in the holy place. It highlights Yahuah’s redemptive plan: sin brings separation, but faithfulness brings restoration (Romans 5:17–21). Let this encourage pursuit of wisdom from above—true wisdom leads to life in Yahuah’s presence (James 3:17; Proverbs 8:35). Test all things: does a teaching restore to this fragrant paradise or perpetuate the fall? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Tree of Knowledge in the Eastern Paradise

verses.text: And I proceeded to another place, and I saw a tree whose fragrance was like the fragrance of the mastic tree.
And its leaves were like the leaves of the vine, and its fruit was like the clusters of the vine, very beautiful; and the fragrance of that tree penetrated far beyond the valley.
And I said: ‘This tree is beautiful beyond all trees, and its fragrance surpasses all fragrance.’

Then answered the angel who was with me, and said unto me: ‘This is the tree of wisdom, of which thy father old (in years) and thy aged mother, who were before thee, have eaten, and they learnt wisdom, and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked, and they were driven out of the garden.’
And from that time forward no one has been permitted to touch it until the great judgement, when His righteousness shall be avenged upon the sinners, and its fruit given to the righteous and humble.
Then shall it be given to the righteous and humble, and its fruit shall be for life to the elect; it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (God), the Eternal King.

Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, and into the holy place shall they enter; and its fragrance shall be in their bones, and they shall live a long life on earth, such as thy fathers lived: and in their days shall no sorrow or plague or torment or calamity touch them.’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 31 explicitly identifies the central fragrant tree as the tree of knowledge of good and evil from Eden—the one Adam and Eve ate from, gaining wisdom but also shame, nakedness, and expulsion. Its beauty and penetrating fragrance remain, yet it is strictly guarded until the great judgment. After judgment, its fruit is restored to the righteous and humble, granting life, wisdom, joy, and long, affliction-free existence when transplanted to Yahuah’s temple in the holy place. This completes the Eden-redemption arc: what caused the fall becomes a source of blessing in the end for the faithful. - Verses 1–4: Beautiful tree with mastic-like fragrance, vine-like leaves/fruit; angel identifies it as the tree of wisdom eaten by Adam and Eve—leading to opened eyes, knowledge of nakedness, and expulsion from the garden. - Cross-refs: Genesis 2:17; 3:6–7, 22–24 (tree of knowledge… ate… eyes opened… knew they were naked… driven out… lest he take also of tree of life); Proverbs 3:13–18 (happy is the man who finds wisdom… she is a tree of life to those who lay hold of her). - Verses 5–7: Guarded until great judgment—then fruit given to righteous/humble/elect for life; transplanted to temple of Yahuah (God); joy, entry to holy place, fragrance in bones, long life without sorrow/plague/torment/calamity. - Cross-refs: Revelation 22:2, 14 (tree of life… leaves for healing… right to tree of life and enter city); Isaiah 35:10 (ransomed return with everlasting joy… sorrow and sighing flee); Ezekiel 47:12 (trees by river… leaves not fade… fruit not fail); Revelation 21:3–4 (Elohim (God) dwells with men… no more death, sorrow, crying, pain); Psalm 133:2 (precious ointment… runs down… fragrance of unity and blessing). Key Insight for Discernment: The tree of knowledge—source of humanity’s fall and expulsion—is redeemed in the eschaton: guarded now to prevent premature access, but its fruit will restore wisdom and life to the righteous after judgment. This shows Yahuah’s redemptive sovereignty—what was lost through disobedience is restored through faithfulness. The promise of fragrance in bones, long life, and no calamity points to deep inner renewal and Edenic reversal in the holy place. It calls us to humility and righteousness—the elect inherit what was forfeited (Romans 5:17–19). Let this transform how we view “forbidden” knowledge: true wisdom comes from Yahuah (God) in His timing (James 1:5; Proverbs 2:6). Test all things: does a path echo Eden’s restoration or repeat the fall? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Garden of Righteousness and the Two Trees

verses.text: And after these fragrant odours, as I looked toward the north over the mountains, I saw seven mountains full of choice nard, and fragrant trees, and cinnamon, and pepper.
And thence I went over the summits of all these mountains, far towards the east of the earth, and passed above the Erythraean sea, and went far from it, and passed over the angel Zataêl.
And I went to the garden of righteousness, and saw beyond those trees many other large ones, trees of fragrance, trees of myrrh, trees of aloes, and trees whose fragrance was beyond all fragrance.

And the tree of life was in the midst of the garden, and its fragrance was sweeter than all fragrance, and its leaves and its flowers and its wood wither not for ever, and its fruit is beautiful, and its fruit is like clusters of the vine, very beautiful.
And I said: ‘Behold this beautiful tree, and what is its name?’

Then answered the angel who was with me, and said unto me: ‘This is the tree of wisdom, of which thy father old (in years) and thy aged mother, who were before thee, have eaten, and they learnt wisdom, and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked, and they were driven out of the garden.’
And from that time forward no one has been permitted to touch it until the great judgement, when His righteousness shall be avenged upon the sinners, and its fruit given to the righteous and humble.
Then shall it be given to the righteous and humble, and its fruit shall be for life to the elect; it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (God), the Eternal King.

Then shall they rejoice with joy and be glad, and into the holy place shall they enter; and its fragrance shall be in their bones, and they shall live a long life on earth, such as thy fathers lived: and in their days shall no sorrow or plague or torment or calamity touch them.’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 32 brings the eastward journey to its climax in the “garden of righteousness”—a visionary restoration of Eden, filled with choice spices (nard, cinnamon, pepper), myrrh, aloes, and surpassing fragrance. The tree of life stands central, eternally unfading, with beautiful vine-like fruit. The angel reaffirms its identity as the tree of wisdom/knowledge (from Genesis 3), eaten by Adam and Eve, leading to their expulsion. It remains inaccessible until the great judgment, when its fruit is granted to the righteous/humble/elect for life, transplanted to Yahuah’s temple in the holy place—bringing joy, holy entry, inner fragrance/healing (“in their bones”), long life, and complete freedom from sorrow, plague, torment, or calamity. - Verses 1–3: Northern mountains with nard, cinnamon, pepper; garden of righteousness beyond, with myrrh, aloes, and trees of overwhelming fragrance. - Cross-refs: Song of Solomon 4:13–14 (paradise… spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon… aloes… all chief spices); Genesis 2:8–9 (garden eastward in Eden… tree of life and tree of knowledge in midst); Revelation 22:2 (tree of life in midst of street… on either side of river). - Verses 4–9: Tree of life central, sweet fragrance, unfading, beautiful fruit; angel explains it as tree of wisdom—eaten by parents, leading to knowledge/nakedness/expulsion; guarded until judgment—then fruit for righteous/elect, transplanted to temple; joy, entry to holy place, fragrance in bones, long life without affliction. - Cross-refs: Genesis 3:6–7, 22–24 (ate… eyes opened… knew naked… driven out… cherubim guard way to tree of life); Revelation 2:7 (to him who overcomes… eat from tree of life in paradise of Elohim (God)); Revelation 22:14 (blessed who wash robes… right to tree of life); Isaiah 65:20–23 (no more infant of days… elect enjoy work of hands… no sorrow); Ezekiel 47:12 (trees… leaves not fade… fruit not fail… healing); Revelation 21:4 (no more death, sorrow, crying, pain). Key Insight for Discernment: The garden of righteousness reunites the two Eden trees—life and wisdom—once separated by the fall, now preserved for full restoration. The guarded tree symbolizes Yahuah’s mercy in withholding premature access to prevent further corruption, yet His promise opens it to the righteous after judgment. Fragrance in bones signifies deep, permeating renewal—body, soul, spirit healed in His presence. This vision closes the paradise sequence with hope: the fall is reversed, Eden reclaimed for the elect in Yahuah’s holy place. It calls us to humility and righteousness—the humble inherit life eternal (James 4:10; 1 Peter 5:6). Test all things: does a path restore to this garden of fragrance and life, or repeat Eden’s loss? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Ends of the Earth and the Portals of the Luminaries

verses.text: And from thence I proceeded to the ends of the earth, and saw there great beasts, and birds different from one another, and of various kinds, and beauty.
And to the east of those beasts I saw the ends of the earth whereon the heaven rests, and the portals of the heaven open.

And I saw six portals out of which the sun rises, and six portals in which the sun sets, and the moon rises and sets in those portals, and the leaders of the stars and those whom they lead: six in the east and six in the west following them, and also many other chariots and their leaders.
And the greatness of them all is as the greatness of the sun, and their chariots are like the chariots of the sun.
And all the stars rise and set in their own order, and they do not change their course.
And I saw the four winds which support the earth and the firmament of the heaven.
And I saw the winds which turn the heaven, and cause the disc of the sun and all the stars to set.
And I saw the winds on the earth carrying the clouds: I saw the paths of the angels.
And I saw at the end of the earth the firmament of the heaven above.
And I proceeded to the north, and I saw there the great mountains of precious stones, and the trees of paradise, and the fragrant trees.
