And I saw the treasuries of the snow and the treasuries of the hail, and the treasuries of the clouds, and the treasuries of the dew and the rain.
And I saw the treasuries of all the winds: I saw how He has ordered all creation by His wisdom, and how He has founded the world upon them.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 33 shifts from paradise to the structural edges of creation: the “ends of the earth” with diverse beasts and birds, the six eastern rising and six western setting portals for sun, moon, and stars (each led by appointed guides/chariots), the four winds supporting earth and heaven, and treasuries of snow, hail, clouds, dew, rain, and winds. Everything operates under fixed laws—no deviation—testifying to Yahuah’s perfect wisdom and foundation of the world. This echoes earlier nature-obedience themes (Ch. 2–5, 23) and contrasts the rebellious (Watchers, transgressing stars) who abandoned their courses. - Verses 1–5: Ends of earth with varied beasts/birds; six portals east/west for sun/moon/stars; chariots/leaders; all maintain order without change. - Cross-refs: Genesis 1:14–18 (lights for signs/seasons/days/years… to rule day/night); Psalm 104:19 (appointed moon for seasons; sun knows its going down); Jeremiah 31:35 (ordinances of moon/stars do not fail); Job 38:31–33 (bind Pleiades… loose Orion… ordinances of heavens?). - Verses 6–9: Four winds supporting earth/firmament; winds turning heaven/sun/stars; carrying clouds; paths of angels at earth’s end/firmament above. - Cross-refs: Job 26:7–11 (hangs earth on nothing… pillars of heaven tremble); Psalm 148:8 (stormy wind fulfilling His word); Isaiah 40:22 (stretches heavens like curtain… circle of earth); Zechariah 6:5 (four spirits/winds of heaven going out from standing before Yahuah (God)). - Verses 10–12: Northern mountains with paradise trees; treasuries of snow/hail/clouds/dew/rain/winds; all ordered by Yahuah’s wisdom, world founded upon them. - Cross-refs: Job 38:22–23 (treasuries of snow/hail reserved for time of trouble); Psalm 135:7 (makes clouds rise… brings wind from treasuries); Jeremiah 10:12–13 (made earth by power… established world by wisdom… brings wind from treasuries); Proverbs 3:19–20 (Yahuah (God) founded earth by wisdom… heavens established by understanding). Key Insight for Discernment: The ends of the earth reveal Yahuah’s meticulous design—portals, winds, treasuries, luminaries all obey fixed laws, glorifying the Creator. No chaos here; everything serves its appointed purpose. This contrasts sharply with the fallen who transgressed their orders (leading to binding). The vision calls us to emulate creation’s faithfulness: keep our place, fulfill our role in Yahuah’s order. Let the unchanging courses inspire trust in His sovereignty—He who orders the cosmos orders our lives too (Psalm 119:89–91; Colossians 1:16–17). Test all things: does a path align with Elohim’s appointed laws or invite disorder? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Four Quarters of the Earth and Their Portals

verses.text: And from thence I went to the north, to the ends of the earth, and there I saw three portals of the heaven open: through each of them proceed north winds: when they blow there is dew and rain and hoar-frost.

And from thence I went to the east, to the ends of the earth, and saw there three portals of the heaven open: through each of them proceed east winds: when they blow there is dew and rain and hoar-frost.

And from thence I went to the south, to the ends of the earth, and saw there three portals of the heaven open: through each of them proceed south winds: when they blow there is dew and rain and hoar-frost.

And from thence I went to the west, to the ends of the earth, and saw there three portals of the heaven open: through each of them proceed west winds: when they blow there is dew and rain and hoar-frost.
And I saw the mountains of the earth, and the rivers that go forth from them, and the valleys that receive them.
And I saw the four quarters of the earth, and the winds which divide the earth into four parts.
And I saw the winds which support the earth and the firmament of the heaven.
And I saw how the winds stretch out the vaults of heaven, and have their station between heaven and earth: these are the pillars of the heaven.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 34 systematically explores the four cardinal directions (north, east, south, west), each with three heavenly portals through which winds blow, bringing dew, rain, and hoar-frost—regulating climate and seasons. The chapter also notes mountains, rivers flowing from them into valleys, and the four winds that divide the earth into quarters while supporting its structure and the heavenly firmament as pillars. This vision underscores Yahuah’s precise division and sustenance of creation: portals and winds ensure balance, no chaos, all under divine wisdom—echoing the unchanging order of the luminaries (Ch. 33) and contrasting the rebellion that disrupts such harmony. - Verses 1–4: Three portals per direction (north, east, south, west) for winds carrying dew/rain/hoar-frost; symmetric regulation across quarters. - Cross-refs: Zechariah 6:5 (four spirits of heaven… go forth from standing before Yahuah (God)); Psalm 135:7 (He brings wind out of His treasuries… makes clouds rise from ends of earth); Jeremiah 10:13 (He makes clouds rise from ends of earth… brings wind from treasuries); Job 37:9–10 (from the south comes whirlwind… from north cold… breath of Elohim (God) gives ice). - Verses 5–8: Mountains/rivers/valleys; four winds dividing earth; supporting earth/firmament as pillars stretching vaults of heaven. - Cross-refs: Job 26:7–11 (hangs earth on nothing… pillars of heaven tremble); Psalm 104:5–9 (set earth on foundations… mountains up, valleys down); Isaiah 40:12 (measured waters… marked off heavens); Proverbs 8:27–29 (set compass on face of deep… appointed foundations of earth). Key Insight for Discernment: The four quarters and portals reveal Yahuah’s intentional symmetry—winds from every direction sustain life (dew/rain) and structure (pillars/firmament), preventing collapse or imbalance. This testifies to Elohim’s wisdom in bounding and dividing creation (Genesis 1:6–8). It warns against transgressing boundaries, as the fallen did, while encouraging trust in His provision. Let the winds and portals remind us: Yahuah’s order is for blessing—rain for growth, winds for stability (Psalm 147:8–9). Test all things: does a path respect Yahuah’s divisions or seek to blur them? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Western Quarter and Its Portals

verses.text: And from thence I proceeded to the west of the ends of the earth, and saw there three portals of the heaven open such as I had seen in the east, but small, and three portals to the north, small likewise.
And the portals of the west are small, and through them proceed the west winds: when they blow there is dew and rain and hoar-frost.
And from thence I went to the ends of the earth in the west, and saw there great mountains and high hills, and deep valleys.
And there I saw rivers coming forth from those mountains, and flowing into the valleys below.
And I saw the four quarters of the earth, and the winds which divide the earth into four parts.
And I saw the winds which support the earth and the firmament of the heaven.
And I saw how the winds stretch out the vaults of heaven, and have their station between heaven and earth: these are the pillars of the heaven.
And I saw the portals of the heaven open in the west, and through them proceed the winds which bring dew and rain and hoar-frost.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 35 details the western quarter, mirroring the symmetry of the other directions (Ch. 34): three small portals open for west winds that bring dew, rain, and hoar-frost, maintaining seasonal balance. The region features great mountains, high hills, deep valleys, and rivers flowing from the heights into the lowlands—illustrating how Yahuah’s design channels water for life and fertility. The four winds continue to divide the earth into quarters while supporting its structure and the heavenly firmament as pillars. This reinforces the theme of creation’s perfect division and sustenance: boundaries prevent chaos, winds and portals ensure provision, all ordered by Yahuah’s wisdom. - Verses 1–2, 8: Three western portals (small, like northern ones) for west winds carrying dew/rain/hoar-frost. - Cross-refs: Psalm 135:7 (He causes vapors to ascend… brings wind from His treasuries); Job 37:17 (how your garments are hot when He quiets the earth by the south wind); Ecclesiastes 11:3 (if the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves on the earth). - Verses 3–4: Great mountains, high hills, deep valleys; rivers flowing from mountains into valleys. - Cross-refs: Psalm 104:8–10 (mountains rose, valleys sank… springs break forth in valleys); Isaiah 41:18 (open rivers on bare heights… fountains in valleys); Ezekiel 47:1–8 (water flowing from temple… deepening river bringing life). - Verses 5–7: Four winds dividing earth into quarters; supporting earth/firmament as pillars stretching vaults. - Cross-refs: Job 26:7–11 (hangs earth on nothing… pillars of heaven tremble); Zechariah 6:5 (four spirits/winds going forth from Yahuah (God)); Psalm 148:8 (stormy wind fulfilling His word). Key Insight for Discernment: The western quarter’s portals, mountains, valleys, and rivers show Yahuah’s balanced provision—winds bring moisture, heights channel water to lows, sustaining life across creation. This symmetry across quarters (east, west, north, south) testifies to Elohim’s intentional design: no part is neglected, all serves the whole. It contrasts sharply with the disorder introduced by rebellion (Watchers transgressing boundaries). The vision encourages trust in Yahuah’s order—He who divides the earth and sends rain for blessing will provide for the faithful (Matthew 5:45; Psalm 147:8–9). Test all things: does a path respect Yahuah’s boundaries and divisions, or seek to disrupt His wise order? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Southern Quarter and the Harmony of the Four Quarters

verses.text: And from thence I proceeded to the south, to the ends of the earth, and saw there three portals of the heaven open: through each of them proceed south winds: when they blow there is dew and rain and hoar-frost.
And there I saw great mountains and high hills, and deep valleys, and rivers flowing from the mountains into the valleys.
And I saw the four quarters of the earth, and the winds which divide the earth into four parts.
And I saw the winds which support the earth and the firmament of the heaven.
And I saw how the winds stretch out the vaults of heaven, and have their station between heaven and earth: these are the pillars of the heaven.
And I saw the portals of the heaven open in the south, and through them proceed the winds which bring dew and rain and hoar-frost.
And I saw the mountains of the earth, and the rivers that go forth from them, and the valleys that receive them.
And I saw the four winds which support the earth and the firmament of the heaven.
And I saw how Yahuah (God) has ordered all creation by His wisdom, and how He has founded the world upon them.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 36 completes the survey of the earth’s four quarters by detailing the southern direction: three open portals for south winds bringing dew, rain, and hoar-frost—mirroring the symmetry of the other quarters (Ch. 34–35). The south features great mountains, high hills, deep valleys, and rivers flowing from heights to lows, illustrating how Yahuah (God) channels water for life and fertility across creation. The four winds divide the earth into quarters, support its structure and heavenly firmament as pillars stretching the vaults, and are ordered by Yahuah’s wisdom, founding the world upon them. This final directional vision emphasizes complete harmony: boundaries, portals, winds, mountains, rivers, and valleys all function in perfect balance under Elohim’s sovereign design—no part neglected, no chaos allowed. - Verses 1, 6: Three southern portals for south winds carrying dew/rain/hoar-frost. - Cross-refs: Job 37:17 (garments hot when He quiets earth by south wind); Psalm 147:8 (covers heavens with clouds… prepares rain for earth); Jeremiah 5:24 (fear Yahuah (God)… gives rain early and latter in season). - Verses 2–3, 7: Great mountains/hills, deep valleys, rivers flowing from mountains into valleys. - Cross-refs: Psalm 104:8–10 (mountains rose, valleys sank… springs break forth in valleys); Isaiah 41:18 (open rivers on bare heights… fountains in valleys); Ezekiel 47:1–8 (water from temple… deepening river bringing life). - Verses 4–5, 8–9: Four winds dividing/supporting earth/firmament as pillars; Yahuah (God) orders creation by wisdom, founds world upon them. - Cross-refs: Job 26:7–11 (hangs earth on nothing… pillars of heaven tremble); Zechariah 6:5 (four spirits/winds from before Yahuah (God)); Proverbs 3:19–20 (Yahuah (God) founded earth by wisdom… established heavens by understanding); Psalm 148:8 (stormy wind fulfilling His word). Key Insight for Discernment: The southern quarter completes the perfect circle of creation—every direction, portal, wind, mountain, river, and valley serves Yahuah’s balanced purpose, sustaining life and glorifying the Creator. This symmetry across all quarters testifies to Elohim’s meticulous wisdom: He divides to unite, bounds to bless. It stands in absolute contrast to the disorder of rebellion (Watchers transgressing boundaries). The vision calls us to live within Yahuah’s appointed order—let the winds from every quarter remind us: He provides, sustains, and judges with perfect equity (Matthew 5:45; Psalm 147:8–9). Test all things: does a path fit within Yahuah’s wise divisions and bring life, or transgress and bring chaos? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Second Vision – Parables of the Righteous and the Elect

verses.text: The second vision which he saw, the vision of wisdom—which Enoch the son of Yered, the son of Mahalalel, the son of Kenan, the son of Enosh, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, saw.
And this is the beginning of the words of wisdom which I lifted up my voice to speak and say to those who dwell on the dry ground: Hear, you men of old time, and see, you that come after!
The words of the Holy One in the vision which I saw, and the words of the Holy Great One, and the vision of the Holy One and of heaven which I saw.
And I heard everything, and from them I understood as I saw, but not for this generation, but for a remote one which is for to come.
Concerning the elect I said, and took up my parable concerning them: The Holy Great One will come forth from His dwelling,
And the eternal Elohim (God) will tread upon the earth, (even) on Mount Sinai, [And appear from His camp] And appear in the strength of His might from the heaven of heavens.
And all shall be smitten with fear And the Watchers shall quake, And great fear and trembling shall seize them unto the ends of the earth.
And the high mountains shall be shaken, And the high hills shall be made low, And shall melt like wax before the flame
And the earth shall be wholly rent in sunder, And all that is upon the earth shall perish, And there shall be a judgement upon all (men).

But with the righteous He will make peace. And will protect the elect, And mercy shall be upon them. And they shall all belong to Elohim (God), And they shall be prospered, And they shall all be blessed. And He will help them all, And light shall appear unto them, And He will make peace with them.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 37 serves as the superscription and introduction to the Book of Parables (Ch. 37–71), a distinct section of 1 Enoch focused on eschatological parables, the hidden wisdom of heaven, and the revelation of the “Elect One” / “Son of Man.” Enoch, tracing his genealogy back to Adam, declares these words of wisdom not for his own generation but for a future, remote one (eschatological audience). He lifts his voice to the “men of old time” and those who come after, proclaiming the coming forth of the Holy Great One (Yahuah (God)) in might from His dwelling, treading on earth (Sinai imagery), causing cosmic upheaval, fear among Watchers and all flesh, and universal judgment. Yet for the righteous and elect, He brings peace, protection, mercy, prosperity, blessing, light, and covenant shalom. - Verses 1–4: Second vision of wisdom; genealogy to Adam; words for future generation; understanding from heavenly visions. - Cross-refs: Genesis 5:1–24 (genealogy of Enoch); Hebrews 11:5 (by faith Enoch was translated… pleased Elohim (God)); Daniel 12:4, 9 (seal the book until the time of the end… words closed up and sealed till the time of the end). - Verses 5–10: Parable concerning the elect; Yahuah (God) comes forth from dwelling, treads earth (Sinai), appears in might; cosmic terror (Watchers quake, mountains shake/melt, earth rends, judgment on all); peace, protection, mercy, blessing, light, and peace for righteous/elect. - Cross-refs: Deuteronomy 33:2 (Yahuah (God) came from Sinai… ten thousands of set-apart ones); Habakkuk 3:3–6 (Elohim (God) came from Teman… mountains shook); Micah 1:3–4 (Yahuah (God) comes forth from His place… mountains melt); Isaiah 24:19–20 (earth broken… reels like drunkard); Jude 1:14–15 (Enoch prophesied: Yahuah (God) comes with ten thousands… execute judgment); Psalm 37:11 (meek inherit earth… delight in abundant peace); Romans 5:1 (peace with Elohim (God) through our Master Yahusha (Jesus) Messiah); Isaiah 57:19 (peace to far and near). Key Insight for Discernment: This introduction pivots from the Watchers narrative to messianic/eschatological parables. The vision is for a future generation facing tribulation—promising Yahuah’s direct intervention: judgment on the wicked (cosmic upheaval) but shalom for the elect. The repetition of peace/mercy/light for the righteous underscores hope amid judgment. It aligns with canonical prophecy (Sinai theophany, Day of Yahuah (God)) and points forward to the “Son of Man” revelations ahead. Let this encourage endurance: the remote generation is us—hold fast, for Yahuah (God) comes to judge and redeem (Hebrews 10:37; James 5:7–8). Test all things: does a teaching prepare for this visitation in goodness or ignore the coming judgment? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The First Parable – Judgment on Sinners and Revelation of the Elect One

verses.text: The first parable which Enoch spoke concerning the righteous and the elect, when the sun rises and the light appears on the earth:

And the righteous shall be victorious in the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits, and He will cause the sinners and the godless to be destroyed from the face of the earth, and those who have led the world astray shall be bound with chains, and in their assemblage-place of destruction shall they be imprisoned, and all their works shall vanish from the face of the earth.
And from henceforth there shall be nothing that is destroyed, for the Elect One shall appear before Him, and all the deeds of the sinners shall be revealed before Him.

And from henceforth they that possess the earth shall no longer be strong and exalted, nor shall they be able to look with contempt on the face of the holy, for Yahuah (God) of Spirits has appeared upon the throne of His glory, and all evil shall depart before His face.
And the word of the mouth of the Holy One shall be powerful in the mouth of the righteous, and the word of the mouth of the sinners shall be powerless.
And in those days the kings and the mighty who possess the earth shall be cast down from their thrones, and they shall be cast into the furnace of fire, and their faces shall be covered with shame.

And the Yahuah (God) of Spirits shall cause them to be cast down into the furnace of fire, and they shall be cast into the furnace of fire, and their faces shall be covered with shame, and they shall be cast into the furnace of fire.

And in those days the righteous shall be victorious, and the light of the righteous shall shine, and the sinners shall be cast into darkness, and the righteous shall be victorious in the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits.
And the sinners shall cry out and lament, and they shall not find mercy, and their spirits shall be cast into the furnace of fire.

And in those days the Elect One shall sit on the throne of glory, and shall judge the secret things, and no one shall be able to utter a lying word before Him; for the Yahuah (God) of Spirits has appointed Him, and He has revealed all the hidden things.
And the Yahuah (God) of Spirits has revealed to the righteous and elect the secrets of wisdom, and they shall be victorious, and they shall not be ashamed, and they shall not be confounded.
And the sinners shall be driven from the face of the earth, and they shall be bound with chains, and their works shall be destroyed, and they shall be cast into the furnace of fire.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 38 opens the First Parable (Ch. 38–44), focusing on eschatological judgment and the triumph of the righteous. Enoch prophesies the rising of light for the elect, the destruction of sinners and the godless from the earth, the binding of those who led astray, and the appearance of the Elect One before Yahuah (God) of Spirits. Kings and mighty oppressors face humiliation and the furnace of fire; the righteous shine, speak powerfully, and inherit victory in Yahuah’s name. The Elect One sits on the throne of glory, judges secrets, and no lie can stand before Him—Yahuah (God) has appointed and revealed hidden wisdom to the righteous/elect, ensuring their ultimate vindication. - Verses 1–5: Parable for righteous/elect; sun/light rising symbolizes victory; sinners/godless destroyed, bound, works vanish; Elect One appears, deeds revealed. - Cross-refs: Malachi 4:1–2 (day comes burning like oven… wicked as stubble… Sun of Righteousness arise with healing); Psalm 37:9–11 (evildoers cut off… meek inherit earth); Isaiah 11:4 (judge with righteousness… smite earth with rod of mouth); Jude 1:14–15 (Yahuah (God) comes… convict ungodly); Revelation 19:11–16 (Faithful and True judges… smites nations). - Verses 6–9: Kings/mighty cast from thrones into fire, faces covered with shame; righteous victorious, light shines, sinners in darkness, cry without mercy. - Cross-refs: Isaiah 2:10–17 (hide in dust… lofty looks of man humbled… day of Yahuah (God)); Revelation 6:15–17 (kings, great men hide from face of Him on throne… wrath of Lamb); Luke 1:52 (cast down mighty from thrones… exalted humble); Psalm 9:17 (wicked turned into hell… nations forget Elohim (God)). - Verses 10–12: Elect One on throne of glory, judges secrets, no lying word; hidden wisdom revealed to righteous/elect; sinners driven off, bound, works destroyed, cast into fire. - Cross-refs: Daniel 7:13–14 (Son of Man… given dominion… everlasting kingdom); Matthew 25:31–32 (Son of Man on throne of glory… separates sheep/goats); Revelation 20:11–12 (great white throne… books opened… judged by works); Psalm 96:13 (He comes to judge earth… judge world in righteousness); 1 Corinthians 4:5 (Lord comes… bring hidden things to light). Key Insight for Discernment: The First Parable unveils the core hope of the righteous amid tribulation: Yahuah (God) of Spirits sends the Elect One (Son of Man figure) to judge, destroy evil, and vindicate the faithful. Kings/mighty fall, sinners burn, but the elect shine with revealed wisdom and eternal victory—no shame, no confounding. This is future-oriented prophecy (for the remote generation), blending Sinai theophany, Day of Yahuah (God), and messianic judgment. It calls us to live as the elect: righteous, humble, trusting in the coming revelation. Let the furnace for the wicked and light for the righteous sharpen resolve—judgment is certain, mercy for the repentant (2 Peter 3:9; Romans 2:4–11). Test all things: does a teaching align with this coming victory of the Elect One or deny it? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Dwellings of the Righteous and the Throne of Glory

verses.text: And it shall come to pass in those days that the elect and holy children of the earth will behold the secrets of the heaven, and the kingdom of the Elect One shall be revealed to them, and they shall rejoice and be glad.
And in those days the righteous shall dwell with the righteous, and the elect with the elect, and the sinners shall be driven from the face of the earth.
And I saw the dwellings of the elect and the dwellings of the holy, and my spirit longed for those dwellings.

And there mine eyes saw their dwellings with His righteous angels, and their resting-places with the holy, and they intercede and pray for the children of men, and righteousness flows before them like water, and mercy like dew upon the earth.
And in those days the voice of the Holy One shall be heard in the heaven, and the voice of the Elect One shall be heard from the throne of glory.
And in those days the elect shall dwell upon the earth, and the righteous shall dwell with them, and they shall not be separated.
And the Yahuah (God) of Spirits shall abide over them, and with them they shall eat and drink and praise the Yahuah (God) of Spirits.
And in those days the mountains shall leap like rams, and the hills shall skip like lambs, and the righteous shall be victorious in the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits.
And the light of the righteous shall shine like the light of the sun, and the sinners shall be as darkness, and they shall not be able to stand before the face of the Holy One.
And the righteous shall be victorious, and the elect shall be victorious, and they shall not be ashamed, and they shall not be confounded.
And I saw the four presences which surround the throne of glory, and they praise Yahuah (God) of Spirits, and they intercede for the children of men.
And I heard the voices of those four presences as they uttered praises before Yahuah (God) of glory.
And the first voice blesses Yahuah (God) of Spirits for ever and ever.
And the second voice I heard blessing the Elect One and the elect who hang upon Yahuah (God) of Spirits.
And the third voice I heard praying and interceding for those who dwell on the earth and supplicate in the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits.
And I heard the fourth voice fending off the Satans and forbidding them to come before Yahuah (God) of Spirits to accuse them who dwell on the earth.
After that I asked the angel of peace who went with me, saying unto me: ‘These four presences which I have seen and whose words I have heard, to whom do they belong?’

And he said unto me: ‘This first is Michael, the merciful and long-suffering: and the second, who is set over all sickness and all wounds, is Raphael: and the third, who is set over all the powers, is Gabriel: and the fourth, who is set over the repentance unto hope of those who inherit eternal life, is named Phanuel.’
And these are the four presences which surround Yahuah (God) of Spirits.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 39 deepens the First Parable with a vision of the heavenly dwellings: the righteous and elect live in harmony with holy angels, interceding for humanity; righteousness flows like water, mercy like dew. Enoch longs for these resting-places. The chapter introduces the four presences (archangels) surrounding Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ throne of glory—Michael (merciful/long-suffering), Raphael (over sickness/wounds), Gabriel (over powers), Phanuel (over repentance/hope for eternal life)—each praising, interceding, and defending. The righteous dwell on earth in victory and light, unashamed, while sinners face darkness and separation. The Lord of Spirits abides with them, sharing table fellowship and praise. - Verses 1–10: Elect behold heaven’s secrets; righteous/elect dwell together on earth; sinners driven off; dwellings with angels; intercession, righteousness/mercy flow; Yahuah’s voice from throne; mountains leap, righteous victorious/shining, sinners as darkness. - Cross-refs: Isaiah 11:6–9 (wolf with lamb… earth full of knowledge of Yahuah (God)); Isaiah 35:10 (ransomed return with joy… sorrow flees); Psalm 133:1–3 (brethren dwell in unity… dew of Hermon); Revelation 21:3–4 (Elohim (God) dwells with men… no more sorrow); Malachi 4:2 (Sun of Righteousness arise with healing); Psalm 97:11–12 (light sown for righteous… rejoice in Yahuah (God)). - Verses 11–19: Four presences around throne praise/intercede/defend; Michael (merciful), Raphael (healing), Gabriel (powers), Phanuel (repentance/hope); surround Yahuah (God) of Spirits. - Cross-refs: Revelation 4:6–8 (four living creatures around throne… cease not day/night saying Holy, holy, holy); Isaiah 6:1–3 (seraphim around throne… Holy, holy, holy); Daniel 10:13, 21 (Michael… one of chief princes); Luke 1:19 (Gabriel stands in presence of Elohim (God)); Revelation 8:2–5 (seven angels… present prayers); Tobit 12:15 (Raphael one of seven who present prayers—apocryphal parallel). Key Insight for Discernment: This vision reveals the heavenly reality: Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ throne surrounded by archangels who praise, intercede, heal, protect, and guide repentance—while the righteous dwell in unity with angels, sharing fellowship and victory. The contrast is stark—light/joy for elect, darkness/shame for sinners. Phanuel’s role in repentance/hope emphasizes mercy available now for those who turn. The chapter bridges earthly tribulation to heavenly assurance: the elect are known, protected, and destined for glory. It calls us to live as the righteous—humble, victorious in Yahuah’s name (1 Peter 5:6–10). Test all things: does a teaching reflect this heavenly fellowship and victory or deny the coming separation? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Four Presences and the Secrets of Heaven

verses.text: And after that I saw thousands of thousands and myriads of myriads, and an infinite number of people, standing before Yahuah (God) of Spirits.

And on the four sides of Yahuah (God) of Spirits I saw four presences, different from those that stand, and I learnt their names: for the angel that went with me made known to me their names, and showed me all the hidden things.
And I heard the voices of those four presences as they uttered praises before Yahuah (God) of glory.
The first voice blesses Yahuah (God) of Spirits for ever and ever.
And the second voice I heard blessing the Elect One and the elect ones who hang upon Yahuah (God) of Spirits.
And the third voice I heard praying and interceding for those who dwell on the earth and supplicate in the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits.
And I heard the fourth voice fending off the Satans and forbidding them to come before Yahuah (God) of Spirits to accuse them who dwell on the earth.

After that I asked the angel of peace who went with me, who showed me everything that is hidden, saying unto me: ‘These four presences which I have seen and whose words I have heard, to whom do they belong?’

And he said unto me: ‘This first is Michael, the merciful and long-suffering: and the second, who is set over all sickness and all wounds, is Raphael: and the third, who is set over all the powers, is Gabriel: and the fourth, who is set over the repentance unto hope of those who inherit eternal life, is named Phanuel.’
And these are the four presences which surround Yahuah (God) of Spirits.
And the voices of those upon the earth that bless Yahuah (God) of Spirits shall be heard in the heaven, and the voices of those who bless the Elect One shall be heard in the heaven.
And the voice of the righteous shall be heard in the heaven, and the voice of the sinners shall be powerless.
And in those days the secrets of the thunder and the lightning shall be revealed, and the secrets of the winds and the clouds, and the secrets of the sun and the moon and the stars shall be revealed.
And all the secrets of the ends of the earth shall be revealed, and the treasuries of the winds shall be opened, and the foundations of the earth shall be laid bare.
And the secrets of the deep shall be revealed, and the secrets of Sheol shall be laid bare.
And all the secrets of the luminaries shall be revealed, and the secrets of the stars shall be made known.
And all the secrets of the thunder and the lightning shall be revealed to the righteous and elect.
And the secrets of the winds and the clouds shall be revealed to the righteous and elect.
And the secrets of the sun and the moon and the stars shall be revealed to the righteous and elect.
And all the secrets of the ends of the earth shall be revealed to the righteous and elect.
And the treasuries of the winds shall be opened to the righteous and elect.
And the foundations of the earth shall be laid bare to the righteous and elect.
And the secrets of the deep shall be revealed to the righteous and elect.
And the secrets of Sheol shall be laid bare to the righteous and elect.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 40 expands on the four presences (archangels) surrounding Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ throne: Michael (merciful/long-suffering), Raphael (healing/sickness), Gabriel (powers), Phanuel (repentance/hope for eternal life). They ceaselessly praise, bless the Elect One and elect, intercede for earth’s dwellers, and defend against Satans’ accusations. Enoch hears the voices of the righteous ascending to heaven, while sinners’ words are powerless. The chapter then reveals that hidden cosmic secrets—thunder/lightning, winds/clouds, sun/moon/stars, earth’s ends, treasuries of winds, foundations, deep, Sheol—are unveiled to the righteous and elect, preparing them for the final judgment and triumph. - Verses 1–10: Innumerable host before Yahuah (God); four presences praise/intercede/defend; named Michael, Raphael, Gabriel, Phanuel—surrounding the throne. - Cross-refs: Revelation 5:11–12 (myriads of angels around throne… saying with loud voice: Worthy is the Lamb); Revelation 8:3–4 (angel with censer offers prayers of saints); Daniel 7:10 (thousand thousands ministered… ten thousand times ten thousand stood before Him); Isaiah 6:2–3 (seraphim around throne… Holy, holy, holy); Luke 1:19 (Gabriel stands in presence of Elohim (God)). - Verses 11–24: Voices of righteous heard in heaven; sinners powerless; secrets of thunder/lightning/winds/clouds/sun/moon/stars/ends of earth/treasuries/foundations/deep/Sheol revealed to righteous/elect. - Cross-refs: Job 38:4–38 (foundations of earth… treasuries of snow/hail… ordinances of heavens… secrets of deep); Psalm 19:1–4 (heavens declare glory of Elohim (God)… no speech nor language… voice not heard); Daniel 2:22 (He reveals deep and secret things); Amos 3:7 (Yahuah (God) reveals His secret to His servants the prophets); 1 Corinthians 2:9–10 (eye has not seen… but Elohim (God) has revealed to us by His Spirit… deep things of Elohim (God)); Revelation 10:7 (mystery of Elohim (God) finished… declared to His servants the prophets). Key Insight for Discernment: The four presences model heavenly intercession, mercy, healing, power, and hope—surrounding Yahuah’s throne while defending the elect against accusation. The revelation of cosmic secrets to the righteous/elect prepares them for judgment and victory, showing Yahuah (God) shares hidden wisdom with the faithful (not the proud or sinners). This contrasts the Watchers’ illicit revelation of secrets with divine disclosure in righteousness. It encourages seeking Yahuah’s wisdom now—He reveals deep things to those who fear Him (Psalm 25:14; Proverbs 3:32). Let the ceaseless praise and unveiled secrets inspire awe and perseverance: the righteous’ voices are heard, their path illuminated (Psalm 119:105). Test all things: does a teaching reveal Yahuah’s truth or hide it in deception? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Secrets of Lightning, Winds, and the Division of the Righteous and Sinners

verses.text: And after that I saw all the secrets of the heavens, and how the kingdom is divided, and how the actions of men are weighed in the balance.

And there I saw the mansions of the elect and the mansions of the holy, and mine eyes saw there all the sinners being driven from thence who deny the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits, and being dragged off: and they could not abide because of the punishment which proceeds from Yahuah (God) of Spirits.

And there mine eyes saw the secrets of the lightning and of the thunder, and the secrets of the winds, how they are divided to blow over the earth, and the secrets of the clouds and dew, and there I saw from whence they proceed in that place and from whence they saturate the dusty earth.

And there I saw closed chambers out of which the winds are divided, the chamber of the hail and winds, the chamber of the mist, and of the clouds, and the cloud thereof hovers over the earth from the beginning of the world.

And I saw the chambers of the sun and moon, whence they proceed and whither they come again, and their glorious return, and how one is superior to the other, and their stately orbit, and how they do not leave their orbit, and they add nothing to their orbit and they do not take away from it, and they keep faith one with another: and in accordance with an oath they set and they rise.

And after that I saw the hidden and the visible path of the moon, and she accomplishes the monthly revolution by day and by night—the one holding a position opposite to the other before Yahuah (God) of Spirits. And they give thanks and praise and rest not; for unto them is their thanksgiving rest.

For the sun changes oft for a blessing or a curse, and the course of the path of the moon is light to the righteous and darkness to the sinners in the name of Yahuah (God), who made a division between the light and the darkness, and divided the spirits of men, and strengthened the spirits of the righteous in the name of His righteousness.
And no angel here has power to intercede for man, nor yet is any angel able to hear the prayer of man.
But He Himself is the judge of all, and He judges all according to their deeds.

And in those days the sinners shall be driven from the face of the righteous, and the righteous shall be victorious in the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits, and the sinners shall be cast into the furnace of fire.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 41 unveils more hidden cosmic mechanisms and eschatological divisions: the chambers of lightning/thunder/winds/clouds/dew/hail/mist, the regulated paths of sun and moon (never deviating, bound by oath), their superior/inferior courses, and how they bring blessing or curse. The moon’s light shines on the righteous while darkness covers sinners—Yahuah (God) divides light from darkness, good from evil spirits. No angel intercedes for man; Yahuah (God) alone judges deeds. The chapter culminates in the final separation: sinners driven off, righteous victorious in Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ name, sinners cast into the furnace of fire. - Verses 1–4: Secrets of heavens/kingdom/actions weighed; mansions of elect/holy; sinners driven off, unable to abide punishment; chambers of lightning/thunder/winds/clouds/dew/hail/mist. - Cross-refs: Job 38:22–30 (treasuries of snow/hail… path for lightning… ordinances of heavens); Psalm 135:7 (clouds rise from ends of earth… brings wind from treasuries); Jeremiah 10:13 (voice of thunder… clouds from ends of earth); Psalm 148:8 (fire/hail/snow/clouds/stormy wind fulfilling His word). - Verses 5–7: Chambers of sun/moon; unchanging orbits/oaths; sun changes for blessing/curse; moon light for righteous/darkness for sinners; Yahuah (God) divides light/darkness, strengthens righteous spirits. - Cross-refs: Genesis 1:14–18 (lights for signs/seasons… rule day/night); Psalm 104:19 (moon for seasons; sun knows going down); Psalm 19:4–6 (sun circuit… nothing hidden from heat); Malachi 4:2 (Sun of Righteousness arise with healing); Isaiah 60:19–20 (Yahuah (God) everlasting light… sun/moon no more needed); 2 Corinthians 4:6 (Elohim (God) who commanded light to shine… shine in hearts). - Verses 8–10: No angel intercedes for man; Yahuah (God) alone judges deeds; sinners driven off, righteous victorious, sinners into furnace of fire. - Cross-refs: Hebrews 1:14 (ministering spirits… for those who inherit salvation); Hebrews 2:16 (He does not give aid to angels, but to seed of Abraham); Romans 2:6–11 (Yahuah (God) renders to each according to deeds); Matthew 25:41, 46 (eternal fire for devil/angels… eternal punishment); Revelation 20:12–15 (judged by works… lake of fire). Key Insight for Discernment: Yahuah (God) alone judges—no angelic intercession overrides deeds. Cosmic secrets (lightning, winds, luminaries) serve blessing for righteous, curse for sinners—divided by His wisdom. The chapter bridges natural order (unchanging orbits) to moral order (separation of righteous/sinners). It warns: no mediator for the unrepentant; victory belongs to those strengthened by Yahuah’s righteousness. The furnace awaits the wicked, but light and life await the faithful. Let this sharpen focus on deeds and repentance—judgment is by works, mercy through Yahuah’s name (Romans 2:6; James 2:13). Test all things: does a teaching emphasize Yahuah’s sole judgment and division of light/darkness, or blur accountability? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Second Parable – Wisdom’s Rejection and the Dwelling of the Righteous

verses.text: Wisdom found no place where she might dwell; then a dwelling-place was assigned her in the heavens.
Wisdom went forth to make her dwelling among the children of men, but she found no dwelling-place: Wisdom returned to her place, and took her seat among the angels.
And unrighteousness went forth from her chambers: she found whom she sought, and dwelt with them, as rain in a desert and dew in a thirsty land.

And I saw the dwellings of the elect and the dwellings of the holy, and mine eyes saw there all the sinners being driven from thence who deny the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits, and being dragged off: and they could not abide because of the punishment which proceeds from Yahuah (God) of Spirits.

And there mine eyes saw their dwellings with His righteous angels, and their resting-places with the holy, and they intercede and pray for the children of men, and righteousness flows before them like water, and mercy like dew upon the earth.
And in those days the voice of the Holy One shall be heard in the heaven, and the voice of the Elect One shall be heard from the throne of glory.
And in those days the elect shall dwell upon the earth, and the righteous shall dwell with them, and they shall not be separated.
And the Yahuah (God) of Spirits shall abide over them, and with them they shall eat and drink and praise the Yahuah (God) of Spirits.
And in those days the mountains shall leap like rams, and the hills shall skip like lambs, and the righteous shall be victorious in the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits.
And the light of the righteous shall shine like the light of the sun, and the sinners shall be as darkness, and they shall not be able to stand before the face of the Holy One.
And the righteous shall be victorious, and the elect shall be victorious, and they shall not be ashamed, and they shall not be confounded.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 42 opens the Second Parable with a poignant allegory: Wisdom (personified as a divine attribute or entity) searches for a home among humanity but finds none worthy—unrighteousness welcomes her instead, flourishing like rain in a desert. Wisdom returns to heaven, taking her seat among the angels. The chapter then contrasts this rejection with the blessed state of the elect and righteous: their dwellings with holy angels, intercession for men, flowing righteousness/mercy, and ultimate victory. The righteous live in unity with Yahuah (God) of Spirits abiding among them—feasting, praising, shining in light—while sinners face darkness and inability to stand before the Holy One. The imagery of leaping mountains and skipping hills evokes creation’s joy at redemption. - Verses 1–3: Wisdom’s failed search for dwelling on earth; unrighteousness takes her place, flourishing in barren places. - Cross-refs: Proverbs 8:22–31 (Wisdom with Yahuah (God) at creation… delights in sons of men); Baruch 3:9–4:4 (Wisdom not found among men… has found her dwelling in Elohim (God)); Sirach 24:1–12 (Wisdom seeks resting-place… commands to dwell in Jacob); James 3:17 (wisdom from above… pure, peaceable); Romans 1:21–25 (exchanged truth for lie… worshiped creation). - Verses 4–11: Dwellings of elect/holy with angels; intercession, righteousness/mercy flow; sinners driven off; Yahuah (God)/ Elect One’s voice heard; righteous dwell with Yahuah (God), victorious, shining, unashamed; sinners in darkness. - Cross-refs: Psalm 133:1–3 (brethren dwell in unity… dew of Hermon); Revelation 21:3 (tabernacle of Elohim (God) with men); Isaiah 35:10 (ransomed return with joy… sorrow flees); Malachi 4:2 (Sun of Righteousness arise with healing); Psalm 97:11–12 (light sown for righteous); Hebrews 12:22–24 (Mount Zion… spirits of righteous made perfect); Revelation 22:3–5 (no more curse… they shall reign forever). Key Insight for Discernment: Wisdom’s rejection by humanity (and embrace by unrighteousness) explains the world’s disorder—yet the righteous receive her in heaven and will dwell with Yahuah (God) in the end. The chapter contrasts earthly rejection with heavenly acceptance: the elect’s dwellings are secure with angels, their victory assured in Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ presence. This parable warns that rejecting divine wisdom invites unrighteousness, while humility opens the way to eternal fellowship and light. It points forward to the ultimate restoration where Wisdom returns fully with the Elect One. Let this call us to seek wisdom now—lest we miss her dwelling among the righteous (Proverbs 1:20–33; James 1:5). Test all things: does a teaching embrace Wisdom’s path or reject her like the unrighteous? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Vision of Lightning and Stars – The Righteous and the Elect

verses.text: And I saw other lightnings and the stars of heaven, and I saw how He called them all by their names and they hearkened unto Him.

And I saw how they are weighed in the balance according to their light, and according to the measure of their days, and how their revolution produces lightning, and in accordance with the number of the change of the months they change their revolution.
And when the year of their revolution is accomplished, they all return to their place in their own order, and they do not transgress their prescribed law.
And I saw how the chariots of heaven run in their courses, and they do not turn aside from their path.
And I saw the chariots of the sun and moon, and they do not change their path.
And I saw the four winds which support the earth and the firmament of the heaven.
And I saw how the winds stretch out the vaults of heaven, and have their station between heaven and earth: these are the pillars of the heaven.
And I saw the winds of heaven which turn and bring the circumference of the sun and all the stars to their setting.
And I saw the winds on the earth carrying the clouds: I saw the paths of the angels.
And I saw at the end of the earth the firmament of the heaven above.
And I proceeded to the north, and I saw there the great mountains of precious stones, and the trees of paradise, and the fragrant trees.
And I saw the treasuries of the snow and the treasuries of the hail, and the treasuries of the clouds, and the treasuries of the dew and the rain.
And I saw the treasuries of all the winds: I saw how He has ordered all creation by His wisdom, and how He has founded the world upon them.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 43 presents a symbolic vision of cosmic order as a parable for the righteous and elect: the stars and lightning (representing the faithful) are called by name by Yahuah (God) of Spirits, weighed in balance according to their light and days, and return faithfully to their places without transgression. Their revolution produces light, and they maintain prescribed law—contrasting sharply with the fallen angels/stars who deviated and were bound (Ch. 18, 21). The chariots of sun/moon, four winds as pillars, and treasuries of elements all operate under Yahuah’s wisdom, founding the world securely. This reinforces that the righteous, like obedient stars, shine, endure, and return to their appointed place in glory. - Verses 1–5: Stars/lightning called by name, hearkening to Yahuah (God); weighed by light/days; revolution produces lightning; return to place without transgression; chariots of sun/moon unchanging. - Cross-refs: Psalm 147:4 (He counts the number of the stars; He calls them all by name); Isaiah 40:26 (He brings out host by number… calls them all by name); Psalm 19:1–4 (heavens declare glory… no speech, yet voice heard); Job 38:31–33 (can you bind Pleiades… know ordinances of heavens?); Jeremiah 31:35 (ordinances of sun/moon/stars do not fail). - Verses 6–13: Four winds supporting earth/firmament as pillars; turning heaven/sun/stars; carrying clouds; paths of angels; northern precious mountains, paradise/fragrant trees; treasuries of snow/hail/clouds/dew/rain/winds; creation ordered by Yahuah’s wisdom, world founded upon them. - Cross-refs: Job 26:7–11 (hangs earth on nothing… pillars of heaven tremble); Zechariah 6:5 (four spirits/winds from before Yahuah (God)); Psalm 135:7 (clouds from ends of earth… wind from treasuries); Proverbs 3:19–20 (Yahuah (God) founded earth by wisdom… heavens by understanding); Psalm 104:5 (foundations of earth set so it cannot be moved). Key Insight for Discernment: The obedient stars/lightning parable the righteous and elect: named, weighed, faithful in course, shining in light—never transgressing Yahuah’s law. The fallen (who changed course) face binding; the faithful return to glory. Cosmic order (winds, treasuries, luminaries) testifies to Yahuah’s wisdom sustaining creation—inviting the righteous to emulate this faithfulness amid tribulation. The vision promises: those who keep their appointed path will shine eternally (Daniel 12:3—“those who turn many to righteousness like stars forever”). Let this encourage steadfastness—your name is known, your course appointed (Isaiah 43:1). Test all things: does a path shine with obedience like the stars, or deviate like the fallen? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Vision of Lightning and the Stars of the Righteous

verses.text: Also another phenomenon I saw in regard to the secrets of lightning and thunder, and the secrets of the winds, how they are divided to blow over the earth, and the secrets of the clouds and dew, and there I saw from whence they proceed in that place and from whence they saturate the dusty earth.

And there I saw closed chambers out of which the winds are divided, the chamber of the hail and winds, the chamber of the mist, and of the clouds, and the cloud thereof hovers over the earth from the beginning of the world.

And I saw the chambers of the sun and moon, whence they proceed and whither they come again, and their glorious return, and how one is superior to the other, and their stately orbit, and how they do not leave their orbit, and they add nothing to their orbit and they do not take away from it, and they keep faith one with another: and in accordance with an oath they set and they rise.

And after that I saw the hidden and the visible path of the moon, and she accomplishes the monthly revolution by day and by night—the one holding a position opposite to the other before Yahuah (God) of Spirits. And they give thanks and praise and rest not; for unto them is their thanksgiving rest.

For the sun changes oft for a blessing or a curse, and the course of the path of the moon is light to the righteous and darkness to the sinners in the name of Yahuah (God), who made a division between the light and the darkness, and divided the spirits of men, and strengthened the spirits of the righteous in the name of His righteousness.
And no angel here has power to intercede for man, nor yet is any angel able to hear the prayer of man.
But He Himself is the judge of all, and He judges all according to their deeds.

And in those days the sinners shall be driven from the face of the righteous, and the righteous shall be victorious in the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits, and the sinners shall be cast into the furnace of fire.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 44 extends the cosmic revelations with a focus on lightning and thunder as parables for sudden divine judgment and illumination. Lightning flashes across the sky—brief, powerful, illuminating darkness—symbolizing the righteous and elect who shine in their generation, testifying to Yahuah’s glory before returning to their place. Thunder accompanies, representing the voice of judgment. The chapter reiterates the unchanging obedience of sun, moon, and stars (oaths, orbits, no deviation), their courses bringing blessing to the righteous and curse to sinners. Yahuah (God) divides light from darkness, strengthens the righteous’ spirits, and alone judges deeds—no angel intercedes. Sinners are driven away, cast into the furnace; the righteous triumph in Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ name. - Verses 1–4: Secrets of lightning/thunder/winds/clouds/dew; chambers of elements; sun/moon chambers, orbits, oaths, unchanging faithfulness. - Cross-refs: Job 38:25–27 (path for lightning… channels for waters… waste and desolate land); Psalm 29:3–9 (voice of Yahuah (God)… breaks cedars… shakes wilderness); Psalm 147:4 (counts stars… calls them by name); Jeremiah 31:35 (ordinances of sun/moon/stars do not fail). - Verses 5–8: Sun/moon bring blessing/curse; moon light for righteous/darkness for sinners; Yahuah (God) divides light/darkness, strengthens righteous; no angelic intercession; Yahuah (God) judges deeds; sinners driven off, cast into fire; righteous victorious. - Cross-refs: Genesis 1:4 (Elohim (God) divided light from darkness); Malachi 4:1–2 (day burns like oven… Sun of Righteousness arises with healing); Romans 2:6–11 (Yahuah (God) renders according to deeds); Matthew 25:41, 46 (eternal fire… eternal punishment); Revelation 20:12–15 (judged by works… lake of fire); Psalm 37:6 (righteousness shine like dawn… justice like noonday sun). Key Insight for Discernment: Lightning’s flash—sudden, illuminating, unstoppable—parables the righteous who shine briefly but powerfully in darkness, testifying before returning to Yahuah (God). The unchanging luminaries contrast the fallen who broke their orbits. Yahuah (God) alone judges—no proxy intercession; deeds determine destiny. This chapter warns of final separation (righteous light, sinners fire) while promising strength and victory for the faithful. It calls us to shine now—be faithful in our “course” like the stars (Philippians 2:15—“shine as lights in the world”). Let the division of light/darkness sharpen resolve: choose the path that ends in victory, not the furnace (John 3:19–21). Test all things: does a teaching bring light and obedience, or darkness and transgression? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Third Parable – The Coming of the Elect One and Judgment

verses.text: And this is the third parable concerning those who deny the name of the dwelling of the holy ones and of Yahuah (God) of Spirits.

And into the heaven they shall not ascend, and on the earth they shall not come: such shall be the lot of the sinners who have denied the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits, who are thus preserved for the day of suffering and tribulation.
On that day Mine Elect One shall sit on the throne of glory and shall try their works, and their place shall be nothing and their dwelling shall be with the faithless.

And on that day I will cause Mine Elect One to dwell among them, and I will change the heaven and the earth and the light and the darkness, and I will make the earth a thing of light and the darkness a thing of darkness.
And I will make the sinners to be as straw in the fire, and they shall burn before the face of the holy, and they shall not be quenched.
And the righteous shall be victorious in the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits, and the sinners shall be cast into the furnace of fire.
And in those days the kings and the mighty who possess the earth shall be cast down from their thrones, and they shall be cast into the furnace of fire, and their faces shall be covered with shame.

And the Yahuah (God) of Spirits shall cause them to be cast down into the furnace of fire, and they shall be cast into the furnace of fire, and their faces shall be covered with shame, and they shall be cast into the furnace of fire.

And in those days the righteous shall be victorious, and the light of the righteous shall shine, and the sinners shall be as darkness, and they shall not be able to stand before the face of the Holy One.
And the righteous shall be victorious, and the elect shall be victorious, and they shall not be ashamed, and they shall not be confounded.
And in those days the earth shall give back that which has been entrusted to it, and Sheol also shall give back that which it has received, and hell shall give back that which it owes.
And He shall choose the righteous and holy from among them: for the day has drawn nigh that they should be saved.
And the righteous shall be victorious in the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits, and the sinners shall be cast into the furnace of fire.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 45 launches the Third Parable, intensifying the eschatological focus: the fate of those who deny Yahuah (God) of Spirits (no ascension to heaven, no place on renewed earth—reserved for suffering). The Elect One sits on the throne of glory to judge works; the wicked find no place, while the Elect One dwells among the faithful. Yahuah (God) transforms heaven and earth—light for the righteous, darkness for sinners. Sinners burn like straw before the holy; kings/mighty are cast from thrones into fire, faces covered in shame. The righteous shine victorious, unashamed. The chapter culminates in the resurrection: earth, Sheol, and hell give up their dead; Yahuah (God) chooses the righteous/holy for salvation on the day that draws near. - Verses 1–6: Parable against deniers of Yahuah’s name; no heavenly ascent or earthly place; lot of suffering; Elect One on throne tries works; wicked place nothing; earth changed—light/darkness divided; sinners as straw in fire. - Cross-refs: Revelation 20:11–15 (great white throne… dead judged… death/hell give up dead… lake of fire); Isaiah 66:24 (worm not die, fire not quenched); Malachi 4:1 (day burns like oven… wicked as stubble); 2 Peter 3:10–13 (day of Yahuah (God)… heavens pass away… new heavens/new earth). - Verses 7–10: Kings/mighty cast down into fire, shame; righteous victorious, shining light; sinners darkness, unable to stand before Holy One. - Cross-refs: Isaiah 2:10–17 (hide in dust… lofty humbled); Revelation 6:15–17 (kings hide from face of throne… wrath of Lamb); Psalm 2:10–12 (kings warned… kiss Son lest He be angry); Luke 1:52 (cast down mighty from thrones… exalted humble). - Verses 11–13: Resurrection—earth/Sheol/hell give back dead; Yahuah (God) chooses righteous/holy for salvation; righteous victorious, sinners into fire. - Cross-refs: Daniel 12:2 (many sleep in dust awake—everlasting life or contempt); John 5:28–29 (all in graves hear voice… resurrection of life or condemnation); Revelation 20:13 (sea/death/hell give up dead… judged by works); 1 Corinthians 15:52–53 (dead raised incorruptible… mortal puts on immortality). Key Insight for Discernment: The Third Parable centers on the Elect One’s enthronement and judgment: deniers face exclusion from both realms, kings/mighty humiliated in fire, while the righteous shine and inherit salvation. Resurrection is universal—none escape accounting—but Yahuah (God) chooses the holy for life. This intensifies hope for the elect amid oppression: the day draws near; transformation awaits. It warns the powerful: thrones fall, shame awaits unrighteousness. Let this strengthen resolve—stand with the righteous, for Yahuah’s justice prevails (Romans 8:18–23; Revelation 22:12). Test all things: does a teaching prepare for this throne-judgment and resurrection, or deny the Elect One’s coming? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21).

chapters.title: The Ancient of Days and the Son of Man

verses.text: And there I saw One who had a head of days, and His head was white like wool, and with Him was another being whose countenance had the appearance of a man, and his face was full of graciousness, like one of the holy angels.
And I asked the angel who went with me, who showed me all the hidden things, concerning that Son of Adam, who he was, and whence he was, (and) why he went with the Head of Days?

And he answered and said unto me: This is the Son of Adam who hath righteousness, with whom dwelleth righteousness, and who revealeth all the treasures of that which is hidden, because Yahuah (God) of Spirits hath chosen him, and whose lot hath the pre-eminence before Yahuah (God) of Spirits in uprightness for ever.

And this Son of Adam whom thou hast seen shall raise up the kings and the mighty from their seats, [And the strong from their thrones] And shall loosen the reins of the strong, And break the teeth of the sinners.
[And he shall put down the kings from their thrones and kingdoms] Because they do not extol and praise Him, Nor humbly acknowledge whence the kingdom was bestowed upon them.
And he shall humble the countenance of the strong, And shall abase the pride of the mighty, And shall make the earth shake, And shall lay low the inhabitants thereof, And shall not be ashamed.

And the countenance of the strong shall be covered with shame, And darkness shall be their dwelling, And worms shall be their bed, And they shall have no hope of rising from their beds, Because they do not extol the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits.
And these are they who judge the stars of heaven, [And raise their hands against the Most High,] And tread upon the earth and dwell upon it.

And all their deeds manifest unrighteousness, And their power rests upon their riches, And their faith is in the gods which they have made with their hands, And they deny the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits,
And they persecute the houses of His congregations, And the faithful who hang upon the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 46 unveils one of the most striking revelations in 1 Enoch: the vision of the Ancient of Days (Head of Days) on the throne—white-haired, majestic—and beside Him the Son of Man / Elect One, full of grace like a holy angel. Enoch inquires about this figure, and the accompanying angel explains: the Son of Man is chosen by Yahuah (God) of Spirits, dwells in righteousness, reveals hidden treasures, and holds pre-eminence forever. He will judge and humble kings/mighty, loosen their reins, break sinners’ teeth, cast them into darkness/worms (no hope of rising), because they deny Yahuah (God), trust in idols, persecute the faithful, and exalt their power/riches. The righteous, who hang upon Yahuah’s name, are vindicated. The Elect One, the Ancient of Days, and the Formless/Formed Structure The existing commentary correctly identifies the Son of Man as named before the sun and stars were created, enthroned, chosen by Yahuah (God) of Spirits. It cross-references Daniel 7 and Revelation 1 accurately. What it does not do — and what this Enochian vision demands — is explain why there are two figures here and what their relationship actually is. - Verses 1–3: Ancient of Days (white head like wool); Son of Man beside Him, gracious countenance; chosen by Yahuah (God) of Spirits, righteousness dwells with Him, reveals hidden things, pre-eminent forever. - Cross-refs: Daniel 7:9–10, 13–14 (Ancient of Days… throne like fiery flame… Son of Man with clouds… given everlasting dominion); Revelation 1:13–14 (one like Son of Man… hair white like wool); Isaiah 11:2–5 (Spirit rests on Him… judge with righteousness… smite earth with rod of mouth). - Verses 4–7: Son of Man raises/humbles kings/mighty from thrones, loosens reins, breaks teeth of sinners; they covered in shame, darkness dwelling, worms bed, no rising—because no praise/acknowledgment of Yahuah (God). - Cross-refs: Psalm 2:10–12 (kings warned… kiss Son lest angry); Isaiah 2:10–17 (lofty looks humbled… day of Yahuah (God)); Revelation 6:15–17 (kings hide from throne… wrath of Lamb); Psalm 49:16–20 (fear not when one becomes rich… no glory in death… like beasts that perish). - Verses 8–10: They judge stars/heaven, tread earth, trust idols/handmade gods, deny Yahuah (God) of Spirits, persecute congregations/faithful who hang on His name. - Cross-refs: Daniel 7:25 (speak against Most High… wear out saints); Revelation 13:5–7 (beast speaks blasphemies… war against saints); Psalm 94:4–7 (arrogant boast… crush people… say Yahuah (God) does not see); Isaiah 10:1–4 (woe to those who decree unrighteous decrees… poor crushed… no place to flee). Key Insight for Discernment: This chapter is foundational for understanding the “Son of Man” title in the New Testament—named before the sun and stars were created, chosen by Yahuah (God) of Spirits, enthroned beside the Ancient of Days, executing judgment on oppressors and revealing hidden things. Kings/mighty fall for denying Yahuah (God), trusting idols, and persecuting the faithful. The righteous, who cling to His name, inherit vindication and eternal pre-eminence. It warns the powerful: thrones are temporary, denial brings shame/darkness. It comforts the persecuted: the Elect One comes to reverse injustice. Let this vision fuel hope and courage—hang upon Yahuah’s name, for the Son of Man reigns (Matthew 26:64; Revelation 1:13). Test all things: does a teaching honor the Elect One’s judgment and vindication of the faithful, or exalt human power? (Acts 17:11; 1 Thessalonians 5:21). The Head of Days and the Son of Man: Understanding What Enoch Saw Enoch sees two figures. One is seated — the Ancient of Days, the Head of Days, white-haired, majestic, enthroned. The other stands beside Him — the Son of Man, full of grace, chosen, pre-eminent, about to be given judgment authority over all kings and mighty. This is not a vision of two gods. And it is not a vision of three separate personalities arranged in a Trinitarian council. It is the vision of the Formless and the Formed — the eternal structure that Scripture reveals from beginning to end, now made visible to Enoch in the heavenly court. The seated one — the Head of Days — is the Father: the infinite, formless source from which all things proceed. He does not appear in theophanic form to the patriarchs. He does not wrestle with Jacob. He does not walk in the garden. He does not speak from the fire on Sinai. He is the source — the one before all things, the throne from which all authority flows. He cannot be reduced to “a god.” He cannot be categorized as one personality among three. He is the formless infinite, the one Yahusha (Jesus) called “the only true God” (John 17:3) and to whom Yahusha (Jesus) submitted from eternity. The one beside Him — the Son of Man, the Elect One — is the Formed: the Word who drew itself from within the formless and became the expressed, active God. This is the God of the Old Testament — the one who appeared to Abraham at the oak of Mamre (Genesis 18), who wrestled with Jacob at the Jabbok (Genesis 32), who spoke to Moses from the burning bush (Exodus 3), who led Israel through the wilderness in a pillar of fire (Exodus 13). The Formed one has always had a face. The Father has no form that creation can contain. When Enoch sees the Son of Man named before the Head of Days before the sun and stars were created (Chapter 48:2–3), he is seeing what John would later write: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God” (John 1:1). The Word — the Formed one — was with the Father before creation. Named before creation. Chosen before creation. Pre-eminent before creation. Then the Formed one entered creation fully — not just as theophany and appearance, but as flesh. That is Yahusha (Jesus). This is why Yahusha (Jesus) could say “the Father is greater than I” (John 14:28) and simultaneously “I and the Father are one” (John 10:30). He is not lying in either statement. He is describing the eternal relationship between the Formless and the Formed: the Formed proceeds from the Formless, remains part of the Formless, submits to the will of the Formless — and is, at the same time, fully God. Not a lesser god. Not a second god. The expressed God. The Formed one. The Trinity doctrine imports Greek philosophical categories into a Hebrew revelation that has no such structure. Enoch did not see a council of equals. He saw the Father on the throne and the Son of Man standing beside Him — not as an equal among equals, but as the one who proceeds from the Ancient of Days and carries His full authority into creation and judgment. And Enoch himself? He is the witness. He is the scribe. He is the righteous man taken up to see what was hidden. He is not the Elect One. He is not the Son of Man. He beholds the Son of Man and weeps in awe before Yahuah (God) of Spirits. There is no confusion in the vision itself — only in teachers who have tried to make Enoch into what the vision explicitly shows him worshipping. Cross-refs: John 1:1–3 (Word with God, Word was God, all things made through Him); John 14:28 (Father is greater than I — submission of the Formed to the Formless); John 10:30 (I and the Father are one — unity of Formless and Formed); John 17:5 (glory I had with You before the world was — the Formed one’s pre-existence with the Father); Colossians 1:15–17 (image of the invisible God, firstborn of creation, before all things, by Him all consist); John 17:3 (the only true God — the Father as the Formless source); Genesis 18:1–2 (Yahuah (God) appeared to Abraham — the Formed one in theophany); Exodus 3:2–4 (Angel of Yahuah (God) in flame, then Yahuah (God) speaks — the Formed one); 1 John 4:2–3 (test: does it confess Yahusha (Jesus) come in the flesh?). The Head of Days and the Elect One — The Formless and the Formed The Parables do not present a theological puzzle here. They present what Enoch was shown. Two figures. One seated — the Head of Days, the Ancient of Days, enthroned, white-haired, the source of all authority. One standing beside Him — the Son of Man, the Elect One, chosen, pre-eminent, about to receive the authority of judgment over all kings and mighty. This is not two gods. It is not three separate personalities assembled in a council. It is the Formless and the Formed — the eternal structure Scripture reveals from Genesis to Revelation, now made visible in the heavenly court. The seated one is the Father — the infinite source from which all things proceed. He has no form creation can contain. He does not appear to the patriarchs. He does not wrestle with Jacob or walk in the garden or speak from the fire on Sinai. He is the throne. He is the source. The one Yahusha (Jesus) called “the only true God” (John 17:3) and to whose will Yahusha (Jesus) submitted from eternity. The one standing beside Him — the Elect One, the Son of Man of the Parables — is the Formed: the Word drawn from within the Formless, the expressed and active God, the one who has always had a face in creation. This is the God of the Old Testament interactions. The one who appeared to Abraham at Mamre (Genesis 18). Who wrestled with Jacob at the Jabbok (Genesis 32). Who spoke from the burning bush (Exodus 3). Who led Israel in the pillar of fire (Exodus 13). The Formed one entered creation fully in Yahusha (Jesus) — not for the first time appearing, but for the first time as flesh. When Chapter 48 says the Son of Man was named before the Head of Days before the sun and stars were created, it is saying what John would later write: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God” (John 1:1). Named before creation. Chosen before creation. Pre-eminent before creation. This is why Yahusha (Jesus) could say “the Father is greater than I” (John 14:28) and “I and the Father are one” (John 10:30) without contradiction. The Formed proceeds from the Formless, remains of the Formless, submits to the will of the Formless — and is simultaneously fully God. Not a lesser god. Not a second god. The expressed God, the Formed one, come in the flesh. The Trinity imports Greek philosophical architecture into a Hebrew revelation that carries no such structure. Enoch did not see a council of equals. He saw the Father enthroned and the Son of Man standing beside Him — not as one equal among equals but as the one who proceeds from the Ancient of Days and carries His full authority into creation and judgment. Cross-refs: John 1:1–3 (Word with God, Word was God, all things through Him); John 14:28 (Father greater than I — the Formed submits to the Formless); John 10:30 (I and the Father are one — unity of source and expression); John 17:3 (the only true God — the Father as formless source); John 17:5 (glory with You before the world was — pre-existence of the Formed); Genesis 18:1–2 (Yahuah (God) appeared to Abraham — the Formed in theophany); Exodus 3:2–4 (Angel of Yahuah (God) in flame, Yahuah (God) speaks — the Formed one); Colossians 1:15–17 (image of the invisible God, before all things, by Him all consist).

chapters.title: The Prayer of the Righteous Ascends, and Judgment Draws Near

verses.text: And in those days shall have ascended the prayer of the righteous, And the blood of the righteous from the earth before Yahuah (God) of Spirits.

In those days the holy ones who dwell above in the heavens Shall unite with one voice And supplicate and pray [and praise, And give thanks and bless the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits] On behalf of the blood of the righteous which has been shed, And that the prayer of the righteous may not be in vain before Yahuah (God) of Spirits, That judgement may be done unto them, And that they may not have to suffer for ever.

In those days I saw the Head of Days when He seated Himself upon the throne of His glory, And the books of the living were opened before Him: And all His host which is in heaven above and His counsellors stood before Him.

And the hearts of the holy were filled with joy; Because the number of the righteous had been offered, And the prayer of the righteous had been heard, And the blood of the righteous been required before Yahuah (God) of Spirits.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 47 shifts focus to the vindication of the persecuted righteous: their prayers and shed blood rise as a cry before Yahuah (God) of Spirits, prompting heavenly intercession by the holy ones (angels/saints). This leads to the Head of Days(Ancient of Days) opening the books of the living on His glorious throne, with all heavenly host attending. The righteous rejoice as their cries are heard, their blood avenged, and judgment prepared—ending endless suffering. It builds on Chapter 46’s judgment theme, showing divine response to oppression: the faithful’s endurance is not forgotten; heaven unites in advocacy, and Yahuah (God) acts decisively. Verse 1: The prayer and blood of the righteous ascend from earth to Yahuah (God) of Spirits. Cross-refs: Revelation 6:9–11 (souls under altar cry “How long?”… given white robes, told to rest until number complete); Genesis 4:10 (Abel’s blood cries from ground); Psalm 9:12 (Yahuah (God) remembers blood… avenges); Luke 18:7–8 (Yahuah (God) avenge elect who cry day/night… speedily). Verse 2: Heavenly holy ones unite in voice to supplicate, pray, praise, thank, and bless Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ name on behalf of shed blood; so prayers not in vain, judgment executed, no eternal suffering. Cross-refs: Revelation 8:3–5 (prayers of saints with incense… fire cast to earth); Psalm 141:2 (prayer as incense before Yahuah (God)); Hebrews 12:24 (blood of sprinkling that speaks better than Abel’s). Verse 3: Enoch sees Head of Days on throne of glory; books of living opened; heavenly host/counsellors stand before Him. Cross-refs: Daniel 7:9–10 (Ancient of Days takes seat… books opened… thousand thousands minister); Revelation 20:12 (books opened… judged by things written… book of life); Malachi 3:16 (book of remembrance… Yahuah (God) hearkens). Verse 4: Hearts of holy filled with joy—righteous number offered (complete), prayer heard, blood required (avenged) before Yahuah (God) of Spirits. Cross-refs: Philippians 4:3 (names in book of life); Psalm 56:8 (put my tears in Your bottle… in Your book); Revelation 7:9–17 (great multitude… washed robes… serve before throne); Isaiah 25:8 (wipe away tears… swallow up death). Key Insight for Discernment: This chapter powerfully depicts Yahuah (God) of Spirits as responsive to injustice—the cries of martyrs and oppressed righteous are not ignored; they ascend like incense, triggering heavenly unity and divine action. The Head of Days on the throne (with opened books) signals final accounting: persecution ends, vengeance comes, joy for the faithful. It echoes the NT’s assurance that Yahuah (God) hears persistent prayer and avenges His elect swiftly (Luke 18:7–8). For today: in times of trial or denial of Yahuah’s name (as in prior chapters), cling to prayer—your blood/cries rise before Him. Test teachings: do they acknowledge Yahuah’s justice for the persecuted, or minimize suffering? The righteous’ vindication fuels endurance; the oppressors’ day ends in required blood (Hebrews 10:30–31; Romans 12:19). Hang upon Yahuah’s name—He opens the books, and joy awaits the faithful (Revelation 7:9–17).

chapters.title: The Fount of Righteousness; the Son of Man Named; Judgment on Kings and Mighty

verses.text: And in that place I saw the fountain of righteousness Which was inexhaustible: And around it were many fountains of wisdom: And all the thirsty drank of them, And were filled with wisdom, And their dwellings were with the righteous and holy and elect.
And at that hour that Son of Adam was named In the presence of Yahuah (God) of Spirits, And his name before the Head of Days.
Yea, before the sun and the signs were created, Before the stars of the heaven were made, His name was named before Yahuah (God) of Spirits.
He shall be a staff to the righteous whereon to stay themselves and not fall, And he shall be the light of the Gentiles, And the hope of those who are troubled of heart.
All who dwell on earth shall fall down and worship before him, And will praise and bless and celebrate with song Yahuah (God) of Spirits.
And for this reason hath he been chosen and hidden before Him, Before the creation of the world and for evermore.

And the wisdom of Yahuah (God) of Spirits hath revealed him to the holy and righteous; For he hath preserved the lot of the righteous, Because they have hated and despised this world of unrighteousness, And have hated all its works and ways in the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits: For in his name they are saved, And according to his good pleasure hath it been in regard to their life.
In these days shall the kings and the mighty who possess the earth implore (Him) To grant them a little respite from His angels of punishment To whom they were delivered.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 48 continues the Parables’ focus on the named-before-creation, exalted Son of Man (Elect One): a never-failing fountain of righteousness and wisdom sustains the righteous/elect/holy.
