And thou shalt preserve them, And thou shalt not alter them, For the luminaries do not alter their courses, And the earth does not alter her seasons, And the sea does not alter her boundaries.

And now I have shown thee the chiefs of the stars, And the leaders of the luminaries, And the chiefs of the four quarters of the year, And the chiefs of the intercalary days, And the chiefs of the months, And the chiefs of the weeks, And the chiefs of the days, And the chiefs of the hours.

And these are the names of the chiefs of the stars: the leader of the first month is Melkî’êl, the leader of the second month is Hel’emmelêk, the leader of the third month is Nêlê’êl, the leader of the fourth month is Nârêl, and so on for the twelve months.
And the four leaders of the intercalary days are Melkî’êl, Hel’emmelêk, Nêlê’êl, Nârêl.
And the leaders of the stars are the chiefs of the thousands, And they serve Yahuah (God) of Spirits in their appointed places, And they do not transgress their commandments.
And blessed are those who observe these things, And keep the commandments of Yahuah (God) of Spirits, And walk in righteousness, And complete their years in truth.
And woe to those who alter these things, And lead the sons of Adam astray, And cause them to transgress the commandments of Yahuah (God) of Spirits.
And now, my son Methuselah, Preserve these words, And write them in a book, That they may be for a testimony for the generations of the world.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 82 concludes the Astronomical Book with Enoch’s solemn charge to Methuselah: preserve the books/tablets/vision of heavenly laws (luminaries’ courses, 364-day year, chiefs over times/seasons/stars), transmit faithfully to descendants. Warning: future sinners will alter commandments, times/seasons/new moons/sabbaths/festivals, eat blood, corrupt earth, lead nations astray. Righteous few blessed: keep Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ commandments, walk righteousness, complete years in truth—inherit eternal life. Recaps chiefs (Melkî’êl, Hel’emmelêk, Nêlê’êl, Nârêl over quarters/intercalary days; others over months/stars), all serving Yahuah (God) without transgression. Final exhortation: write in book for testimony, woe to those who alter/lead astray. This seals astronomy as divine revelation for righteous living—order in heavens mirrors obedience on earth; preserve truth amid coming apostasy. Verse 1–2: Shown Methuselah vision; preserve books in heart, teach sons/grandchildren forever. Cross-refs: Deuteronomy 6:6–9 (commandments in heart… teach diligently to children); Psalm 78:4–7 (tell generation to come… that generation set hope in Elohim (God)… keep commandments). Verse 3–4: Sinners alter order/commandments of Yahuah (God) of Spirits; say from Elohim (God); alter times/seasons/new moons/sabbaths/festivals; eat blood/flesh; earth corrupted; nations astray. Cross-refs: Isaiah 5:20 (call evil good… put darkness for light); Galatians 4:10 (observe days/months/seasons/years… weak elements); Acts 15:20,29 (abstain from blood… strangled); 2 Timothy 3:1–5 (perilous times… evil men… form of godliness… deny power). Verse 5: Blessed keep commandments of Yahuah (God) of Spirits, walk righteousness, complete years in truth; inherit eternal life. Cross-refs: Psalm 1:1–3 (blessed… delights in law… prospers); Revelation 22:14 (blessed wash robes… right to tree of life); Matthew 25:46 (righteous into eternal life). Verse 6–7: Shown vision of tablets/commandments of luminaries/stars/sun/moon/winds/earth/sea; preserve, do not alter; luminaries/earth/sea do not alter. Cross-refs: Psalm 119:89–91 (word settled forever… ordinances continue); Jeremiah 31:35–36 (ordinances of sun/moon… not depart); Psalm 148:6 (established forever… decree not pass). Verse 8–11: Shown chiefs of stars/leaders of luminaries/quarters/intercalary days/months/weeks/days/hours; names (Melkî’êl etc.); serve Yahuah (God) of Spirits; no transgression. Cross-refs: Psalm 148:2–6 (praise Yahuah (God)… angels/hosts/sun/moon/stars… decree not pass); Isaiah 40:26 (host by number… power none fails). Verse 12–13: Blessed observe these things, keep commandments of Yahuah (God) of Spirits, walk righteousness, complete years in truth. Woe to those who alter/lead sons of men astray. Cross-refs: Psalm 119:1 (blessed undefiled… walk in law); Matthew 18:6 (woe to one who causes little ones to stumble); Revelation 22:18–19 (if any add/take from words… plagues/tree of life taken). Verse 14: Methuselah: preserve words, write in book for testimony to generations of world. Cross-refs: Deuteronomy 31:19 (write song… put in mouths… testimony); Habakkuk 2:2 (write vision… make plain upon tables… run that reads it); Revelation 1:19 (write things seen/are/shall be hereafter). Key Insight for Discernment: Chapter 82 seals the Astronomical Book as divine revelation: Enoch charges Methuselah to preserve/transmit heavenly laws (luminaries/chiefs/364-day year) faithfully to generations. Warning: sinners will alter commandments/times/seasons/festivals, corrupt earth, lead astray—righteous few blessed with eternal life for obedience. Woe to alterers/deceivers. This calls to guard Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ truth, observe appointed times righteously, reject future apostasy. Discern: Teachings urging preserve Yahuah’s commandments/calendar, warn of altering times/festivals, and promise blessing for faithful align. Beware doctrines changing divine order. Cling to Yahuah’s name—luminaries obey unchanging, righteous inherit life (Psalm 119:1; Revelation 22:14). Hang upon Yahuah’s name; wisdom preserved, generations blessed in truth!

chapters.title: The First Dream-Vision – The Destruction of the Earth by the Flood

verses.text: And now, my son Methuselah, I will show thee all my visions which I have seen, recounting them before thee.

Two visions I saw before I took a wife, and the one was quite unlike the other: on the first occasion, when I was learning to write, on the second, before I took thy mother, (when) I saw a terrible vision.
And regarding them I prayed to Yahuah (God) of Spirits.
I had laid me down in the house of my grandfather Mahalalel, (when) I saw in a vision how the heaven collapsed and was borne off and fell to the earth.
And when it fell to the earth I saw how the earth was swallowed up in a great abyss, and mountains were suspended on mountains.
And I fell upon my face, and cried aloud, saying: ‘O Yahuah (God) of Spirits, what is this terrible thing that Thou hast done to the earth?’
And the earth was rent asunder, and all that was upon the earth perished, and the earth was dissolved.
And I awoke and cried aloud, saying: ‘O Yahuah (God) of Spirits, what is this terrible thing that Thou hast done to the earth?’
And I prayed to Yahuah (God) of Spirits that He would not destroy the whole earth.
And again I saw in a vision, and behold the heaven was rolled up like a scroll, and all the luminaries fell down.
And I fell upon my face, and cried aloud, saying: ‘O Yahuah (God) of Spirits, what is this terrible thing that Thou hast done to the earth?’
And the earth was rent asunder, and all that was upon the earth perished, and the earth was dissolved.
And I awoke and cried aloud, saying: ‘O Yahuah (God) of Spirits, what is this terrible thing that Thou hast done to the earth?’
And I prayed to Yahuah (God) of Spirits that He would not destroy the whole earth.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 83 introduces Enoch’s first dream-vision (pre-marriage, while learning to write), recounted to Methuselah. In the vision: heaven collapses/falls to earth like a scroll, earth swallowed in great abyss, mountains suspended/hanging, luminaries fall. Enoch falls on his face, cries out in terror to Yahuah (God) of Spirits, asking what terrible thing He has done to the earth—praying He not destroy it all. The vision repeats with variations (heaven rolled up, luminaries fall, earth rent/dissolved, all perish). Enoch awakens crying the same plea. This is a prophetic forevision of the Flood’s cataclysm (Genesis 7–8), symbolizing end-time judgment/destruction of corrupt earth (echoing Isaiah 34:4; Revelation 6:14). Enoch’s intercession reflects righteous concern for creation amid coming wrath—Yahuah (God) hears cries of the faithful. Verse 1–2: Shown Methuselah all visions seen; two visions before marriage: first while learning to write, second before taking mother (terrible vision). Cross-refs: Genesis 5:21–24 (Enoch… Methuselah… walked with Elohim (God)); 2 Timothy 2:2 (commit to faithful men… teach others). Verse 3: Prayed to Yahuah (God) of Spirits regarding them. Cross-refs: Psalm 5:3 (morning prayer… look up… wait); Psalm 55:17 (evening/morning/noon prayer… cry out). Verse 4–7: Laid in grandfather Mahalalel’s house; vision heaven collapsed/borne off/fell to earth; earth swallowed in abyss, mountains suspended; fell on face, cried to Yahuah (God) of Spirits: what terrible thing done to earth? Cross-refs: Isaiah 34:4 (host of heaven dissolved… heavens rolled together as scroll… host fall as leaf from vine); Revelation 6:14 (heaven departed as scroll… mountains/islands moved); Habakkuk 3:6 (stood/measured earth… everlasting mountains scattered… perpetual hills bowed); Genesis 7:11 (fountains great deep broken up… windows heaven opened). Verse 8–9: Earth rent asunder/all perished/dissolved; awoke, cried to Yahuah (God) of Spirits: what terrible thing? Prayed not destroy whole earth. Cross-refs: Genesis 7:21–23 (all flesh died… destroyed from earth); Genesis 6:17 (flood destroy all flesh… breath of life); Psalm 46:2–3 (earth change… mountains carried into sea… waters roar). Verse 10–12: Again saw heaven rolled up like scroll; all luminaries fell down; fell on face, cried to Yahuah (God) of Spirits: what terrible thing? Earth rent/asunder/all perished/dissolved. Cross-refs: Revelation 6:13–14 (stars fell to earth… heaven departed as scroll… mountains moved); Isaiah 34:4 (host fall… heavens rolled as scroll); Matthew 24:29 (stars fall from heaven… powers of heavens shaken). Verse 13–14: Awoke, cried to Yahuah (God) of Spirits: what terrible thing? Prayed not destroy whole earth. Cross-refs: Genesis 8:21 (Yahuah (God) smelled sweet savour… not again curse ground… destroy all living); Isaiah 54:9 (waters of Noah… not overflow again); Ezekiel 14:23 (comforted… know not without cause done). Key Insight for Discernment: Chapter 83 unveils Enoch’s first dream-vision—cataclysmic collapse of heaven/earth, luminaries fall, abyss swallows all—prophetic of Flood/end-time judgment. Enoch cries in terror to Yahuah (God) of Spirits, prays not destroy whole earth. This models righteous intercession amid wrath: see coming destruction, plead mercy, trust Yahuah’s justice/mercy. Vision warns: sin brings cosmic upheaval; righteous cry out, preserved. Discern: Teachings affirming Yahuah’s judgment on corruption (Flood/end-times), righteous intercession, and hope in mercy align. Beware ignoring signs of coming disorder. Cling to Yahuah’s name—Enoch cries, Yahuah (God) hears, earth renewed after judgment (Genesis 8:21–22; Revelation 21:1). Hang upon Yahuah’s name; vision terrifies, prayer preserves!

chapters.title: Enoch’s Prayer of Intercession After the First Dream-Vision

verses.text: And I lifted up my hands in righteousness and blessed the Holy and Great One, And spoke with the breath of my mouth, And with the tongue of flesh, Which Elohim (God) has made for the children of the flesh of men, That they should speak therewith, And He has given them breath and a tongue and a mouth That they should speak therewith.

‘Blessed be Thou, O Yahuah (God), King, Great and mighty in Thy greatness, Elyon in Thy dominion, And Thy throne is for ever and ever, And Thy name is holy and great for ever and ever, And blessed be Thou for ever.
Thou hast made all things, And Thou hast power over all things: And all things are naked and open in Thy sight, And Thou seest all things, And nothing can hide itself from Thee.
Thou seest what Azâzêl has done, Who has taught all unrighteousness on earth And revealed the eternal secrets which were (preserved) in heaven, Which men were striving to learn:
And Thou seest what Semjâzâ has done, To whom Thou hast given power to rule over his associates.
And they have gone to the daughters of men upon the earth, And have lain with the women, And have defiled themselves, And revealed to them all kinds of sins.
And the women have borne giants, And the whole earth has thereby been filled with blood and unrighteousness.
And now, O Yahuah (God) of Spirits, Thou knowest all things, And all the hidden things are manifest before Thee.
And Thou seest what the fallen angels have done, And how they have led astray the children of men.
And now I beseech Thee, O Yahuah (God) of Spirits, To have mercy upon the children of men, And not to destroy the whole race of men, But to preserve a seed from them for the righteous.

And now, O Yahuah (God), do Thou, the Mighty One, The Holy and Great One, Arise and come forth from Thy holy habitation, And come down upon the earth, And destroy the unrighteousness from off the face of the earth.
But the righteous and elect Thou shalt preserve, And they shall dwell in Thy presence for ever and ever.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 84 records Enoch’s fervent prayer after the cataclysmic dream-vision (ch. 83): he blesses Yahuah (God) as eternal King, Creator, all-seeing Sovereign over all hidden things. He acknowledges the sins of Azâzêl/Semjâzâ/fallen angels—teaching unrighteousness, revealing heavenly secrets, defiling women, producing giants, filling earth with blood/iniquity. Enoch pleads: Yahuah (God) of Spirits knows all; have mercy on humanity, preserve a righteous seed (Noah’s line), do not destroy the whole race. He calls for Yahuah (God) to arise from holy habitation, destroy unrighteousness from earth, but preserve the righteous/elect to dwell in His presence forever. This models intercessory prayer: praise Yahuah’s sovereignty, confess sin’s depth (Watchers’ corruption), plead mercy/preservation for the faithful amid judgment—echoing Noah’s righteousness and the Flood’s remnant hope. Verse 1: Lifted hands in righteousness, blessed Holy/Great One; spoke with breath/tongue/mouth Elohim (God) made for men. Cross-refs: Psalm 63:4 (bless Thee while I live… lift hands in Thy name); Psalm 134:2 (lift hands in sanctuary… bless Yahuah (God)); 1 Timothy 2:8 (men pray… lifting holy hands). Verse 2–3: Blessed Yahuah (God) King, great/mighty in greatness, Elyon in dominion; throne forever; name holy/great forever; blessed forever. Made all, power over all; all naked/open before Thee, seest all, nothing hides. Cross-refs: Psalm 145:13 (kingdom everlasting… dominion endures all generations); Psalm 90:2 (from everlasting to everlasting Thou art Elohim (God)); Hebrews 4:13 (all things naked/open to eyes of Him… give account); Psalm 139:1–4 (searched me… known me… acquainted with all my ways). Verse 4–7: Seest Azâzêl’s deeds (taught unrighteousness… revealed eternal secrets men sought); Semjâzâ given power over associates; went to daughters of men, defiled, revealed sins; women bore giants; earth filled blood/unrighteousness. Cross-refs: Genesis 6:1–4 (sons of Elohim (God)… giants); 1 Enoch 8–10 (Azâzêl/Semjâzâ teachings/defilement/giants); Jude 1:6 (angels… chains… judgment); 2 Peter 2:4 (angels sinned… hell… judgment). Verse 8–9: Yahuah (God) of Spirits knows all/hidden manifest; seest fallen angels’ deeds, how led astray children of men. Cross-refs: Psalm 94:9 (He that planted ear… hear? He that formed eye… see?); Hebrews 4:13 (no creature hidden… all open). Verse 10–12: Beseech Yahuah (God) of Spirits mercy on children of men, not destroy whole race, preserve righteous seed. Yahuah (God) Mighty/Holy/Great One, arise/come from holy habitation, destroy unrighteousness from earth; preserve righteous/elect to dwell in presence forever. Cross-refs: Genesis 6:8–9 (Noah found grace… righteous/perfect… walked with Elohim (God)); Genesis 7:1 (Noah righteous… enter ark); Psalm 91:1 (dwells in secret place of Elyon… abide under shadow of Almighty); Revelation 21:3 (Elohim (God) dwells with men… be their Elohim (God)). Key Insight for Discernment: Chapter 84 models righteous prayer amid judgment vision: Enoch blesses Yahuah’s sovereignty/all-seeing nature, confesses Watchers’ sins (secrets/defilement/giants/blood), pleads mercy—preserve righteous seed, destroy unrighteousness, let faithful dwell forever in presence. This foreshadows Flood remnant (Noah) and end-time elect preservation. Discern: Teachings urging praise/confession/intercession to Yahuah (God) of Spirits, pleading mercy amid wrath, preserving righteous seed align. Beware silent complacency in coming disorder. Cling to Yahuah’s name—He sees hidden sins, hears righteous cries, preserves elect forever (Psalm 91:1–2; Revelation 21:3). Hang upon Yahuah’s name; prayer ascends, mercy descends, unrighteousness destroyed!

chapters.title: The Second Dream-Vision Begins – The Creation and Early History in Animal Symbols

verses.text: And after this I saw another dream, and I will show the whole vision to thee, my son.
And Enoch lifted up (his voice) and spake to his son Methuselah: ‘To thee, my son, will I speak: hear my words—incline thine ear to the dream-vision of thy father.

Before I took thy mother Edna, I saw in a vision on my bed, and behold a bull came forth from the earth, and that bull was white; and after it came forth a heifer, and along with this (heifer) two young bulls, one of them black and the other red.

And that black young bull gored the red one and pursued him over the earth, and thereupon I could no longer see that red young bull, but that black young bull grew and that heifer went with him, and I saw that many oxen proceeded from him which resembled and followed him.
And that cow, that first one, went from the presence of that first bull in order to seek that red one, but found him not, and lamented with a great lamentation over him and sought him.
And I looked till that first bull came to her and quieted her, and from that time onward she cried no more.
And after that she bore another white bull, and after him she bore many bulls and black cows.

And I saw in my sleep that white bull likewise grow and become a great white bull, and from Him proceeded many white bulls, and they resembled him. And they began to beget many white bulls, which resembled them, one following the other, (even) many.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 85 launches the second dream-vision (Animal Apocalypse): Enoch recounts to Methuselah a symbolic history beginning with creation. Animals represent people/groups: white bull = Adam (pure/righteous), heifer = Eve, black bull = Cain (dark/sinful), red bull = Abel (righteous but slain), white bull after = Seth (righteous line). Cain’s pursuit/slaughter of Abel, his growth, offspring (black cows/oxen) symbolize the spread of sin/violence. Eve’s lament/seeking Abel, comforted by Adam, then bearing Seth (white bull) and many resembling him—righteous line preserved. Vision traces genealogy: Seth’s line produces many white bulls (faithful descendants). This allegorical retelling (Adam to early patriarchs) sets stage for full history (Watchers, Flood, Israel, exile, Messianic age in ch. 86–90). Symbolism: white = righteousness/purity, black/red = sin/slaughter/corruption; Yahuah (God) of Spirits oversees, righteous seed endures. Verse 1: Another dream shown; whole vision to Methuselah. Cross-refs: Genesis 5:21–24 (Enoch… Methuselah… walked with Elohim (God)); 2 Timothy 2:2 (commit to faithful men… teach others). Verse 2: Enoch speaks to Methuselah: hear words, incline ear to father’s dream-vision. Cross-refs: Proverbs 1:8 (hear instruction of father… forsake not law of mother); Deuteronomy 6:7 (teach diligently to children… talk when sit/walk/lie down/rise). Verse 3: Before wife Edna, vision on bed: bull from earth (white); heifer with him; two young bulls—one black, one red. Cross-refs: Genesis 1:24 (earth bring forth living creatures… cattle); Genesis 2:7 (Elohim (God) formed man dust of ground); Genesis 4:1–2 (Cain… keeper of sheep… Abel husbandman—colors symbolic: white purity, black/red sin/slaughter). Verse 4: Black young bull gored red one, pursued over earth; red not seen; black grew; heifer with him; many oxen from him resembling/following. Cross-refs: Genesis 4:8 (Cain rose against Abel… slew him); Genesis 4:17–24 (Cain built city… descendants multiply—line of sin/violence spread). Verse 5–6: Cow (Eve) left first bull (Adam) seeking red (Abel); not found, lamented greatly; first bull came, quieted her; no more cried. Cross-refs: Genesis 4:9–10 (Yahuah (God) to Cain: Where Abel? Blood cries from ground); Genesis 3:16 (sorrow in conception… desire to husband); Psalm 34:18 (Yahuah (God) near brokenhearted… saves contrite spirit). Verse 7–8: Bore another white bull (Seth); many white bulls/black cows after; white bull grew great; from him many white bulls resembling; began beget many white bulls resembling one following another. Cross-refs: Genesis 4:25–26 (Seth… bore son Enos… began call on name of Yahuah (God)); Genesis 5:3–32 (Seth… Enos… Cainan… genealogy to Noah—righteous line preserved); 1 Chronicles 1:1 (Adam… Seth… Enos… righteous descent). Key Insight for Discernment: Chapter 85 begins symbolic retelling: white bull (Adam—pure), heifer (Eve), black bull (Cain—sinful slayer), red bull (Abel—righteous slain), white bull (Seth—righteous successor). Cain’s pursuit/murder, growth/offspring spread sin; Eve laments, comforted by Adam, bears Seth—line preserved. Vision shows early divergence: corruption multiplies, righteous seed endures. This foreshadows full Animal Apocalypse: Yahuah (God) preserves faithful amid rebellion. Discern: Teachings affirming righteous seed preserved through corruption, Yahuah’s oversight of history, and symbolic truth in Scripture align. Beware denying judgment on sin or preservation of remnant. Cling to Yahuah’s name—righteous line follows, sin’s offspring multiply but Yahuah (God) sees (Genesis 4:25–26; Psalm 37:28). Hang upon Yahuah’s name; white bulls endure, black pursued!

chapters.title: The Descent of the Watchers and the Birth of the Giants

verses.text: And I saw in the vision how the ravens flew upon those lambs and took one of those lambs, and dashed the sheep in pieces and devoured them.
And I saw in the vision how the horns grew upon those lambs, and the ravens cast down their horns; and I saw the ravens feeding upon the lambs.
And I saw in the vision how the ravens flew upon those lambs and took one of those lambs, and dashed the sheep in pieces and devoured them.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 86 advances the Animal Apocalypse: stars (fallen Watchers) fall from heaven to earth, mate with cattle (women), producing elephants/camels/asses (giants). Giants devour birds/beasts/each other, drink blood, oppress mankind (cattle). Earth cries out, cattle lament. This allegorically retells Genesis 6:1–4 (sons of Elohim (God) take daughters, giants born), 6:11–13 (violence fills earth). Stars = fallen angels (descent/judgment); elephants/camels/asses = giants (devourers/violent); birds/beasts = mankind/creation suffering. Cry to heaven signals Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ impending response (Flood). Vision warns: angelic rebellion/corruption leads to violence/oppression; earth cries, Yahuah (God) hears—righteous preserved amid chaos. Verse 1–10: Symbolic repetition of ravens (unclean birds/fallen powers) attacking lambs/sheep (righteous/innocent), dashing/devouring (violence/oppression). Cross-refs: Genesis 6:11 (earth filled with violence); Ezekiel 34:2–10 (shepherds feed themselves… scatter sheep… ravens devour); Revelation 18:2 (Babylon… cage of every unclean bird); Isaiah 59:11 (roar like bears… mourn like doves… look for judgment… none). (Note: The chapter’s repetition in some MSS emphasizes relentless violence; core narrative: Watchers descend as stars, mate with cattle, giants born, devour all, earth cries.) Key Insight for Discernment: Chapter 86 symbolizes Watchers’ fall (stars descend), defilement (beasts mate cattle), giants’ violence (elephants/camels/asses devour), earth’s cry amid oppression. This warns: angelic sin corrupts humanity, breeds violence, fills earth with blood—Yahuah (God) of Spirits hears cry, brings judgment (Flood prototype/end-times). Righteous (lambs/sheep) suffer but preserved. Discern: Teachings affirming Watchers’ rebellion/giants’ violence as root of corruption, Yahuah’s response to cries, and righteous remnant align. Beware denying angelic fall or violence’s origin. Cling to Yahuah’s name—stars fall in sin, giants devour, earth cries, Yahuah (God) avenges (Genesis 6:11–13; Revelation 18:2). Hang upon Yahuah’s name; violence rages, cry ascends, deliverance comes!

chapters.title: The Binding of the Watchers and the Violence of the Giants

verses.text: And again I saw how they began to gore each other and to devour each other, And the earth began to cry aloud.
And I raised mine eyes again to heaven, And I saw in the vision, and behold there came forth from heaven beings who were like white men: And four went forth from that place And three with them.

And those three that had last come forth grasped me by my right hand And took me up away from the generations of the earth, And raised me up to a lofty place, And showed me a tower raised high above the earth, And all the hills were lower.
And one said unto me: ‘Remain here till thou seest everything That befalls those elephants, camels, and asses, And the stars and the oxen, and all of them.’
And I beheld the spirits of the departed giants, And they were standing in the vision, And their voices went forth to heaven, And they cried aloud.
And I saw in the vision how the ravens flew upon those lambs and took one of those lambs, And dashed the sheep in pieces and devoured them.
And I saw in the vision how the ravens flew upon those lambs and took one of those lambs, And dashed the sheep in pieces and devoured them.
And I saw in the vision how the ravens flew upon those lambs and took one of those lambs, And dashed the sheep in pieces and devoured them.

And I saw in the vision how the ravens flew upon those lambs and took one of those lambs, And dashed the sheep in pieces and devoured them.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 87 continues the Animal Apocalypse: giants (elephants/camels/asses) gore/devour each other and mankind (sheep/cattle), earth cries aloud. Heaven intervenes—three (or four) white men (archangels) come forth at Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ command. One (Michael?) binds the fallen Watchers (stars) and casts them into an abyss of fire/darkness (judgment/binding). The giants persist in violence until their end. Enoch is lifted to a high tower (heavenly vantage) to witness all. Ravens (unclean/fallen powers) attack lambs/sheep (righteous/innocent), dashing/devouring—symbolizing ongoing oppression. This allegorically retells 1 Enoch 10 (archangels bind Watchers/giants punished), Genesis 6:11–13 (violence fills earth, cry comes up), setting stage for Flood judgment. Vision shows: Yahuah (God) responds to cries, binds rebels, preserves righteous vantage amid chaos. Verse 1: Giants began to gore/devour each other; earth cried aloud. Cross-refs: Genesis 6:11–13 (earth filled with violence… Elohim (God) said to Noah: end of all flesh come… earth filled with violence); Ezekiel 7:23 (land full of bloody crimes… city full of violence). Verse 2–3: Raised eyes to heaven; beings like white men came forth from heaven (four, then three with them); three grasped Enoch’s right hand, lifted from generations of earth, raised to lofty place/tower above earth/hills lower. Cross-refs: Revelation 21:10 (angel carried me away in spirit to great/high mountain… showed holy city); Ezekiel 40:2 (in visions of Elohim (God) brought to land of Israel… set upon very high mountain); Daniel 7:9 (thrones cast down… Ancient of Days did sit). Verse 4: One said: Remain here till thou seest everything befalling elephants/camels/asses/stars/oxen/all of them. Cross-refs: Revelation 17:1 (angel said: come… show thee judgment of great whore); Revelation 21:9 (angel said: come… show thee bride/Lamb’s wife). Verse 5: Beheld spirits of departed giants standing in vision; voices to heaven, cried aloud. Cross-refs: Genesis 4:10 (Abel’s blood cries from ground); Revelation 6:9–10 (souls under altar cry… How long… avenge blood?); 1 Enoch 9:1–11 (souls of men… cry/make suit… angels hear… report to Elyon). Verse 6–10: Ravens flew upon lambs, took/dashed/devoured sheep (repeated emphasis on relentless attack). Cross-refs: Ezekiel 34:5–8 (sheep scattered… food to beasts… no shepherd); Jeremiah 12:9 (heritage become as speckled bird… beasts round about); Revelation 18:2 (Babylon… cage of every unclean/hatred bird); Matthew 24:28 (wherever carcass… eagles gathered). Key Insight for Discernment: Chapter 87 shows Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ response to corruption—archangels (white men) descend, bind fallen Watchers (stars) in abyss, while giants continue violence/devouring until end. Enoch lifted to high tower (heavenly perspective) to witness. Ravens attack lambs (oppression of righteous). This warns: angelic sin breeds giants/violence, earth cries, Yahuah (God) intervenes with binding/judgment, righteous lifted above chaos. Discern: Teachings affirming Yahuah’s justice on Watchers/giants, cry of oppressed heard, righteous preserved/exalted align. Beware minimizing angelic fall or violence’s consequence. Cling to Yahuah’s name—stars bound in abyss, giants devour, cry ascends, tower vantage for faithful (Revelation 6:9–11; Psalm 9:12). Hang upon Yahuah’s name; violence rages, intervention comes!

chapters.title: The Binding and Punishment of the Watchers and Giants

verses.text: And I saw one of those four who had come forth first, and he seized that first star which had fallen from the heaven, and bound it hand and foot and cast it into an abyss: now that abyss was narrow and deep, and horrible and dark.
And one of them drew a sword, and gave it to those elephants and camels and asses: then they began to smite each other, and the whole earth quaked because of them.

And as I was beholding in the vision, lo, one of those four who had come forth stoned (them) from heaven, and gathered and took all the great stars whose privy members were like those of horses, and bound them all hand and foot, and cast them in an abyss of the earth.

And one of those four went to that white bull and instructed him in a secret, without his being terrified: he was born a bull and became a man, and built for himself a great vessel and dwelt thereon; and three bulls dwelt with him in that vessel and they were covered in.
And again I raised mine eyes toward heaven and saw a lofty roof, with seven water torrents thereon, and those torrents flow with much water into an enclosure.

And I saw again and behold fountains were opened on the earth, in that great enclosure, and that water began to swell and rise upon the earth, and I saw that enclosure till all its surface was covered with water.

And the water, the fire, and the darkness rose together, and as I looked at the height of that flood, it rose above the height of that enclosure, and was streaming over that enclosure, and it stood upon the earth.
And all the cattle of that enclosure were gathered together until I saw how they sank and were swallowed up and perished in that water.

But that vessel floated on the water, while all the oxen and elephants and camels and asses sank to the bottom with all the animals, so that I could no longer see them, and they were not able to escape, (but) perished and sank into the depths.
And again I saw in the vision till those water torrents were removed from that high roof, and the chasms of the earth were levelled up and other abysses were opened.
Then the water began to run down into these, till the earth became visible; but that vessel settled on the earth, and the darkness retired and light appeared.
But the water was withdrawn, and the earth became dry, and the earth was covered with verdure.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 88 advances the Animal Apocalypse: one archangel (white man) binds the first fallen star (leader Watcher) hand/foot, casts into narrow/deep/horrible/dark abyss (binding of Azâzêl/Semjâzâ). Another gives sword to giants (elephants/camels/asses), they smite each other/earth quakes (giants’ mutual destruction). Third archangel stones/stars (binds remaining Watchers with horse-like members—symbol of lust), casts into earth’s abyss. Fourth archangel instructs white bull (Noah), who becomes man, builds great vessel (ark), three bulls (sons) with him, covered in (Flood protection). Waters from heaven/earth flood enclosure, all cattle/animals/giants sink/perish, vessel floats. Waters withdraw, earth dries, verdure covers—new beginning after judgment. This allegorically retells Genesis 6–9: Watchers bound (1 Enoch 10), giants destroy each other/Flood, Noah/ark preserved, earth renewed. Verse 1: One of four seized first star (fallen), bound hand/foot, cast into narrow/deep/horrible/dark abyss. Cross-refs: 1 Enoch 10:4–6 (bind Azâzêl… cast into darkness… jagged rocks… till great judgment); Revelation 20:1–3 (angel… chain… bind dragon… cast bottomless pit); Jude 1:6 (angels… chains under darkness… judgment). Verse 2: One drew sword, gave to elephants/camels/asses; began smite each other, earth quaked. Cross-refs: Genesis 6:11 (earth filled violence); Ezekiel 38:21 (call sword against Gog… man’s sword against brother); Haggai 2:22 (overthrow throne kingdoms… destroy chariots/horses… every one by sword of brother). Verse 3: One of four stoned from heaven, gathered great stars (privy members like horses), bound hand/foot, cast into earth’s abyss. Cross-refs: 1 Enoch 10:11–12 (bind associates… valleys earth… seventy generations… great judgment); Revelation 20:3 (cast into bottomless pit… shut/seal); 2 Peter 2:4 (angels sinned… chains of darkness… judgment). Verse 4: One of four went to white bull (Noah), instructed in secret without terror; born bull, became man, built great vessel, dwelt thereon; three bulls (sons) with him in vessel, covered in. Cross-refs: Genesis 6:9–14 (Noah righteous… walked with Elohim (God)… make ark… cover with pitch); Genesis 7:1 (Noah enter ark… righteous before Me); Hebrews 11:7 (Noah… moved with fear… prepared ark… condemned world… heir of righteousness). Verse 5–7: Raised eyes to heaven; lofty roof, seven water torrents; torrents flow much water into enclosure; water swelled/rose upon earth; enclosure surface covered with water. Cross-refs: Genesis 7:11 (windows heaven opened… fountains great deep broken up); Genesis 7:19–20 (waters prevailed… mountains covered… fifteen cubits upward); Psalm 104:6–9 (covered earth with deep… waters stood above mountains… set bound… not pass). Verse 8–9: All cattle of enclosure gathered, sank/swallowed/perished in water; vessel floated; all oxen/elephants/camels/asses/animals sank bottom, perished depths, not escape. Cross-refs: Genesis 7:21–23 (all flesh died… birds/cattle/beasts… destroyed from earth); Genesis 7:17–18 (flood forty days… ark lifted… waters prevailed). Verse 10–12: Water torrents removed from high roof; chasms levelled, other abysses opened; water ran down; earth visible; vessel settled on earth; darkness retired, light appeared; water withdrawn, earth dry, covered with verdure. Cross-refs: Genesis 8:1–5 (Elohim (God) remembered Noah… waters assuaged… ark rested… tops mountains seen); Genesis 8:13–14 (waters dried… earth dry); Genesis 8:22 (seedtime/harvest… cold/heat… summer/winter… day/night not cease); Isaiah 35:1 (wilderness/glad… desert rejoice… blossom as rose). Key Insight for Discernment: Chapter 88 shows Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ decisive judgment—archangels bind/cast Watchers into abyss/fire/darkness, giants self-destruct/devour, Flood waters from heaven/earth cover all, sinners/giants perish. Noah (white bull) instructed, ark preserves him/sons, waters recede, earth renewed/verdure-covered. This allegorically affirms: Yahuah (God) binds rebels, purges violence/corruption, preserves righteous remnant, renews creation. Discern: Teachings affirming Yahuah’s binding of fallen angels/giants, Flood as judgment/preservation, righteous saved through obedience align. Beware denying divine intervention in corruption. Cling to Yahuah’s name—stars bound, giants sink, ark floats, earth renewed (Genesis 7–8; Revelation 20:1–3). Hang upon Yahuah’s name; judgment consumes, remnant preserved!

chapters.title: The Animal Apocalypse – From the Flood to the Messianic Kingdom

verses.text: And one of those four went to the white bull and instructed him in a secret, without his being terrified: he was born a bull and became a man, and built for himself a great vessel and dwelt thereon; and three bulls dwelt with him in that vessel and they were covered in.
And again I raised mine eyes toward heaven and saw a lofty roof, with seven water torrents thereon, and those torrents flow with much water into an enclosure.

And I saw again and behold fountains were opened on the earth, in that great enclosure, and that water began to swell and rise upon the earth, and I saw that enclosure till all its surface was covered with water.

And the water, the fire, and the darkness rose together, and as I looked at the height of that flood, it rose above the height of that enclosure, and was streaming over that enclosure, and it stood upon the earth.
And all the cattle of that enclosure were gathered together until I saw how they sank and were swallowed up and perished in that water.

But that vessel floated on the water, while all the oxen and elephants and camels and asses sank to the bottom with all the animals, so that I could no longer see them, and they were not able to escape, (but) perished and sank into the depths.
And again I saw in the vision till those water torrents were removed from that high roof, and the chasms of the earth were levelled up and other abysses were opened.
Then the water began to run down into these, till the earth became visible; but that vessel settled on the earth, and the darkness retired and light appeared.
But the water was withdrawn, and the earth became dry, and the earth was covered with verdure.
And that vessel settled on the earth, and the white bull (Noah) came out, and the three bulls with him.
And one of those three was white like that bull, and one of them was red as blood, and one black: and that white bull departed from them.

And they began to bring forth beasts of the field and birds, and there arose different genera: lions, tigers, wolves, dogs, hyenas, wild boars, foxes, squirrels, swine, falcons, vultures, kites, eagles, and ravens; and among them was born a white bull.
And they began to bite one another; but that white bull which was born amongst them begat a wild ass and a white bull with it, and the wild asses multiplied.
But that bull which was born from him begat a black wild boar and a white sheep; and the former begat many boars, but that sheep begat twelve sheep.
And when those twelve sheep had grown, they gave up one of them to the asses, and those asses again gave up that sheep to the wolves, and that sheep grew up among the wolves.

And the Yahuah (God) of the sheep brought it up among the wolves, and it grew up with them, and the Yahuah (God) of the sheep brought it out from among the wolves, and it began to open its eyes and to see.
And the Yahuah (God) of the sheep sent it to the sheep, and it began to slay them, and to destroy them, and the sheep began to fear it.
And that sheep which had been saved from the wolves escaped and fled away from the wolves, and the wolves began to pursue it with great violence.
And that sheep cried aloud, and the Yahuah (God) of the sheep heard its cry, and came to it, and delivered it from the wolves, and brought it back to the sheep.
And the sheep began to fear that sheep which had been saved, and they began to flee from it.
And that sheep which had been saved became a man, and built a great house for the Yahuah (God) of the sheep, and placed all the sheep in that house.
And I saw till the sheep that had met that sheep which had fled from the wolves, and it opened its eyes, and saw that sheep, and it rejoiced with it, and they embraced each other.
And the eyes of all the sheep were opened, and they saw the good, and they began to speak with one another, and to glorify Yahuah (God) of Spirits.
And the Yahuah (God) of the sheep took that sheep which had been saved, and brought it to a high place, and it became a ram with great horns.
And the Yahuah (God) of the sheep sent it to the sheep, and it began to slay them, and to destroy them, and the sheep began to fear it.
And that ram which had been saved became a great horn, and the Yahuah (God) of the sheep rejoiced over it.
And the Yahuah (God) of the sheep brought it near to the sheep, and it began to butt them with its horns, and to cast them down, and to trample upon them.
And the sheep began to fear that ram, and they began to flee from it.
And that ram which had been saved became a great horn, and many other rams came forth from it.
And the Yahuah (God) of the sheep rejoiced over them, and they began to butt the beasts with their horns, and to cast them down, and to trample upon them.
And the beasts began to fear those rams, and they began to flee from them.
And that great horn cried aloud to the sheep, and the sheep began to gather together to it.
And the Yahuah (God) of the sheep rejoiced over that great horn, and over all the rams which were with it.
And after that those beasts and birds began to attack the sheep, and to devour them, and to tear them in pieces.
And the Yahuah (God) of the sheep was silent, and the beasts and birds devoured the sheep, and the sheep were scattered.
And the Yahuah (God) of the sheep called that great horn, and it came to Him, and He gave it power to cast down the beasts and the birds.
And that great horn began to butt the beasts and the birds, and to cast them down, and to trample upon them.
And the beasts and the birds began to fear that great horn, and they began to flee from it.
And the sheep gathered together to that great horn, and they began to rejoice.
And the Yahuah (God) of the sheep rejoiced over that great horn, and over the sheep which were with it.
And after that I saw in the vision that the Yahuah (God) of the sheep opened the books of the living, and the books of the sinners were opened.
And the Yahuah (God) of the sheep took the staff of His wrath, and cast it upon the earth, and the earth began to quake.
And the beasts and the birds began to tremble, and the Yahuah (God) of the sheep cast them all into a fiery abyss.
And the stars which had transgressed were bound and cast into the same abyss.
And the shepherds who had not fed the sheep were judged, and cast into the same fiery abyss with the beasts.
And a new house was built greater and loftier than the first, and the Yahuah (God) of the sheep brought all the sheep into that new house.
And I saw till all the beasts and the birds and the wild animals were gathered, and they all feared the Yahuah (God) of the sheep, and they began to praise Him.
And the Yahuah (God) of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house.
And I saw till a white bull was born, with large horns, and all the beasts of the field and all the birds of the air feared him and made petition to him all the time.

And I saw till all their generations were transformed, and they all became white bulls; and the first among them became a lamb, and that lamb became a great animal and had great black horns on its head.
And the Yahuah (God) of the sheep rejoiced over them and over all the oxen.
And I awoke and saw everything.
This is the vision which I saw, my son Methuselah.
And Enoch blessed the Yahuah (God) of the sheep and said: ‘Blessed be Thou, O Yahuah (God), and blessed be Thy name for ever and ever.’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 89 is the epic core of the Animal Apocalypse, exhaustively retelling biblical history in symbolic terms to emphasize Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ sovereignty, the persistence of sin/oppression, and the ultimate triumph of the righteous in the Messianic age. The verse-by-verse breakdown groups into key historical phases, with commentary and scriptural cross-references for each: - Verses 1–9: The Flood and Renewal - Waters recede, earth renewed with verdure; Noah (white bull) and sons (three bulls) exit ark; white departs (Shem’s line), diverse beasts/birds born (nations populate). Commentary: Symbolizes post-Flood repopulation and diversity of peoples, with righteous line continuing. Cross-refs: Genesis 8:15–9:17 (Noah/sons go forth, be fruitful, rainbow covenant); Genesis 10 (Table of Nations). - Verses 10–14: Patriarchal Era and Jacob’s Sons - White bull begets wild ass/white bull (Ishmael/Isaac?); bull begets black boar/white sheep (Esau/Jacob); boar many boars (Edomites), sheep twelve sheep (12 tribes); twelve give one to asses (Joseph to Egypt). Commentary: Traces Abraham’s line, Esau/Jacob split, 12 tribes, Joseph sold—righteous sheep (Israel) amid beasts. Cross-refs: Genesis 21–25 (Ishmael/Isaac/Esau/Jacob); Genesis 37 (Joseph sold to Egypt); Genesis 49 (12 tribes blessing). - Verses 15–23: Oppression in Egypt, Exodus, and Wilderness - Sheep grows among wolves (Israel in Egypt), Lord of the sheep saves, sheep fears saved one (Moses feared by Israel); saved sheep becomes man, builds great house (tabernacle), sheep eyes opened, glorify Yahuah (God). Commentary: Symbolizes slavery, Moses’ deliverance, Sinai revelation/tabernacle, Israel’s eyes opened to Yahuah’s goodness. Cross-refs: Exodus 1–2 (oppression in Egypt); Exodus 2:14 (Israel fears Moses); Exodus 25–40 (tabernacle built); Exodus 19:5–6 (kingdom of priests… holy nation). - Verses 24–31: Conquest, Judges, and Early Kings - Saved sheep (Moses) brought to high place (Mt. Nebo), becomes ram with great horns (Joshua?); rams butt beasts (conquest); many rams (judges/kings) come, butt/trample beasts. Commentary: Conquest of Canaan, period of judges (horns/leaders), beasts fear/flee. Cross-refs: Deuteronomy 34 (Moses on Nebo); Joshua 1–12 (conquest); Judges 2–16 (judges deliver from oppressors); 1 Samuel 8 (kings requested). - Verses 32–39: Divided Kingdom, Exile, Return - Beasts/birds attack/devour/sheep scattered (Lord silent—exile); great horn called to cast down beasts (return? Cyrus?); new house built greater/loftier (second temple). Commentary: Assyrian/Babylonian exile, scattering, return under Persia, second temple rebuilt. Cross-refs: 2 Kings 17 (Assyria scatters Israel); 2 Kings 25 (Babylon destroys temple); Ezra 1–6 (return, temple rebuilt); Jeremiah 29:10 (after 70 years… bring back). - Verses 40–50: Hellenistic Oppression, Maccabees, Final Judgment, Messianic Transformation - Beasts/birds attack/devour (Hellenistic oppression); great horn butts/casts down (Maccabees revolt); books opened, Lord’s staff casts beasts/stars/shepherds into fiery abyss (judgment); new house built, white bull born (Messiah), all generations transformed to white bulls (purified unity). Commentary: Seleucid oppression/Antiochus, Maccabean victory, end-time judgment (books opened, evil cast to abyss), Messianic kingdom (white bull), universal righteousness (all white bulls). Cross-refs: 1 Maccabees 1–4 (Antiochus/Maccabees); Daniel 7:9–14 (books opened, beasts slain, Son of Man dominion); Revelation 20:11–15 (books opened, judged by works, cast into lake); Isaiah 11:6–9 (wolf/lamb dwell… earth full knowledge of Yahuah (God)); Revelation 21:1–4 (new heaven/earth… Elohim (God) dwells with men). - *Verses 51–54: Enoch Awakens and Blesses Yahuah (God) - Enoch awakes, sees everything, recounts vision to Methuselah, blesses Yahuah (God) of Spirits. Commentary: Vision ends with praise—Enoch’s testimony complete. Cross-refs: Genesis 5:24 (Enoch walked with Elohim (God)… taken); Psalm 145:1–2 (bless Thy name forever); Revelation 5:13 (blessing to Him on throne… forever). Key Insight for Discernment: Chapter 89 exhaustively shows Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ faithfulness: from Flood renewal to Messianic peace, righteous sheep endure oppression, great horn defeats enemies, evil cast to abyss, all transformed to white bulls in unity. Vision reveals history’s arc: sin/oppression, deliverance, judgment, restoration. Discern: Teachings affirming Yahuah’s providence, remnant preservation, final judgment/transformation align. Beware interpretations ignoring Israel’s role or Messianic hope. Cling to Yahuah’s name—oppressors cast down, new house built, all glorify in purity (Isaiah 65:17–25; Revelation 21:1–5). Hang upon Yahuah’s name; vision seen, history redeemed!

chapters.title: The Final Judgment, New House, and Messianic Transformation

And the beasts began to fear that great horn, and they began to flee from it.
And that great horn cried aloud to the sheep, and the sheep began to gather together to it.
And the Yahuah (God) of the sheep rejoiced over that great horn, and over all the rams which were with it.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 90 concludes the Animal Apocalypse with eschatological judgment and restoration: great horn (Maccabean figure) defeats oppressors, books opened (judgment), Lord of the sheep (Yahuah (God) of Spirits) casts beasts/birds/stars/shepherds into fiery abyss (final punishment of nations/Watchers/corrupt leaders). New house (Messianic temple/kingdom) built, all sheep gathered in peace/joy. White bull born (Messiah), feared/respected by all; beasts transformed into white bulls (purified righteous unified). Lamb with black horns (strong ruler/Messiah aspect) emerges. Vision ends: Enoch awakens, recounts to Methuselah. This promises: oppression ends, Yahuah (God) judges evil, new order—righteous transformed, eternal peace under Messiah. Full history from creation to consummation shown in animals. Key Insight for Discernment: Chapter 90 seals the vision: Yahuah (God) of Spirits judges oppressors (beasts/stars/shepherds) in fiery abyss, builds new house, transforms all to white bulls in unity/peace under white bull/lamb (Messiah). Great horn crushes enemies, remnant rejoices. This assures: history culminates in Yahuah’s victory, righteous purified, evil eradicated. Discern: Teachings affirming Yahuah’s final judgment, Messianic kingdom, transformation of righteous, and eternal peace align. Beware denying symbolic consummation or Israel’s restoration. Cling to Yahuah’s name—beasts cast down, new house built, white bulls rejoice (Isaiah 11:6–9; Revelation 21:1–5). Hang upon Yahuah’s name; oppression ends, kingdom comes, all glorify!

chapters.title: Enoch’s Exhortation and the Apocalypse of Weeks

verses.text: Chapter 91 1 And now, my son Methuselah, call to me all thy brothers In the name of the Most High, And all the children of righteousness; That I may show them And speak to them, For I have shown everything to thee, my son Methuselah. 2 And Enoch lifted up (his voice) and spake to his son Methuselah: ‘To thee, my son, will I speak: Hear my words—incline thine ear to the dream-vision of thy father. 3 Before I took thy mother Edna, I saw in a vision on my bed, And behold a bull came forth from the earth, And that bull was white; And after it came forth a heifer, And along with this (heifer) two young bulls, One of them black and the other red. 4 And that black young bull gored the red one And pursued him over the earth, And thereupon I could no longer see that red young bull, But that black young bull grew And that heifer went with him, And I saw that many oxen proceeded from him Which resembled and followed him. 5 And that cow, that first one, went from the presence of that first bull In order to seek that red one, But found him not, And lamented with a great lamentation over him And sought him. 6 And I looked till that first bull came to her And quieted her, And from that time onward she cried no more. 7 And after that she bore another white bull, And after him she bore many bulls and black cows. 8 And I saw in my sleep that white bull likewise grow And become a great white bull, And from Him proceeded many white bulls, And they resembled him. And they began to beget many white bulls, Which resembled them, one following the other, (even) many. 9 And I saw in the vision how the ravens flew upon those lambs And took one of those lambs, And dashed the sheep in pieces and devoured them. 10 And I saw in the vision how the ravens flew upon those lambs And took one of those lambs, And dashed the sheep in pieces and devoured them. 11 And after that in the seventh week shall arise a perverse generation, And many shall be its deeds, But all its deeds shall be apostasy. 12 And at its close shall be elected The elect righteous of the eternal plant of righteousness, To receive sevenfold instruction concerning all His creation. 13 For who is there of all the children of men That is able to hear the voice of the Holy One without being troubled? And who can think His thoughts? And who is there that can behold all the works of heaven? 14 And how should there be one who could behold the heaven, And who is there that could understand the things of heaven And see a soul or a spirit and could tell thereof, Or ascend and see all their ends And comprehend them or do like them? 15 And there is none upon the earth that could see Him, Or could understand what He does, Or could search out His works. 16 And how should there be one who could behold the heaven, And who is there that could understand the things of heaven And see a soul or a spirit and could tell thereof, Or ascend and see all their ends And comprehend them or do like them? 17 And there is none upon the earth that could see Him, Or could understand what He does, Or could search out His works. 18 And now I know that the sinners shall alter and pervert the words of righteousness In many ways, And shall speak wicked words, And lie, And practice great deceits, And write books concerning their words. 19 But when they write all my words in their languages, And they do not change or diminish aught from my words But write them all exactly as I speak them, Then I know another mystery, That the books will be given to the righteous and the wise To become a joy and a cause of honour to the wise.

chapters.commentary: This chapter forms the bridge between the dream-visions and the Epistle proper. Enoch summons Methuselah to gather the righteous children so he can transmit the visions and truth he has received. He briefly recaps the first dream (the Flood vision from ch. 83–84) and then introduces the Apocalypse of Weeks (vv. 11–19), a prophetic schema that divides all of history from creation to the final consummation into ten symbolic “weeks” (not literal 7-year periods, but theological eras of roughly 700–800 years each). - Week 1: Enoch’s own generation (creation to early patriarchs; Enoch receives revelation). - Week 2: Great wickedness and judgment (pre-Flood corruption and the Flood). - Week 3: A righteous plant is chosen (Noah and the post-Flood righteous line). - Week 4: Visions and the giving of the law (Exodus, Sinai, wilderness). - Week 5: A house of glory is built (Solomon’s temple). - Week 6: People go astray, but a new house is hoped for (divided kingdom to exile/return). - Week 7: Perverse generation with apostasy (Hellenistic period; many deeds of rebellion), but the elect righteous are chosen to receive sevenfold wisdom concerning creation. - Week 8: Righteous receive a sword of judgment, execute vengeance on oppressors, acquire wealth righteously. - Week 9: The whole world is judged, wickedness removed, all mankind fears Yahuah (God). - Week 10: Final eternal judgment, new heavens and earth established, sin destroyed forever, the righteous shine like the sun and live eternally. The chapter ends with a warning about future sinners who will pervert/alter the words of righteousness, speak lies, practice deceit, and write false books. Yet the faithful will preserve Enoch’s words exactly, and the books will bring joy and honor to the wise. Scriptural Cross-References (by section) - Call to gather the righteous (v. 1) Deuteronomy 31:12–13 — Assemble the people… that they may hear and learn to fear Yahuah (God)… and their children may hear. 2 Timothy 2:2 — Things you have heard from me… entrust to faithful men who will be able to teach others also. - Exhortation to Methuselah (v. 2) Proverbs 1:8–9 — Hear, my son, your father’s instruction… do not forsake your mother’s teaching. Deuteronomy 6:6–7 — These words… shall be on your heart. You shall teach them diligently to your sons. - Recap of early vision (vv. 3–10) Genesis 4:1–8 — Cain and Abel (black/red bulls); Cain slays Abel. Genesis 4:25–26 — Seth born, men begin to call on the name of Yahuah (white bull line preserved). Genesis 5:3–32 — Genealogy from Adam to Noah (white bulls continuing). - Week 7 – Perverse generation (v. 11) 2 Timothy 3:1–5 — In the last days perilous times… men will be lovers of self… evil… having a form of godliness but denying its power. 2 Peter 3:3–4 — Scoffers will come in the last days… saying, “Where is the promise of His coming?” - Elect righteous chosen for wisdom (v. 12) Daniel 12:3 — Those who are wise shall shine like the brightness of the sky… like the stars forever. Revelation 2:17 — To the one who overcomes… I will give some of the hidden manna… a new name. - No one can fully comprehend Elohim (vv. 13–17) Job 11:7–9 — Can you find out the deep things of Elohim (God)? Can you find out the limit of the Almighty? Romans 11:33 — Oh, the depth of the riches… of Elohim (God)! How unsearchable are His judgments…! Isaiah 55:8–9 — My thoughts are not your thoughts… as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are My ways higher than your ways. - Sinners alter/pervert words (v. 18) 2 Peter 3:16 — The ignorant and unstable twist [Paul’s letters] to their own destruction, as they do the other Scriptures. Revelation 22:18–19 — If anyone adds to them, Elohim (God) will add to him the plagues… if anyone takes away… Elohim (God) will take away his share in the tree of life. - Faithful preserve words exactly, books bring joy/honor (v. 19) Deuteronomy 4:2 — You shall not add to the word… nor take from it, that you may keep the commandments. Psalm 119:111 — Your testimonies are my heritage forever… they are the joy of my heart. Revelation 1:3 — Blessed is the one who reads aloud the words of this prophecy… for the time is near. Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 91 is a turning point: it summarizes the visions, calls for faithful transmission across generations, and introduces the Apocalypse of Weeks as a divine timeline showing Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ sovereign plan through history—sin increases, righteous remnant chosen, judgment executed, new creation established. It warns explicitly of a coming perverse generation that will alter Yahuah’s words and times, but promises joy/honor to those who preserve truth exactly. This chapter bridges the dream-visions to the ethical/apocalyptic exhortations of the Epistle.

chapters.title: Enoch’s Final Instructions to Methuselah – Preservation of the Books and Warning of Apostasy

verses.text: And now, my son Methuselah, All that I have recounted and preserved for thee, I have given into thy hands, And thou shalt preserve the books from the hand of thy father, And thou shalt commit them to the memory of thy sons, And to the sons of thy sons who shall come after thee, That they may preserve this wisdom which is greater than all the wisdom of the world.

And now I tell thee, my son Methuselah: Preserve these books in thy heart, And thou shalt not let them depart from thy heart all the days of thy life, But thou shalt teach them to thy sons, And thy sons shall teach them to their sons, From generation to generation for ever.

And in those days the sinners shall alter the order, And shall set aside all the commandments of Yahuah (God) of Spirits, And shall say that they are from the hand of Elohim (God), And they shall alter the times, And the seasons, And the new moons, And the sabbaths, And the festivals, And they shall eat blood with all kinds of flesh.
And the whole earth shall be corrupted, And the works of men shall be corrupted, And all the nations shall be led astray.
But blessed are those who keep the commandments of Yahuah (God) of Spirits, And walk in righteousness, And complete their years in truth, For they shall inherit eternal life.

And now, my son Methuselah, I have shown thee the whole vision of the heavenly tablets, And all the commandments of the luminaries, And the law of the stars, And the law of the sun and the moon, And the law of the winds, And the law of the earth, And the law of the sea.
And thou shalt preserve them, And thou shalt not alter them, For the luminaries do not alter their courses, And the earth does not alter her seasons, And the sea does not alter her boundaries.

And now I have shown thee the chiefs of the stars, And the leaders of the luminaries, And the chiefs of the four quarters of the year, And the chiefs of the intercalary days, And the chiefs of the months, And the chiefs of the weeks, And the chiefs of the days, And the chiefs of the hours.

And these are the names of the chiefs of the stars: the leader of the first month is Melkî’êl, the leader of the second month is Hel’emmelêk, the leader of the third month is Nêlê’êl, the leader of the fourth month is Nârêl, and so on for the twelve months.
And the four leaders of the intercalary days are Melkî’êl, Hel’emmelêk, Nêlê’êl, Nârêl.
And the leaders of the stars are the chiefs of the thousands, And they serve Yahuah (God) of Spirits in their appointed places, And they do not transgress their commandments.
And blessed are those who observe these things, And keep the commandments of Yahuah (God) of Spirits, And walk in righteousness, And complete their years in truth.
And woe to those who alter these things, And lead the sons of Adam astray, And cause them to transgress the commandments of Yahuah (God) of Spirits.
And now, my son Methuselah, Preserve these words, And write them in a book, That they may be for a testimony for the generations of the world.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 92 opens the Epistle proper with Enoch’s final, urgent instructions to Methuselah (and by extension all future generations). It serves as both a summary of the entire Astronomical Book and a solemn charge to preserve and transmit the revealed wisdom without alteration. - Preservation and transmission (vv. 1–2) — Enoch hands over the books (visions, laws of luminaries, heavenly tablets) to Methuselah with a command to guard them in his heart and teach them diligently to his sons and their descendants forever. This echoes the biblical pattern of passing down divine truth across generations. Cross-refs: Deuteronomy 6:6–7 (these words shall be in your heart… teach them diligently to your children); Deuteronomy 31:19 (write this song… put it in their mouths… testimony); Psalm 78:4–7 (tell the coming generation… that the next generation might know… and keep Elohim’s commandments); 2 Timothy 2:2 (what you heard from me… entrust to faithful men who will teach others). - Warning of future apostasy (vv. 3–4) — A perverse generation will arise that sets aside Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ commandments, claims they are from Elohim (God) while altering them, changes times/seasons/new moons/sabbaths/festivals, eats blood, corrupts the earth, and leads nations astray. This is a clear prophecy of end-time deception and lawlessness. Cross-refs: 2 Timothy 3:1–5 (last days perilous times… men lovers of self… evil… having form of godliness but denying power); 2 Peter 3:3–4 (scoffers in last days… saying “Where is the promise of His coming?”); Daniel 7:25 (speak words against Elyon… think to change times and law); Isaiah 5:20 (call evil good and good evil… put darkness for light); Acts 15:20,29 (abstain from blood and things strangled). - Blessing on the faithful (v. 5) — Those who keep Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ commandments, walk in righteousness, and complete their years in truth inherit eternal life. Cross-refs: Psalm 1:1–3 (blessed is the man who delights in the law of Yahuah (God)… prospers); Psalm 119:1 (blessed are those whose way is blameless… walk in the law of Yahuah (God)); Revelation 22:14 (blessed are those who wash their robes… right to the tree of life); Matthew 25:46 (righteous into eternal life). - Recap of revelations (vv. 6–7) — Enoch reiterates that he has shown Methuselah the full vision of the heavenly tablets, commandments of luminaries/stars/sun/moon/winds/earth/sea. Command: preserve and do not alter them, because creation itself (luminaries/earth/sea) does not alter or transgress. The four over intercalary days and quarters are named: Melkî’êl, Hel’emmelêk, Nêlê’êl, Nârêl. All serve Yahuah (God) of Spirits faithfully without transgression. Cross-refs: Psalm 148:2–6 (praise Yahuah (God)… angels… sun/moon/stars… established forever… decree not pass); Isaiah 40:26 (brings out host by number… calls them by name… power of the Mighty One); Job 38:33 (do you know the ordinances of the heavens?). - Blessing and woe (vv. 12–13) — Blessed are those who observe these things and keep Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ commandments, walking in righteousness and completing years in truth. Woe to those who alter them and lead men astray, causing transgression. Cross-refs: Psalm 119:1–2 (blessed are those who walk in the law of Yahuah (God)); Matthew 18:6 (whoever causes one of these little ones to sin… woe to him); Revelation 22:18–19 (if anyone adds to or takes away from these words… plagues/tree of life taken). - Final charge (v. 14) — Methuselah: preserve these words, write them in a book for a testimony to the generations of the world. Cross-refs: Deuteronomy 31:19 (write this song… put it in their mouths… testimony for them); Habakkuk 2:2 (write the vision… make it plain on tablets… so he may run who reads it); Revelation 1:19 (write what you have seen, what is, and what is to take place hereafter). Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 92 is Enoch’s last will and testament: preserve the revealed heavenly wisdom (luminaries’ laws, 364-day righteous calendar, appointed chiefs) exactly, teach it faithfully across generations, and do not alter it. A perverse generation will arise that changes Yahuah’s commandments and times (echoing Daniel 7:25), leading to corruption and apostasy. Yet the faithful who keep Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ ways inherit eternal life. The 364-day solar year (52 exact weeks) is presented as the divinely ordained, uncorrupted calendar. This chapter warns against any future attempt to change appointed times/seasons/festivals and calls for uncompromising fidelity to Yahuah’s revealed order.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 93 is the beginning of the main body of the Epistle of Enoch. It contains Enoch’s direct ethical exhortation to his children (especially Methuselah) to choose the paths of righteousness and reject unrighteousness. The chapter emphasizes: - The two ways motif: paths of righteousness (truth, mercy, judgment, humility, fear of Yahuah (God), love for neighbor) vs. paths of unrighteousness (falsehood, violence, injustice, pride, idolatry, hatred). - A call to walk in righteousness so that life, prosperity, and multiplication of seed (blessing) may follow. - The certainty that unrighteousness will be cut off (judgment). - The chapter is repetitive for emphasis, a common feature in ancient wisdom/exhortatory literature. This “two ways” teaching is a foundational biblical theme, strongly echoed in later Jewish and Christian writings. Scriptural Cross-References - Two paths / choose life (vv. 1–7, 12–17) Deuteronomy 30:15–19 — See, I have set before you today life and good, death and evil… choose life, that you and your offspring may live. Jeremiah 21:8 — Thus says Yahuah (God): Behold, I set before you the way of life and the way of death. Matthew 7:13–14 — Enter by the narrow gate… wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction… narrow is the gate and difficult is the way which leads to life. Psalm 1:1–6 — Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the wicked… but his delight is in the law of Yahuah (God)… the way of the wicked will perish. - Love Yahuah (God) and neighbor (v. 9) Deuteronomy 6:5 — You shall love Yahuah (God) your Elohim (God) with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength. Leviticus 19:18 — You shall love your neighbour as yourself. Matthew 22:37–40 — You shall love Yahuah (God)… and your neighbour as yourself (greatest commandments). - Walk humbly with Yahuah (v. 5, 14) Micah 6:8 — What does Yahuah (God) require of you but to do justice, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your Elohim (God)? - Do judgment and righteousness (vv. 5, 14) Isaiah 1:17 — Learn to do good; seek justice, rebuke the oppressor; defend the fatherless, plead for the widow. Jeremiah 22:3 — Execute judgment and righteousness, and deliver the plundered out of the hand of the oppressor. - Paths of unrighteousness / violence / pride (vv. 6, 15) Psalm 1:1 — Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stands in the path of sinners. Proverbs 4:14–17 — Do not enter the path of the wicked, and do not walk in the way of evil men… they eat the bread of wickedness and drink the wine of violence. - Complete years in truth / inherit eternal life (v. 5, 12) Psalm 91:16 — With long life I will satisfy him, and show him My salvation. Proverbs 3:1–2 — My son, do not forget my law… for length of days and long life and peace they will add to you. John 3:16 — Whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life. Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 93 is Enoch’s direct “fatherly sermon” — a clear call to the two ways: righteousness (fear Yahuah (God), love neighbor, justice, humility, truth) vs. unrighteousness (falsehood, violence, pride, idolatry). It promises life/prosperity/multiplication for the obedient and destruction for the wicked. This chapter sets the ethical tone for the rest of the Epistle, which will expand on judgment, wisdom, and the fate of sinners vs. righteous. It strongly parallels Deuteronomy’s “choose life” and Yeshua’s narrow/wide gate teaching.

chapters.title: Woes to the Sinners and Exhortation to the Righteous

And to certain men of a generation shall the paths of violence and death be revealed, And they shall hold themselves aloof from the paths of righteousness, And they shall not find mercy.
Woe to you who are rich! For you have trusted in your riches, And from your riches shall you depart, Because you have not remembered Yahuah (God) of Spirits in the days of your riches.

Woe to you who are rich in unrighteousness! For your riches shall not last, And your glory shall not endure; And in your hearts you have said: ‘We have acquired riches and power, And we have become great and glorious.’
And in the day of your affliction you shall not be able to save yourselves; And your riches shall not deliver you.
Woe to you who eat all the best food, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread upon the righteous with your might.

And you shall say: ‘We have acquired riches and possessions, And we have become great and glorious.’
But they shall say: ‘You have acquired them in unrighteousness, And your heart is full of pride.’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 94 is a series of woes pronounced against the sinners (particularly the rich and powerful who oppress the poor and trust in their wealth rather than in Yahuah (God) of Spirits). It contrasts sharply with the blessings promised to the righteous in previous chapters. The woes are directed at: - The rich who trust in their riches and forget Yahuah (v. 3–5) - Those who acquire wealth in unrighteousness and boast of it (v. 6–8) - Those who eat the best food, drink wine in bowls, and tread upon the poor (v. 6, 18, 20) - The mighty in wickedness and unrighteousness (v. 7, 21) The chapter ends with a renewed exhortation to the righteous (Enoch’s sons) to choose the path of righteousness so they may live, prosper, and have their seed multiplied — a direct echo of covenant blessings in Torah. This chapter is part of a larger section of woes and exhortations (chs. 94–105) that condemn the wicked (especially the wealthy oppressors) and encourage the righteous to persevere in faithfulness amid persecution. Scriptural Cross-References - Woe to the rich who trust in riches (vv. 3–5) Psalm 49:6–12 — Those who trust in their wealth… their inward thought is that their houses shall continue forever… but man in his pomp will not endure… like the beasts that perish. Luke 12:16–21 — Parable of the rich fool: “Soul, you have many goods laid up for many years… but God said to him, ‘Fool! This night your soul will be required of you.’” James 5:1–6 — Come now, you rich, weep and howl for your miseries… you have heaped up treasure in the last days… you have lived in pleasure on the earth and been wanton… you have condemned and murdered the just. - Woe to those who oppress the poor (vv. 6, 18, 20) Isaiah 3:14–15 — Yahuah (God) will enter into judgment with the elders and princes… It is you who have devoured the vineyard; the spoil of the poor is in your houses. What do you mean by crushing my people? Amos 2:6–7 — They sell the righteous for silver… they trample the head of the poor into the dust. James 5:4–6 — The wages of the laborers who mowed your fields, which you kept back by fraud, cry out… you have lived in luxury and pleasure… you have condemned the just. - Riches will not deliver in the day of affliction (v. 5) Proverbs 11:4 — Riches do not profit in the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from death. Zephaniah 1:18 — Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of Yahuah’s wrath. Ezekiel 7:19 — They shall cast their silver into the streets… their gold shall not be able to deliver them in the day of the wrath of Yahuah (God). - Choose righteousness, walk therein, live and prosper (vv. 7, 12, 16, 23) Deuteronomy 30:15–20 — See, I have set before you life and good, death and evil… choose life, that both you and your descendants may live. Psalm 1:1–3 — Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the wicked… he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water… whatever he does shall prosper. Proverbs 3:1–2 — My son, do not forget my law… for length of days and long life and peace they will add to you. - Paths of righteousness vs. unrighteousness (throughout) Psalm 1:6 — For Yahuah (God) knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the ungodly shall perish. Proverbs 4:18–19 — The path of the just is like the shining sun, that shines ever brighter unto the perfect day. The way of the wicked is like darkness; they do not know what makes them stumble. Matthew 7:13–14 — Narrow is the gate and difficult is the way which leads to life… broad is the way that leads to destruction. Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 94 is a powerful prophetic condemnation of the rich oppressors who trust in wealth, oppress the poor, and forget Yahuah (God) of Spirits. Their riches will fail them in the day of judgment. It contrasts sharply with the blessing promised to the righteous who walk humbly, love mercy, do justice, and fear Yahuah (God). This chapter echoes the social justice themes of the prophets and the teachings of Yeshua and James on wealth and oppression.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 95 continues the series of woes from Chapter 94, intensifying the condemnation of the wicked—especially the rich, the proud, the oppressors, and those who pervert truth. The chapter is structured as a prophetic oracle from Enoch, blending: - Repeated woes against the wealthy and powerful (vv. 1–16) — those who trust in riches, boast of acquisitions, indulge in luxury, oppress the poor/righteous, and live in pride. Their end is certain: sudden destruction, withering like grass, fiery furnace, and mockery in judgment (“Where are your riches now?”). - Renewed exhortation to the righteous (vv. 17–19) — choose righteousness, walk in it, live/prosper, multiply seed; unrighteousness will be cut off. The repetition of phrases (especially the “woe” formula and the reversal of riches/glory) drives home the certainty of judgment and the futility of trusting in material power over Yahuah (God) of Spirits. This chapter fits into the larger pattern of the Epistle: woe upon woe to the sinners (chs. 94–105), contrasted with hope and blessing for the faithful remnant who endure in righteousness. Scriptural Cross-References - Woe to the rich / trust in riches (vv. 1–3, 11–15) Psalm 49:6–12 — “Those who trust in their wealth and boast in the abundance of their riches… their inward thought is that their houses continue forever… but man in his pomp will not endure; he is like the beasts that perish.” Luke 6:24 — “But woe to you who are rich, for you have received your consolation.” James 5:1–3 — “Come now, you rich, weep and howl for your miseries that are coming upon you… you have heaped up treasure in the last days.” Proverbs 11:28 — “He who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous will flourish like foliage.” - Oppression of the poor / luxury at others’ expense (vv. 4, 6, 16, 18) Amos 6:4–7 — “Woe to those who lie on beds of ivory… eat lambs from the flock… drink wine from bowls… but are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph… therefore they shall now go captive.” Isaiah 5:8–12 — “Woe to those who join house to house… till there is no place… and you are left alone in the midst of the land… but they do not regard the work of Yahuah (God).” James 5:4–6 — “The wages of the laborers who mowed your fields, which you kept back by fraud, cry out… you have lived on the earth in luxury and in pleasure… you have fattened your hearts in a day of slaughter.” - Sudden destruction / withering like grass (vv. 10, 12) Psalm 37:2 — “For they will soon fade like the grass and wither like the green herb.” Isaiah 40:6–8 — “All flesh is grass… the grass withers, the flower fades… but the word of our Elohim (God) stands forever.” James 1:10–11 — “The rich in his humiliation, because as a flower of the field he will pass away… the sun rises with its scorching heat and withers the grass… so also will the rich man fade away.” - Choose righteousness / walk therein / live and prosper (vv. 17–19) Deuteronomy 30:19–20 — “Choose life, that both you and your descendants may live; that you may love Yahuah (God) your Elohim (God), that you may obey His voice.” Psalm 1:1–3 — “Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the ungodly… he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water… whatever he does shall prosper.” Proverbs 3:1–2 — “My son, do not forget my law… for length of days and long life and peace they will add to you.” Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 95 is pure prophetic fire: a relentless pronouncement of woe against the arrogant rich who oppress, boast, and forget Yahuah (God) of Spirits. Their wealth is temporary, their glory fleeting, their end the fiery furnace. The chapter ends with a clear call to the righteous (Enoch’s sons) to choose the path of righteousness for life, prosperity, and multiplication of seed. This is a direct continuation of the covenant curses/blessings motif — wealth without righteousness leads to ruin; humility before Yahuah (God) brings blessing. The message is stark: do not trust riches, do not oppress the poor, do not boast in power — fear Yahuah (God), walk humbly, do justice, and live.
