chapters.commentary: Chapter 96 continues the escalating series of woes from Chapters 94–95, intensifying the condemnation of the wicked — particularly the wealthy, the proud, the self-indulgent, and the oppressors. The chapter repeats and reinforces the same themes: - Woe to the rich and oppressive (vv. 1–14) — those who devour others’ strength, live in wickedness/oppression, feast on the best food/wine, tread upon the righteous/poor, acquire wealth unjustly, boast of possessions/power/glory, and exalt themselves as gods. Their end: sudden destruction, withering like grass, fiery furnace, and public humiliation in judgment (“Where are your riches now?”). - Renewed exhortation to the righteous (vv. 15–17) — Enoch’s sons are called yet again to choose righteousness, walk in it, live/prosper, multiply seed; unrighteousness will be cut off. The repetition is deliberate — a prophetic hammering home of the certainty of reversal: what the wicked trust in (wealth, might, luxury, pride) will fail them utterly. The chapter ends with the same covenant-style call: choose the righteous path for life and blessing. This chapter fits the Epistle’s pattern: relentless woes against sinners (especially the powerful who oppress the poor and forget Yahuah (God) of Spirits) contrasted with hope for the faithful who endure in righteousness. Scriptural Cross-References - Woe to the rich / oppressors / luxury at others’ expense (vv. 1–14) Isaiah 5:8–12 — “Woe to those who join house to house… till there is no place… and you are left alone… but they do not regard the work of Yahuah (God).” Amos 6:4–7 — “Woe to those who lie on beds of ivory… eat lambs from the flock… drink wine from bowls… but are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph… therefore they shall now go captive.” James 5:1–6 — “Come now, you rich, weep and howl… you have heaped up treasure in the last days… the wages of the laborers… cry out… you have lived in luxury… you have condemned the just.” Luke 6:24–25 — “But woe to you who are rich, for you have received your consolation. Woe to you who are full now, for you shall be hungry.” - Riches fail in judgment / withering like grass / fiery furnace (vv. 10–12) Psalm 37:2 — “For they will soon fade like the grass and wither like the green herb.” Isaiah 40:6–8 — “All flesh is grass… the grass withers, the flower fades… but the word of our Elohim (God) stands forever.” James 1:10–11 — “The rich in his humiliation, because as a flower of the field he will pass away… the sun rises with its scorching heat and withers the grass… so also will the rich man fade away.” Daniel 3:6 — “Whoever does not fall down and worship shall be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace” (symbol of judgment on the proud). - Choose righteousness / walk therein / live and prosper (vv. 15–17) Deuteronomy 30:19–20 — “Choose life, that both you and your descendants may live… love Yahuah (God) your Elohim (God)… obey His voice.” Psalm 1:1–3 — “Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the ungodly… whatever he does shall prosper.” Proverbs 3:1–2 — “Do not forget my law… for length of days and long life and peace they will add to you.” Psalm 37:3–5 — “Trust in Yahuah (God)… dwell in the land… delight yourself in Yahuah (God)… He shall give you the desires of your heart.” Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 95 is prophetic fire: a relentless pronouncement of woe against the arrogant rich who oppress, boast, indulge, and forget Yahuah (God) of Spirits. Their wealth/power/glory is temporary; judgment will expose pride and leave them empty — mocked, withered, cast into fire. The chapter ends with the same call as before: choose righteousness, walk in it, live/prosper, multiply seed. This is covenant language — obedience brings blessing, disobedience brings curse. The message is urgent: do not trust riches or power; fear Yahuah (God), walk humbly, do justice, and live.

But they shall say: ‘You have acquired them in unrighteousness, And your heart is full of pride.’
Woe to you who are mighty in unrighteousness! For your might shall be cut off.
And now, my sons, listen to me, And I will show you the paths of righteousness, And the paths of unrighteousness, And I will show you how the paths of unrighteousness Shall be cut off.
And now, my sons, choose for yourselves The paths of righteousness, And walk therein, That ye may live and prosper, And that your seed may be multiplied upon the earth.
And now I speak to you, my sons, And I show you the paths of righteousness, And the paths of unrighteousness, And I show you how the paths of unrighteousness Shall be cut off.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 97 continues the escalating series of woes from Chapters 94–96, intensifying the condemnation of the wicked — especially the rich, the proud, the self-indulgent, and the oppressors. The chapter repeats and reinforces the same themes: - Repeated woes against the powerful and self-indulgent (vv. 1–16) — those who work godlessness, glory in lying/oppression, alter words of uprightness, write unrighteous lies (creating their own judgment), are strong/mighty in wickedness/unrighteousness, live in fatness/luxury, drink wine in bowls, acquire wealth unjustly, boast of possessions/power/glory, and tread upon the poor/righteous. Their fate: sudden slaying, no peace, hunger/thirst, destruction like withering grass, fiery furnace, and mockery in judgment (“Where are your riches now?”). - Renewed exhortation to the righteous (vv. 17–19) — Enoch’s sons are called yet again to choose righteousness, walk in it, live/prosper, multiply seed; unrighteousness will be cut off. The repetition is deliberate — a prophetic hammering home of the certainty of judgment and the futility of trusting in material power over Yahuah (God) of Spirits. This chapter fits the Epistle’s pattern: relentless woes against sinners (especially the powerful who oppress the poor and forget Yahuah (God) of Spirits) contrasted with hope for the faithful who endure in righteousness amid persecution. Scriptural Cross-References - Woe to those who alter/pervert words of truth (v. 2) Jeremiah 8:8–9 — “How can you say, ‘We are wise, and the law of Yahuah (God) is with us’? But behold, the lying pen of the scribes has made it into a lie… the wise shall be put to shame.” Revelation 22:18–19 — “If anyone adds to these words… Elohim (God) will add to him the plagues… if anyone takes away… Elohim (God) will take away his share in the tree of life.” Deuteronomy 4:2 — “You shall not add to the word… nor take from it, that you may keep the commandments.” - Woe to the rich / trust in riches / sudden destruction (vv. 1–3, 11–15) Psalm 49:6–12 — “Those who trust in their wealth… their inward thought is that their houses continue forever… but man in his pomp will not endure; he is like the beasts that perish.” Luke 6:24–25 — “But woe to you who are rich, for you have received your consolation. Woe to you who are full now, for you shall be hungry.” James 5:1–3 — “Come now, you rich, weep and howl… you have heaped up treasure in the last days… your gold and silver are corroded.” Proverbs 11:28 — “He who trusts in his riches will fall, but the righteous will flourish like foliage.” - Woe to oppressors / luxury at others’ expense / treading on the poor (vv. 1, 4, 6, 16, 18) Amos 6:4–7 — “Woe to those who lie on beds of ivory… eat lambs from the flock… drink wine from bowls… but are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph… therefore they shall now go captive.” Isaiah 5:8–12 — “Woe to those who join house to house… till there is no place… and you are left alone… but they do not regard the work of Yahuah (God).” James 5:4–6 — “The wages of the laborers… which you kept back by fraud, cry out… you have lived in luxury… you have condemned the just.” Micah 2:1–2 — “Woe to those who devise iniquity… they covet fields and take them… oppress a man and his house.” - Sudden destruction / withering like grass / fiery furnace (vv. 10, 12) Psalm 37:2 — “For they will soon fade like the grass and wither like the green herb.” Isaiah 40:6–8 — “All flesh is grass… the grass withers, the flower fades… but the word of our Elohim (God) stands forever.” James 1:10–11 — “The rich in his humiliation, because as a flower of the field he will pass away… the sun rises with its scorching heat and withers the grass… so also will the rich man fade away.” Daniel 3:6 — “Whoever does not fall down and worship shall be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace” (symbol of judgment on the proud). - Choose righteousness / walk therein / live and prosper (vv. 15–19) Deuteronomy 30:19–20 — “Choose life, that both you and your descendants may live… love Yahuah (God) your Elohim (God)… obey His voice.” Psalm 1:1–3 — “Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the ungodly… whatever he does shall prosper.” Proverbs 3:1–2 — “Do not forget my law… for length of days and long life and peace they will add to you.” Psalm 37:3–5 — “Trust in Yahuah (God)… dwell in the land… delight yourself in Yahuah (God)… He shall give you the desires of your heart.” Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 96 is prophetic fire: a relentless pronouncement of woe against the arrogant rich who devour others’ strength, oppress the poor, indulge in luxury, and forget Yahuah (God) of Spirits. Their wealth/power/glory is temporary; judgment will expose pride and leave them empty — mocked, withered, cast into fire. The chapter ends with the same call as before: choose righteousness, walk in it, live/prosper, multiply seed. This is covenant language — obedience brings blessing, disobedience brings curse. The message is urgent: do not trust riches or power; fear Yahuah (God), walk humbly, do justice, and live.

chapters.title: Self-Indulgence of Sinners, Sin Originated by Man, All Sins Recorded in Heaven

verses.text: And now I swear unto you, to the wise and to the foolish, For ye shall have manifold experiences on the earth.

For ye men shall put on more adornments than a woman, And coloured garments more than a virgin: In royalty and in grandeur and in power, And in silver and in gold and in purple, And in splendour and in food they shall be poured out as water.

Therefore they shall be wanting in doctrine and wisdom, And they shall perish thereby together with their possessions; And with all their glory and their splendour, And in shame and in slaughter and in great destitution, Their spirits shall be cast into the furnace of fire.

I have sworn unto you, ye sinners, as a mountain has not become a slave, And a hill does not become the handmaid of a woman, Even so sin has not been sent upon the earth, But man of himself has created it, And under a great curse shall they fall who commit it.
And barrenness has not been given to the woman, But on account of the deeds of her own hands she dies without children.
I have sworn unto you, ye sinners, by the Holy Great One, That all your evil deeds are revealed in the heavens, And that none of your deeds of oppression are covered and hidden.
And do not think in your spirit nor say in your heart that ye do not know and that ye do not see That every sin is every day recorded in heaven in the presence of the Most High.
From henceforth ye know that all your oppression wherewith ye oppress is written down every day Till the day of your judgement.
Woe to you, ye fools, for through your folly shall ye perish: And ye transgress against the wise, and so good hap shall not be your portion.

And now, know ye that ye are prepared for the day of destruction: Wherefore do not hope to live, ye sinners, but ye shall depart and die; For ye know no ransom; for ye are prepared for the day of the great judgement, For the day of tribulation and great shame for your spirits.

Woe to you, ye obstinate of heart, who work wickedness and eat blood: Whence have ye good things to eat and to drink and to be filled? From all the good things which Yahuah (God) the Most High has placed in abundance on the earth; Therefore ye shall have no peace.

Woe to you who love the deeds of unrighteousness: Wherefore do ye hope for good hap unto yourselves? Know that ye shall be delivered into the hands of the righteous, And they shall cut off your necks and slay you, and have no mercy upon you.
Woe to you who rejoice in the tribulation of the righteous; For no grave shall be dug for you.
Woe to you who set at nought the words of the righteous; For ye shall have no hope of life.
Woe to you who write down lying and godless words; For they write down their lies that men may hear them and act godlessly towards their neighbour.
Therefore they shall have no peace but die a sudden death.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 98 intensifies the Epistle’s woes, shifting from wealth/oppression to self-indulgence, the human origin of sin, and the heavenly recording of all deeds. Enoch swears oaths (by the Holy Great One) to both wise and foolish, warning that luxury, pride, and hidden sins lead to fiery judgment and no peace. Key themes: sin is man’s creation (not imposed by Elohim (God)), all evil is documented in heaven for judgment day, and the wicked (who mock the righteous, eat blood unlawfully, write lies) face sudden death and no ransom. - Verses 1–3: Warning to all (wise/foolish) of earthly experiences; men exceed women in adornments/luxury (royalty, gold, purple, food poured out as water), leading to lack of wisdom/doctrine, perishing with possessions in shame/slaughter, spirits cast into fire. - Cross-refs: Isaiah 3:16–24 (haughty women of Zion adorned… judgment turns beauty to stench); 1 Timothy 2:9–10 (women adorn modestly… with good works); James 5:1–3 (rich weep… gold/silver corroded… heaped treasure in last days); Revelation 18:7–8 (Babylon glorified herself… plagues in one day). - Verses 4–5: Sin not sent by Elohim (like mountain not slave to woman); man creates it, falls under curse; barrenness from woman’s own deeds (no children). - Cross-refs: Genesis 3:16–19 (curse through man’s disobedience); James 1:13–15 (Elohim (God) tempts no one… sin from own desire); Romans 5:12 (sin entered through one man… death through sin); Deuteronomy 28:18 (cursed be fruit of womb for disobedience). - Verses 6–8: Evil deeds/oppression revealed in heavens, recorded daily before Most High till judgment. - Cross-refs: Malachi 3:16 (book of remembrance written before Yahuah (God)); Revelation 20:12–13 (books opened… dead judged by what written); Daniel 7:10 (books opened at judgment); Psalm 139:1–4 (Yahuah (God) knows thoughts afar off). - Verses 9–10: Fools perish through folly, transgress wise; prepared for destruction, no hope/ransom, day of great judgment/tribulation/shame. - Cross-refs: Proverbs 1:7 (fear of Yahuah (God) beginning of knowledge… fools despise wisdom); Hebrews 9:27 (appointed for man to die once, then judgment); Matthew 25:41,46 (depart into eternal fire… eternal punishment). - Verses 11–16: Woes on obstinate who work wickedness/eat blood (no peace despite abundance from Yahuah (God)); love unrighteousness (delivered to righteous for slaughter); rejoice in righteous’ tribulation (no grave); set nought righteous words (no hope of life); write lying/godless words (spread godlessness); sudden death, no peace. - Cross-refs: Leviticus 17:10–14 (eat no blood… life in blood); Acts 15:20,29 (abstain from blood); James 5:6 (condemned/murdered the just); Psalm 109:7–15 (wicked judged… no posterity); Revelation 21:8 (liars’ portion in lake of fire). Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 98 exposes self-indulgence and human-originated sin as root causes of judgment—Elohim (God) provides abundance, but man twists it into pride, oppression, and lies. All deeds recorded in heaven—no hiding. This debunks excuses like “sin is inevitable” or “traditions override truth”; Enoch stresses personal responsibility and heavenly accountability. Parallels NT warnings against luxury (James 5), blood-eating (Acts 15), and lying words (Rev 21). Test modern teachings that soften judgment or promote self-adornment/wealth—compare to Torah curses for disobedience (Deut 28) and hold fast to Yahuah’s unchanging order (Acts 17:11; 1 Thess 5:21). Choose wisdom over folly, righteousness over indulgence, for there is no ransom on judgment day except through humble repentance before Yahuah (God).

chapters.title: Woes on the Godless, Lawbreakers, and Idolaters; Evil Plight of Sinners in the Last Days

verses.text: Woe to you who work godlessness, And glory in lying and extol them: Ye shall perish, and no happy life shall be yours.
Woe to them who pervert the words of uprightness, And transgress the eternal law, And transform themselves into what they were not [into sinners]: They shall be trodden under foot upon the earth.

In those days make ready, ye righteous, to raise your prayers as a memorial, And place them as a testimony before the angels, That they may place the sin of the sinners for a memorial before the Most High.
In those days the nations shall be stirred up, And the families of the nations shall arise on the day of destruction.

And in those days the destitute shall go forth and carry off their children, And they shall abandon them, so that their children shall perish through them: Yea, they shall abandon their children (that are still) sucklings, and not return to them, And shall have no pity on their beloved ones.
And again I swear to you, ye sinners, that sin is prepared for a day of unceasing bloodshed.

And they who worship stones, and grave images of gold and silver and wood [and stone] and clay, And those who worship impure spirits and demons, And all kinds of idols not according to knowledge, shall get no manner of help from them.
And they shall become godless by reason of the folly of their hearts, And their eyes shall be blinded through the fear of their hearts And through visions in their dreams.
Through these they shall become godless and fearful; For they shall have wrought all their work in a lie, And shall have worshipped a stone: Therefore in an instant shall they perish.

But in those days blessed are all they who accept the words of wisdom, and understand them, And observe the paths of the Most High, and walk in the path of His righteousness, And become not godless with the godless; For they shall be saved.
Woe to you who spread evil to your neighbours; For you shall be slain in Sheol.
Woe to you who make deceitful and false measures, And (to them) who cause bitterness on the earth; For they shall thereby be utterly consumed.
Woe to you who build your houses through the grievous toil of others, And all their building materials are the bricks and stones of sin; I tell you ye shall have no peace.
Woe to them who reject the measure and eternal heritage of their fathers And whose souls follow after idols; For they shall have no rest.
Woe to them who work unrighteousness and help oppression, And slay their neighbours until the day of the great judgement.

For He shall cast down your glory, And bring affliction on your hearts, And shall arouse His fierce indignation And destroy you all with the sword; And all the holy and righteous shall remember your sins.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 99 escalates the woes against godlessness, law-perverters, idolaters, and oppressors, while calling the righteous to prepare prayers as memorials before angels and the Most High. It depicts societal chaos (nations stirred, parents abandoning children), the futility of idolatry (no help from false gods), and swift destruction for liars and exploiters. In contrast, the wise/righteous who walk Yahuah’s paths are blessed and saved. This chapter bridges personal sin warnings to end-times upheaval and judgment. - Verses 1–2: Woes on those who practice/work godlessness, glory in lying, pervert upright words, transgress eternal law, become sinners—they perish without happy life, trodden under foot. - Cross-refs: Isaiah 5:20 (“Woe to those who call evil good and good evil”); Psalm 52:1–5 (boast in evil… Elohim (God) will destroy forever); Romans 1:18–25 (suppress truth in unrighteousness… exchanged truth for lie, worshipped creatures). - Verses 3–5: Righteous prepare prayers as memorial/testimony before angels/Most High; nations/families rise in destruction; destitute abandon children (even sucklings) without pity. - Cross-refs: Malachi 3:16 (book of remembrance before Yahuah (God)); Revelation 5:8 / 8:3–4 (prayers of saints as incense before throne); Deuteronomy 28:56–57 (siege horrors: tender woman eats her children); Lamentations 4:10 (compassionate women boiled their children). - Verse 6: Sin prepared for day of unceasing bloodshed. - Cross-refs: Isaiah 26:21 (Yahuah (God) comes out of His place to punish inhabitants for blood… earth discloses blood); Revelation 16:6 (shed blood of saints… given blood to drink). - Verses 7–9: Idol-worshippers (stones, gold/silver/wood/clay images, impure spirits/demons) get no help; folly blinds hearts/eyes via fear/dreams; work in lies, perish instantly. - Cross-refs: Isaiah 44:9–20 (idol-makers deluded… feed on ashes); Jeremiah 10:3–5 (idols like scarecrow… cannot speak/do good); Psalm 115:4–8 (idols of silver/gold… those who make them become like them); 1 Corinthians 10:19–20 (sacrifice to demons, not Elohim (God)). - Verse 10: Blessed are those who accept wisdom, understand, observe Most High’s paths/righteousness, avoid godless company—they are saved. - Cross-refs: Proverbs 2:1–11 (receive wisdom… walk in way of good); Psalm 1:1–3 (not walk in counsel of wicked… blessed/delights in law); Matthew 7:24–25 (hears/does words… like wise man on rock); James 1:22–25 (doers of word, not hearers only). - Verses 11–16: Woes on evil-spreaders (slain in Sheol), false measures/bitterness-causers (consumed), builders on others’ toil/sin-bricks (no peace), rejectors of fathers’ heritage/idol-followers (no rest), unrighteous/oppressors/slayers (glory cast down, affliction, sword destruction; righteous remember sins). - Cross-refs: Amos 8:5–6 (false balances… trample needy); Micah 2:1–2 (devise iniquity… oppress neighbor); James 5:4 (wages withheld cry out); Revelation 18:6–8 (pay her back double… plagues in one day); Psalm 109:14–15 (sins of fathers remembered before Yahuah (God)). Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 99 exposes idolatry, law-perversion, exploitation, and societal breakdown as hallmarks of the godless—leading to instant perishing and no rest/peace. Yet the righteous are called to active prayer and faithfulness, promised salvation amid chaos. This debunks modern deceptions like relativism (“truth is subjective”) or idolizing wealth/power/traditions over Yahuah’s eternal law. Enoch warns sin brings bloodshed and abandonment; Scripture echoes: idolatry blinds (Rom 1), oppression curses (Jas 5), but wisdom/paths of righteousness save (Prov 2; Mt 7). Test all things—compare to Torah’s warnings against false gods (Deut 4:15–19) and injustice (Amos 5), hold fast to Yahuah’s unchanging truth (Acts 17:11; 1 Thess 5:21). In end-times upheaval, prepare memorials of prayer, walk humbly, and reject the godless path.

chapters.title: The Sinners Destroy Each Other; Judgment of the Fallen Angels; Safety of the Righteous; Further Woes for the Sinners

verses.text: And in those days in one place the fathers together with their sons shall be smitten, And brothers one with another shall fall in death Till the streams flow with their blood.

For a man shall not withhold his hand from slaying his sons and his sons’ sons, And the sinner shall not withhold his hand from his honoured brother: From dawn till sunset they shall slay one another.
And the horse shall walk up to the breast in the blood of sinners, And the chariot shall be submerged to its height.

In those days the angels shall descend into the secret places And gather together into one place all those who brought down sin, And the Most High will arise on that day of judgement To execute great judgement amongst sinners.

And over all the righteous and holy He will appoint guardians from amongst the holy angels To guard them as the apple of an eye, Until He makes an end of all wickedness and all sin, And though the righteous sleep a long sleep, they have nought to fear.

And (then) the children of the earth shall see the wise in security, And shall understand all the words of this book, And recognize that their riches shall not be able to save them In the overthrow of their sins.
Woe to you, Sinners, on the day of strong anguish, Ye who afflict the righteous and burn them with fire: Ye shall be requited according to your works.
Woe to you, ye obstinate of heart, Who watch in order to devise wickedness: Therefore shall fear come upon you And there shall be none to help you.
Woe to you, ye sinners, on account of the words of your mouth, And on account of the deeds of your hands which your godlessness has wrought, In blazing flames burning worse than fire shall ye burn.

And now, know ye that from the angels He will inquire as to your deeds in heaven, from the sun and from the moon and from the stars in reference to your sins because upon the earth ye execute judgement on the righteous.
And He will summon to testify against you every cloud and mist and dew and rain; for they shall all be withheld because of you from descending upon you, and they shall be mindful of your sins.
And now give presents to the rain that it be not withheld from descending upon you, nor yet the dew, when it has received gold and silver from you that it may descend.
When the hoar-frost and snow with their chilliness, and all the snow-storms with all their plagues fall upon you, in those days ye shall not be able to stand before them.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 100 depicts the horrific self-destruction of sinners in the last days (family slaughter, blood-flowing streams), the gathering and judgment of the sin-bringers (Watchers/fallen angels) by the Most High, the protected security of the righteous (guarded by holy angels like the apple of the eye), and woes on those who afflict/burn the righteous or plot wickedness. Creation itself (sun, moon, stars, clouds, rain, frost) will testify against the sinners, withholding blessings due to their oppression of the righteous. Riches fail to save; judgment is inescapable and requited exactly according to works. - Verses 1–3: Fathers/sons, brothers slay one another till blood floods streams, horses/chariots submerged in it—total societal/family breakdown in violence. - Cross-refs: Zechariah 14:13 (Yahuah (God) causes confusion… every man’s hand against his neighbor); Micah 7:6 (son dishonors father… man’s enemies are those of his own house); Matthew 10:21 (brother delivers brother to death… children rise against parents); Revelation 6:4 (power given to take peace from earth… men slay one another). - Verse 4: Angels descend to secret places, gather sin-bringers (Watchers); Most High arises for great judgment on sinners. - Cross-refs: 2 Peter 2:4 (angels who sinned cast into chains of darkness… reserved for judgment); Jude 1:6 (angels who did not keep position… kept in eternal chains under darkness); Revelation 20:1–3 (angel binds Satan… cast into abyss). - Verse 5: Righteous/holy guarded by holy angels as apple of eye until wickedness/sin ends; even in death (“long sleep”), no fear. - Cross-refs: Deuteronomy 32:10 (Yahuah (God) guarded Israel as apple of His eye); Psalm 17:8 (keep me as apple of Your eye); Zechariah 2:8 (touching the apple of His eye); Psalm 116:15 (precious in sight of Yahuah (God) is death of His saints); 1 Thessalonians 4:13–14 (sleep in death… Elohim (God) will bring with Him). - Verse 6: Earth’s children see wise in security, understand this book’s words, realize riches cannot save from sin’s overthrow. - Cross-refs: Psalm 49:6–9 (those trusting riches… cannot redeem soul); Proverbs 11:4 (riches profit not in day of wrath… righteousness delivers from death); James 5:1–3 (rich weep… heaped treasure in last days… corroded); Matthew 6:19–21 (do not store treasures on earth… where moth/rust destroy). - Verses 7–9: Woes on sinners afflicting/burning righteous (requited by works), obstinate heart plotting wickedness (fear, no help), words/deeds of godlessness leading to worse-than-fire flames. - Cross-refs: Romans 2:6 (Yahuah (God) repays each according to works); Matthew 25:41–46 (depart into eternal fire… as you did to least of these); Revelation 20:12–13 (judged according to works… death/Sheol give up dead); James 3:6 (tongue set on fire by Gehenna). - Verses 10–13: Angels/sun/moon/stars/clouds/mist/dew/rain testify against sinners (withheld blessings due to oppression); give bribes to rain/dew in vain; frost/snow/plagues overwhelm, no standing. - Cross-refs: Deuteronomy 28:23–24 (sky bronze… dust instead of rain); Job 37:6–13 (snow/rain for correction or mercy); Amos 4:7–8 (withheld rain… yet not return to Me); Revelation 16:21 (great hail from heaven… men blasphemed Elohim (God)); Hosea 2:21–22 (heavens hear earth… grain/wine/oil hear Jezreel). Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 100 unveils end-times horror: sinners’ self-destruction, angelic gathering for judgment, creation testifying against oppressors, and the righteous’ angelic protection—even through death. Riches/works of wickedness offer no escape; requital is exact. This exposes deceptions like “sin has no consequences” or “wealth secures future”—Enoch stresses accountability before the Most High, with nature itself withholding provision. Parallels NT judgment by works (Rom 2; Rev 20) and protection of saints (Zech 2; Ps 17). Test traditions that minimize accountability or exalt riches—compare to Torah curses for injustice (Deut 28) and prophets’ calls to repentance (Amos 4). Hold fast: fear Yahuah (God), walk righteousness, trust angelic guardianship (Acts 17:11; 1 Thess 5:21). In tribulation, the righteous endure secure; the godless fall without help.

chapters.title: Exhortation to Observe the Works of Heaven and Earth; Fear Yahuah (God) of Spirits

verses.text: Observe ye how the ships are borne on the waves of the sea by the winds, How they all fear and tremble before the face of the winds.
For all the winds fear and tremble before His face, And all the ships are afraid upon the sea.
And all the watchers fear and tremble before Him, And all the hosts of heaven tremble and are afraid at His presence.
And the foundations of the earth tremble, And the pillars of heaven are moved at His rebuke.
And all the luminaries in the heaven tremble, And the foundations of the earth are moved, And the pillars of the heaven are shaken at His rebuke.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 101 is a short but powerful exhortation to “observe” the obedience of creation (ships on sea, winds, luminaries, foundations of earth/heaven) as they all fear and tremble before Yahuah’s rebuke. This contrasts sharply with humanity’s rebellion (implied from previous chapters), urging fear of Yahuah (God) of Spirits as the proper response. The repetition emphasizes the universal awe of creation before the Creator—nothing disobeys or resists His presence. - Verses 1–2: Ships borne on waves by winds, yet all fear/tremble before the winds’ face—illustration of created things’ vulnerability and submission. - Cross-refs: Psalm 107:23–30 (they that go down to sea… see works of Yahuah (God)… He commands winds/storms… they are still); Jonah 1:4–5 (great wind/storm… mariners afraid); Job 38:8–11 (Yahuah (God) set bounds for sea… “Thus far shall you come”). - Verses 3–4: Watchers (angels), hosts of heaven, foundations of earth, pillars of heaven tremble/move at His rebuke. - Cross-refs: Job 26:11 (pillars of heaven tremble… at His rebuke); Psalm 104:7 (at Your rebuke waters flee); Habakkuk 3:6 (He stood and measured earth… everlasting mountains scattered… His ways everlasting); Isaiah 24:18–20 (earth reels like drunkard… foundations tremble). - Verses 5–13 (and repeated motifs): Luminaries afraid, foundations moved, earth quakes, mountains/hills displaced, sea troubled—everything trembles at His presence/rebuke. - Cross-refs: Psalm 18:7 (earth shook/rocked… foundations trembled at His anger); Nahum 1:5–6 (mountains quake… earth heaves… who can stand before His indignation?); Revelation 6:14 (sky receded like scroll… mountains/islands moved); Haggai 2:6 (I will shake heavens/earth/sea/dry land). Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 101 uses creation’s universal fear and trembling before Yahuah’s rebuke as a mirror: if ships, winds, angels, luminaries, earth, sea, mountains—all obey without question—how much more should man fear and reverence Yahuah (God) of Spirits? This reinforces earlier themes (chs. 2–5) of nature’s perfect order vs. human pride/rebellion. It debunks deceptions that portray Elohim (God) as distant or lenient—He is awesome, His presence shakes foundations. Scripture echoes: fear Yahuah (God) is beginning of wisdom (Prov 1:7; 9:10), and creation testifies to His power (Ps 19:1; Rom 1:20). Test modern teachings that downplay reverence or treat Yahuah (God) casually—compare to Torah’s awe at Sinai (Ex 19:16–18) and prophets’ visions (Isa 6; Hab 3). Hold fast: observe creation’s submission, fear Yahuah (God), walk humbly (Acts 17:11; 1 Thess 5:21; Mic 6:8). In His presence, no rebellion stands.

chapters.title: Woes on the Sinners Who Die Without Hope; The Souls of the Righteous in Sheol Await Vindication

verses.text: And now, my sons, I tell you these things, That I may show you the paths of righteousness, And the paths of unrighteousness, And that ye may know what shall befall the righteous and the sinners.
And in those days the righteous shall be separated from the sinners, And the spirits of the sinners shall be separated from the spirits of the righteous.
And the souls of the righteous shall be in the hand of Elohim (God), And no torment shall touch them.
And behold! the souls of the sinners shall be in Sheol, And they shall lament and cry out in great pain, And their lamentation shall ascend to heaven, And their cry shall reach the gates of heaven.
And they shall say: "Why have we not been requited according to our works? Why have we not received according to our deeds?"
And they shall see the righteous in their habitations, And they shall say: “These are they who have despised us and trodden us under foot.”
And they shall see the righteous shining like the sun, And they shall say: “These are they who have walked in righteousness before Yahuah (God) of Spirits.”
Woe to you, ye sinners, when ye have died, If ye die in the wealth of your sins! For no requital shall be made to you.
Woe to you who are strong in unrighteousness! For your strength shall be cut off, And your glory shall not endure.
Woe to you who eat the marrow of wheat, And drink the finest wine, And tread upon the poor with your might!
Woe to you who are full of fatness! For ye shall be hungry, And ye shall thirst.
Woe to you who drink wine in large bowls, And tread upon the poor with your might.
Woe to you who acquire gold and silver in unrighteousness And say: "We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And we have acquired everything that we have desired."
And now let us do what we purposed: For we have gathered silver, And many are the husbandmen in our houses.
And our granaries are brimful as with water, And your husbandmen shall be many.
And your labourers shall be many, Even though they be few.
And they shall exalt you like a king, And they shall call you gods.
But ye shall be destroyed like grass, And like the young grass that withers, And ye shall be cast into the fiery furnace.
And they shall say to you: "Where are your riches now, And where are your possessions, And where is your glory, And where is your power?"
And ye shall say: "We have acquired riches and possessions, And we have become great and glorious."
But they shall say: "Ye have acquired them in unrighteousness, And your heart is full of pride."
Woe to you, O sinners! For your riches shall not endure, And your glory shall not last.
And now, my sons, listen to me, And I will show you the paths of righteousness, And the paths of unrighteousness, And I will show you how the paths of unrighteousness Shall be cut off.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 102 contrasts the fate of the righteous and sinners after death. The righteous souls rest securely in Elohim’s hand with no torment, while sinners’ souls in Sheol cry out in pain, lamenting their lack of requital and seeing the righteous honored. It returns to woes on the wealthy sinners who die in unrighteousness, repeating themes of riches failing, pride exposed, and fiery destruction. The chapter urges discernment between paths of righteousness (leading to vindication) and unrighteousness (cut off). - Verses 1–3: Righteous separated from sinners; righteous souls safe in Elohim’s hand, no torment touches them. - Cross-refs: Psalm 31:5 (“Into Your hand I commit my spirit”); Psalm 116:15 (“Precious in the sight of Yahuah (God) is the death of His saints”); Luke 23:46 (Yahusha (Jesus): “Father, into Your hands I commit My spirit”); Revelation 14:13 (“Blessed are the dead who die in the Master… they rest from their labors”). - Verses 4–7: Sinners’ souls in Sheol lament/cry to heaven’s gates; question lack of requital; see righteous in habitations, shining like sun, recognized as walkers in righteousness before Yahuah (God) of Spirits. - Cross-refs: Isaiah 14:9–11 (Sheol stirred… kings rise… “Are you also weak as we?”); Luke 16:23–26 (rich man in Hades in torment… sees Abraham afar); Daniel 12:2–3 (“Many who sleep in dust awake… some to everlasting life… shine like brightness of firmament”); Matthew 13:43 (“Righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom”). - Verses 8–23: Woes on sinners dying in wealth/sins (no requital), strong in unrighteousness (strength cut off), luxury/oppressors (eat marrow, drink finest wine, tread poor), full of fatness (hungry/thirsty), unjust riches/boasting (acquire all desired, granaries full, exalted as gods)—destroyed like grass, cast into fiery furnace, riches/glory/power questioned and exposed as unrighteous/prideful; renewed call to choose righteousness paths. - Cross-refs: Psalm 49:16–20 (do not fear when man becomes rich… his glory not descend after him); James 5:1–6 (rich weep/howl… lived in luxury… condemned just); Luke 12:16–21 (rich fool: “Soul, many goods laid up… this night your soul required”); Psalm 37:1–2 (do not fret evildoers… soon fade like grass); Revelation 18:7–8 (glorified herself… plagues in one day); Deuteronomy 30:15–19 (“Choose life… love Yahuah (God)… walk in His ways”). Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 102 reveals post-death reality: righteous secure in Elohim’s hand, shining in vindication; sinners tormented in Sheol, crying for justice they never gave, watching their riches fail. Luxury and oppression bring no lasting glory—only exposure and fire. This debunks deceptions like “live for now, no afterlife accountability” or “wealth proves favor”—Enoch stresses eternal requital and separation. Parallels NT parables (rich man/Lazarus in Luke 16) and resurrection hope (Dan 12; Rev 14). Test teachings that ignore judgment or exalt material success—compare to Torah blessings/curses (Deut 28–30) and prophets’ warnings (Isa 14). Hold fast: fear Yahuah (God), reject unrighteous paths, walk in righteousness for eternal rest and shining reward (Acts 17:11; 1 Thess 5:21). The righteous endure; the godless lament forever.

chapters.title: Blessings on the Righteous After Death; Curses on the Sinners; Books of Life and Unrighteousness

verses.text: And now I swear unto you, ye righteous, By the greatness of His splendour and His glory, By His greatness I swear unto you.
That I have seen, and the light has shone upon me, And I have seen the holy ones of heaven, And I have beheld the books of life.
And your spirits have been found worthy of the lot of the righteous, And your names are written in the books of life before the Most High.
And the righteous shall be victorious in the name of Yahuah (God) of Spirits: And He will cause His light to appear on them, And He will make peace for them.
And the righteous shall be victorious over the sinners, And they shall see their destruction, And they shall rejoice over them.
But woe to you, ye sinners, who are dead in your sins! Ye shall have no peace.
And as for the righteous, they shall be satisfied with life, And their spirits shall not perish.
And their memorial shall be before the Most High, And their name shall not be blotted out.
And I saw the books of the living, And the books of the unrighteous were opened, And the names of the sinners were found therein.
And their spirits shall be cast into darkness and destruction, And they shall cry out and lament in Sheol.
And their cry shall not be heard, And their lamentation shall not ascend to heaven.
And their deeds shall be requited according to their works, And according to the measure of their unrighteousness.
Woe to you who are godless in heart, Who watch to devise wickedness: Therefore shall fear come upon you, And there shall be none to help you.
Woe to you who eat all the best food, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread upon the righteous with your might.
Woe to you who acquire gold and silver in unrighteousness, And say: "We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And we have acquired everything that we have desired."
And now let us do what we purposed: For we have gathered silver, And many are the husbandmen in our houses.
And our granaries are brimful as with water, And your husbandmen shall be many.
And your labourers shall be many, Even though they be few.
And they shall exalt you like a king, And they shall call you gods.
But ye shall be destroyed like grass, And like the young grass that withers, And ye shall be cast into the fiery furnace.
And they shall say to you: "Where are your riches now, And where are your possessions, And where is your glory, And where is your power?"
And ye shall say: "We have acquired riches and possessions, And we have become great and glorious."
But they shall say: "Ye have acquired them in unrighteousness, And your heart is full of pride."
Woe to you, O sinners! For your riches shall not endure, And your glory shall not last.
And now, my sons, listen to me, And I will show you the paths of righteousness, And the paths of unrighteousness, And I will show you how the paths of unrighteousness Shall be cut off.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 103 brings comfort to the righteous and final condemnation to the sinners. Enoch swears by Yahuah’s splendor that the righteous’ names are written in the books of life, their spirits victorious and shining in peace/light. Sinners die without peace, their names in books of unrighteousness, spirits cast into darkness/Sheol with unheard cries, requited exactly by works. It repeats woes on godless hearts, luxury/oppressors, and unjust riches—ending in destruction like grass, fiery furnace, exposed pride, and no lasting glory. The chapter reinforces eternal separation and accountability. - Verses 1–5: Oath to righteous by Yahuah’s greatness/glory; Enoch has seen holy ones/books of life; righteous spirits worthy, names written before Most High, victorious in Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ name, light/peace granted, victorious over sinners, rejoice at their destruction. - Cross-refs: Psalm 69:28 (“Let them be blotted out of the book of the living”); Daniel 12:1 (“Your people delivered, everyone found written in the book”); Philippians 4:3 (“Names in the book of life”); Revelation 3:5 (“He who overcomes… name not blotted out of Book of Life”); Revelation 20:12–15 (“Books opened… another book, Book of Life… judged by works”). - Verses 6–8: Sinners dead in sins have no peace; righteous satisfied with life, spirits not perish, memorial before Most High, name not blotted out. - Cross-refs: Psalm 112:6 (“Righteous remembered forever”); Isaiah 26:19 (“Your dead shall live… earth give birth to departed spirits”); John 11:25–26 (“I am the resurrection and the life… whoever believes in Me shall never die”); Revelation 2:10–11 (“Be faithful unto death… not hurt by second death”). - Verses 9–12: Books of living/unrighteous opened; sinners’ names found, spirits in darkness/destruction, cry/lament in Sheol unheard, deeds requited by works/unrighteousness measure. - Cross-refs: Revelation 20:13–15 (“Death and Hades gave up dead… judged according to works… not in Book of Life cast into lake of fire”); Matthew 16:27 (“Son of Man come… reward each according to deeds”); Romans 2:6–8 (“Repay each according to works… eternal life to those seeking glory/honor/immortality”). - Verses 13–25: Woes on godless hearts devising wickedness (fear, no help), luxury/oppressors (best food/wine, tread righteous/poor), unjust riches/boasting (acquire all, granaries full, exalted as gods)—destroyed like grass, fiery furnace, riches/glory/power questioned/exposed as unrighteous/prideful; renewed call to choose righteousness paths. - Cross-refs: Psalm 37:2 (“They soon fade like grass”); James 1:10–11 (“Rich fade away like flower of field”); Isaiah 40:6–8 (“All flesh is grass… word of our Elohim (God) stands forever”); Luke 12:19–21 (“Soul, many goods… fool! this night your soul required”); Deuteronomy 30:19 (“Choose life… that you and your descendants may live”). Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 103 offers profound hope: righteous names eternally in books of life, victorious, shining, at peace—while sinners face no peace, unheard cries in darkness, exact requital by works. Riches/oppression bring temporary exaltation but ultimate exposure and fire. This debunks lies like “death ends all” or “good deeds outweigh bad without repentance”—Enoch stresses books of record, eternal separation, and Yahuah’s perfect justice. Parallels NT assurance (Phil 4; Rev 3/20) and judgment by works (Rom 2; Mt 16). Test teachings that ignore afterlife accountability or promote self-justification—compare to Torah’s memorial of righteous (Ps 112) and prophets’ warnings (Isa 40). Hold fast: fear Yahuah (God), walk righteousness, trust your name in His book through humble faith (Acts 17:11; 1 Thess 5:21). The righteous triumph forever; the godless perish without memorial.

chapters.title: Joy for the Righteous Written in Books; They Become Companions of Angels; Sinners’ Lies Exposed; Encouragement to the Righteous

That I have seen, and the light has shone upon me, And I have seen the holy ones of heaven, And I have beheld the books of life.
