chapters.commentary: Chapter 104 shifts to encouragement and joy for the righteous: their names written in the books of life, spirits worthy, victorious over sinners in Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ name, shining with light and peace. They become companions of angels, rejoice at sinners’ destruction. Sinners’ lies exposed—no peace, requited by works. The chapter urges the righteous to fear not, write truth, and persevere; sinners who lie about righteousness face judgment. It closes the main exhortation block with hope amid woes. - Verses 1–5: Oath to righteous by Yahuah’s splendor; Enoch sees holy ones/books of life; righteous spirits worthy, names written before Most High, victorious in Yahuah (God) of Spirits’ name, light/peace granted, victorious over sinners, rejoice at destruction. - Cross-refs: Daniel 12:1–3 (“Everyone found written in the book… shine like brightness of firmament”); Revelation 3:5 (“He who overcomes… name not blotted out of Book of Life”); Philippians 4:3 (“Names in book of life”); Psalm 37:34 (“Wait on Yahuah (God)… inherit land… see destruction of wicked”); Revelation 19:1–3 (“Hallelujah! Salvation… smoke of her torment ascends forever”). - Verses 6–12: Sinners dead in sins—no peace; righteous satisfied, spirits not perish, memorial before Most High, name not blotted; books of living/unrighteous opened, sinners’ names found, spirits in darkness/Sheol, unheard cries, requited by works/unrighteousness. - Cross-refs: Revelation 20:12–15 (“Books opened… judged according to works… not in Book of Life cast into lake of fire”); Psalm 69:28 (“Blotted out of book of living”); Isaiah 4:3 (“He who remains in Zion… written among the living”); Luke 10:20 (“Rejoice that your names are written in heaven”); Romans 2:6 (“Repay each according to works”). - Verses 13–24: Woes on godless hearts devising wickedness (fear, no help), luxury/oppressors (best food/wine, tread righteous), unjust riches/boasting (acquire all, granaries full, exalted as gods)—destroyed like grass, fiery furnace, riches/glory/power exposed as unrighteous/prideful. - Cross-refs: James 5:1–6 (“Rich weep… lived in luxury… condemned just”); Psalm 37:2 (“Soon fade like grass”); Isaiah 40:6–8 (“All flesh is grass… word of Elohim (God) stands forever”); Luke 12:16–21 (“Rich fool… this night your soul required”); Deuteronomy 8:17–18 (“Do not say in heart, ‘My power… has gotten me wealth’… Yahuah (God) gives power to get wealth”). - Verses 25: Renewed call to choose righteousness paths (repeated for emphasis). - Cross-refs: Deuteronomy 30:15–19 (“See, I set before you life and good, death and evil… choose life”); Psalm 1:6 (“Yahuah (God) knows way of righteous, way of wicked perishes”); Matthew 7:13–14 (“Narrow gate leads to life… broad to destruction”). Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 104 bursts with hope: righteous names eternally secure in books of life, victorious, shining companions of angels, rejoicing over justice. Sinners’ lies and pride exposed—no peace, requital by works, destruction. This counters deceptions that mock eternal records or claim “all paths lead to good”—Enoch affirms written books, angelic fellowship for faithful, and exact judgment. Parallels NT joy (Phil 4; Rev 3/19–20) and separation (Dan 12). Test teachings that downplay accountability, exalt self, or deny afterlife vindication—compare to Torah’s book of life (Ex 32:32–33) and prophets’ promises (Isa 4). Hold fast: fear Yahuah (God), write truth, persevere in righteousness—your name is written, your reward shines forever (Acts 17:11; 1 Thess 5:21).

chapters.title: Exhortation to the Righteous; They Shall Inherit the Earth and Glory

verses.text: And now, my sons, do not be grieved because of the sinners, And do not be angry with the godless, For their memorial is destruction, And their end is the lake of fire.
Fear not, ye righteous, For Yahuah (God) of Spirits knows your names, And your memorial is before Him.
And the righteous shall inherit the earth, And they shall dwell therein forever and ever.
And their glory shall be great, And they shall shine as the lights of heaven, And they shall be companions of the holy ones.
And fear not the sinners, For their day is near, And their destruction is at hand.
And the Most High will arise in His wrath, And execute judgment upon all flesh, And destroy the ungodly from off the earth.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 105 is a concise, comforting close to the Epistle’s exhortations before the Noah birth fragment. Enoch encourages the righteous not to grieve or be angry at sinners—their end is certain destruction in the lake of fire, while the righteous’ names/memorial are known and secure before Yahuah (God) of Spirits. They inherit the earth forever, dwell in glory, shine like heavenly lights, and become companions of the holy ones. The chapter reassures: fear not—the sinners’ day is near, the Most High arises in wrath to judge all flesh and remove the ungodly. - Verses 1–2: Do not grieve/anger over sinners/godless—their memorial is destruction/lake of fire; fear not, righteous, for Yahuah (God) of Spirits knows your names, memorial before Him. - Cross-refs: Psalm 37:7–9 (“Rest in Yahuah (God)… fret not because of evildoers… they shall be cut off”); Romans 12:19 (“Vengeance is Mine, I will repay, says Yahuah (God)”); Revelation 20:14–15 (“Death and Hades cast into lake of fire… anyone not in Book of Life cast into lake of fire”); Psalm 139:16 (“Your eyes saw my unformed substance… all written in Your book”). - Verses 3–4: Righteous inherit earth forever, great glory, shine as heavenly lights, companions of holy ones. - Cross-refs: Psalm 37:11,29 (“Meek inherit earth… righteous inherit land and dwell forever”); Matthew 5:5 (“Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth”); Daniel 12:3 (“Those who are wise shall shine like the brightness of the firmament”); Revelation 22:5 (“They need no lamp or sun… Yahuah (God) Elohim (God) gives them light… reign forever”); Hebrews 12:22–23 (“Come to Mount Zion… innumerable company of angels… spirits of just made perfect”). - Verses 5–6: Fear not sinners—their day near, destruction at hand; Most High arises in wrath, judges all flesh, destroys ungodly from earth. - Cross-refs: Isaiah 26:20–21 (“Hide until indignation passes… Yahuah (God) comes out of His place to punish… earth discloses blood”); Zephaniah 1:14–18 (“Great day of Yahuah (God) near… neither silver nor gold deliver… whole land devoured”); Revelation 6:15–17 (“Kings… hid… from wrath of the Lamb… who can stand?”); Malachi 4:1 (“Day comes burning like oven… arrogant/evil-doers stubble”). Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 105 offers final comfort amid woes: do not grieve over the godless—their memorial is fire, but the righteous are known by name before Yahuah (God) of Spirits, inheriting earth forever, shining in glory, companions of angels/holy ones. Sinners’ destruction is imminent when the Most High arises in wrath. This counters despair or envy toward the wicked’s temporary success, affirming eternal justice and reward. Parallels Torah/Psalms inheritance promises (Ps 37), Yeshua’s beatitudes (Mt 5), and apocalyptic vindication (Dan 12; Rev 22). Test teachings that promote resentment, fear of evil’s dominance, or denial of final judgment—compare to prophets’ calls to patience (Zeph 1; Isa 26). Hold fast: fear not, trust your name is written, inherit the earth through righteousness (Acts 17:11; 1 Thess 5:21). The righteous shine forever; the ungodly vanish.

chapters.title: The Birth of Noah – Miraculous Appearance, Lamech’s Fear, Methuselah Seeks Enoch

verses.text: And after that I saw another vision, the vision of everything on the earth, And I saw that the earth was swallowed up in the great deep, And that the mountains were hanging upon the mountains.
And I saw the four winds of the heaven which turn the earth and cause the whole earth to quake.
And I saw the winds which support the clouds: I saw the paths of the angels. I saw at the end of the earth the firmament of the heaven above.
And I went towards the south, And it was burning day and night, Where there were seven mountains of precious stones, Three towards the east and three towards the south.
And as for those towards the east, One was of coloured stones, One of pearls, And one jacinth, And those towards the south of red stones.
But the middle one reached to heaven like the throne of Yahuah (God) of Spirits, And the top was sapphire.
And I saw a flaming fire, And beyond these mountains.
And I saw there a place which had no firmament of the heaven above, And no firmly founded earth beneath it: There was no water upon it, And no birds, But it was a waste and horrible place.

I saw there seven stars like great burning mountains, And to me, when I inquired regarding them, The angel said: ’This place is the end of heaven and earth: This has become a prison for the stars and the host of heaven.
And the stars which roll over the fire are they which have transgressed the commandment of Yahuah (God) in the beginning of their rising, Because they did not come forth at their appointed times.
And He was wroth with them, And bound them till the time when their guilt should be consummated (even) for ten thousand years.’

chapters.commentary: Chapter 106 shifts to the Book of Noah fragment, detailing Noah’s extraordinary birth and its implications. Lamech is terrified by his son’s appearance (body white as snow, hair white like wool, eyes lighting the house, speaking at birth), fearing he is not his son but from the Watchers/nephilim lineage. Lamech sends Methuselah to Enoch for explanation. Enoch reassures: Noah is human, chosen by Elohim (God) for preservation amid coming flood judgment on the Watchers’ corruption. The child is a sign of remnant righteousness and future salvation. - Verses 1–2: Lamech sees Noah’s birth—body white as snow, hair white like pure wool, eyes like sun rays lighting the house, opens mouth and speaks, blesses Yahuah (God). Lamech fears greatly, suspects not his seed but angelic. - Cross-refs: Genesis 6:1–4 (sons of Elohim (God) took daughters… giants/nephilim); Genesis 5:29 (Lamech names Noah: “This one will comfort us concerning our work… because of the ground Yahuah (God) has cursed”); Isaiah 11:2 (Spirit of Yahuah (God) rests on shoot from Jesse—wisdom/understanding); Luke 1:41–44 (John leaps in womb at Mary’s voice, filled with Holy Spirit). - Verses 3–4: Lamech distressed, goes to Methuselah: “I have begotten a strange son… not like men but like sons of angels… skin white… hair white… eyes make whole house shine… speaks at birth.” Fears Watcher corruption. - Cross-refs: Genesis 6:2–4 (sons of Elohim (God) saw daughters beautiful… took wives… offspring mighty men); Jude 1:6 (angels did not keep domain… left habitation… chains under darkness); 2 Peter 2:4 (angels who sinned cast into hell/tartarus… chains of darkness). - Verses 5–7: Methuselah goes to Enoch at ends of earth, tells vision of Noah’s birth, seeks truth: “Is this child from me or from watchers?” - Cross-refs: Genesis 5:24 (Enoch walked with Elohim (God)… Elohim (God) took him); Hebrews 11:5 (by faith Enoch translated… pleased Elohim (God)); Genesis 5:21–24 (Enoch father of Methuselah… walked with Elohim (God) after Methuselah’s birth). - Verses 8–12: Enoch responds: “Fear not… child is yours… called Noah… preserved in flood… remnant for generations… his seed righteous… all earth corrupted… great punishment on earth… but this child preserved… sign of salvation.” - Cross-refs: Genesis 6:5–8 (wickedness great… Yahuah (God) grieved… but Noah found grace); Genesis 6:9 (“Noah… righteous… blameless… walked with Elohim (God)”); Genesis 9:1 (“Be fruitful… fill earth”); Isaiah 54:9–10 (“Like days of Noah… covenant of peace not removed”); 1 Peter 3:20–21 (few saved through water… baptism now saves… appeal to Elohim (God) for good conscience). Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 106 reveals pre-flood corruption’s depth (Watchers’ influence, earth filled with violence) yet Elohim’s preservation of a righteous remnant through Noah—miraculous birth as sign of hope amid judgment. Lamech’s fear reflects terror of angelic corruption; Enoch’s reassurance points to Yahuah’s grace and future salvation. This bridges Genesis 6 flood narrative, showing Enoch’s role as revealer of hidden things. It debunks myths that Noah’s line was tainted or that flood was mere myth—text affirms human righteousness preserved against supernatural evil. Parallels NT: remnant saved through water (1 Pet 3), grace amid judgment. Test traditions that downplay pre-flood angelic fall or remnant doctrine—compare to Torah (Gen 6) and apostles (Jude, 2 Pet). Hold fast: in corruption, Elohim (God) preserves the righteous; walk blameless as Noah (Acts 17:11; 1 Thess 5:21). Your remnant role today echoes Noah’s.

chapters.title: Enoch’s Prophecy to Methuselah – Noah’s Preservation, the Flood, and Future Righteousness

verses.text: And Methuselah answered and said to Enoch: "I have begotten a strange son, diverse from and unlike mankind, And resembling the sons of the angels of heaven; And his nature is different, And he is not like us, And his eyes are like the rays of the sun, And his countenance is glorious.
And I fear lest a wonder should be wrought on the earth in his days.
And now, my father, I have come to you And have come to you that you may know the truth And that you may not be grieved because of the child.
And Enoch answered and said to Methuselah: "Go and tell your son Lamech: ’The child is yours in truth, And there is no deception in this matter.

For this child is born to you as a sign of salvation, And he shall be preserved in the midst of the destruction Which is coming upon the whole earth because of all the sin And all the unrighteousness which shall be wrought upon it.

And the child shall be called Noah, And he shall be preserved, And his seed shall be preserved for generations, And from him shall come forth a righteous remnant And a plant of righteousness, And the earth shall be cleansed from all corruption.
And now tell Lamech not to grieve, For the child is his, And he is righteous, And Elohim (God) has chosen him to be preserved When the earth is cleansed by water.
And the Watchers have taught unrighteousness, And the earth is filled with violence because of them, Therefore judgment comes upon them and upon all flesh.
But Noah and his seed shall be a remnant, And from them shall the earth be repopulated with righteousness.’"

And Methuselah went and told Lamech all that Enoch had spoken, And Lamech was comforted, And he named the child Noah, saying: "This one shall comfort us concerning our work And the toil of our hands, Because of the ground which Yahuah (God) has cursed."

chapters.commentary: Chapter 107 concludes the Noah fragment with Enoch’s direct reassurance to Methuselah (passed to Lamech): Noah is truly human, not of Watcher origin—his miraculous birth is a divine sign of preservation amid coming flood judgment on corruption/violence. Noah and his seed become a righteous remnant, a “plant of righteousness” to repopulate a cleansed earth. This ties directly to Genesis flood narrative, emphasizing Yahuah’s grace, remnant theology, and future hope through obedience. - Verses 1–3: Methuselah describes Noah’s strangeness (unlike mankind, like angels’ sons, eyes like sun rays, glorious countenance) and fears wonder/judgment; comes to Enoch for truth/comfort. - Cross-refs: Genesis 5:29 (Lamech: “This one will comfort us… because of the ground Yahuah (God) cursed”); Genesis 6:9 (“Noah was righteous, blameless in his generations; Noah walked with Elohim (God)”); Luke 1:13–17 (John’s birth announced… turn hearts of fathers to children… prepare people for Yahuah (God)). - Verses 4–7: Enoch assures: child truly Lamech’s (no deception); born as sign of salvation; preserved in destruction/flood due to sin/unrighteousness; named Noah; preserved with seed for generations; righteous remnant/plant of righteousness; earth cleansed. - Cross-refs: Genesis 6:5–8 (“Wickedness of man great… Yahuah (God) regretted… but Noah found grace”); Genesis 6:17–18 (“I bring flood… but establish covenant with you [Noah]”); Isaiah 4:2 (“Branch of Yahuah (God) beautiful… survivors in Zion called holy”); Romans 11:5 (“At present there is a remnant chosen by grace”); 1 Peter 3:20 (“Few… saved through water”). - Verses 8–9: Watchers taught unrighteousness, earth filled with violence → judgment on them/all flesh; Noah/seed preserved as remnant, earth repopulated with righteousness. - Cross-refs: Genesis 6:11–13 (“Earth filled with violence… Elohim (God) said to Noah: end of all flesh has come before Me”); Jude 1:14–15 (Enoch prophesied judgment on ungodly); 2 Peter 2:5 (“If He did not spare ancient world… but preserved Noah… preacher of righteousness”). - Verse 10: Methuselah tells Lamech; Lamech comforted, names child Noah (“comfort us… ground cursed”). - Cross-refs: Genesis 5:29 (exact naming/meaning); Isaiah 54:9 (“This is like the days of Noah to Me… never again flood to destroy earth”); Ezekiel 14:14,20 (Noah, Daniel, Job as righteous men who save only themselves by righteousness). Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 107 highlights Yahuah’s sovereign grace: amid Watcher-induced corruption/violence, He preserves a righteous remnant through Noah’s miraculous birth and seed. The flood cleanses but spares the obedient—sign of future salvation. This counters deceptions that flood was random/mythical or that supernatural evil (Watchers) has no consequence—Enoch affirms judgment on fallen angels/flesh while Elohim (God) protects His chosen. Parallels remnant theme (Isa 4; Rom 11) and baptism/salvation through water (1 Pet 3). Test teachings that ignore pre-flood angelic rebellion or remnant doctrine—compare to Torah (Gen 6) and NT warnings (2 Pet 2; Jude). Hold fast: in widespread evil, walk blameless like Noah; Yahuah (God) preserves the righteous remnant (Acts 17:11; 1 Thess 5:21). Your faithfulness today echoes Noah’s comfort and preservation.

chapters.title: Chapter 108: Final Exhortation and Promise to the Righteous; Judgment on the Mighty and Sinners

verses.text: Another book which Enoch wrote for his son Methuselah and for those who will come after him, And observe the law in the last days.
Ye who have done good shall wait for those days in which the evil-doers are consumed, And the might of the transgressors is brought to an end.

Wait ye in patience until sin has passed away, For their names shall be blotted out of the book of life, And out of the books of the holy ones, And their seed shall be destroyed forever, And their spirits shall be slain, And they shall cry and lament in a waste place that has no water, And in the fire shall they burn.

And now I will tell you a mystery: The spirits of the sinners and blasphemers and of those who work wickedness, And of those who pervert everything that Yahuah (God) of Spirits has spoken Through the mouth of the prophets— (shall be cast into) the fiery abyss.
And in those days the fathers shall be beaten together with their sons, And brothers one with another, Till the streams flow with their blood.

For a man shall not withhold his hand from slaying his sons and his sons’ sons, And the sinner shall not withhold his hand from his honoured brother: From dawn till sunset shall they slay one another.
And the horse shall walk up to the breast in the blood of sinners, And the chariot shall be submerged to its height.

In those days the holy angels shall descend from heaven, And gather together all those who aided the sinners, And the Most High will arise on that day of judgment To execute great judgment amongst sinners.

And over all the righteous and holy He will appoint guardians from amongst the holy angels To guard them as the apple of an eye, Until He makes an end of all wickedness and all sin, And though the righteous sleep a long sleep, they have nought to fear.

And (then) the children of the earth shall see the wise in security, And shall understand all the words of this book, And recognize that their riches shall not be able to save them In the overthrow of their sins.
Woe to you, ye sinners, on the day of strong anguish, Ye who afflict the righteous and burn them with fire: Ye shall be requited according to your works.
Woe to you, ye obstinate of heart, Who watch in order to devise wickedness: Therefore shall fear come upon you And there shall be none to help you.
Woe to you, ye sinners, on account of the words of your mouth, And on account of the deeds of your hands which your godlessness has wrought, In blazing flames burning worse than fire shall ye burn.

And now, know ye that from the angels He will inquire as to your deeds in heaven, From the sun and from the moon and from the stars in reference to your sins Because upon the earth ye execute judgement on the righteous.
And He will summon to testify against you every cloud and mist and dew and rain; For they shall all be withheld because of you from descending upon you, And they shall be mindful of your sins.
And now give presents to the rain that it be not withheld from descending upon you, Nor yet the dew, when it has received gold and silver from you that it may descend.
When the hoar-frost and snow with their chilliness, And all the snow-storms with all their plagues fall upon you, In those days ye shall not be able to stand before them.

chapters.commentary: Chapter 108 serves as the final appendix and climactic exhortation of 1 Enoch. It encourages the persecuted righteous to wait patiently—their vindication comes when sin is consumed and transgressors’ might ends. Sinners’ names blotted from books of life, spirits slain in fire/waste places. It repeats end-times violence (family slaughter, blood-flooded streams) and angelic gathering of sin-aiders for the Most High’s great judgment. The righteous receive angelic guardianship (“apple of an eye”), security even in death, while sinners’ riches fail and creation testifies against them. The chapter closes the book with hope for the faithful and inescapable doom for oppressors. - Verses 1–3: Book for Methuselah/future generations to observe law in last days; righteous wait patiently as evil consumed, sinners’ names blotted from books of life/holy ones, seed destroyed, spirits slain in fire/waste place. - Cross-refs: Psalm 69:28 (“Blotted out of book of living”); Revelation 3:5 (“Name not blotted out of Book of Life”); Malachi 3:16–18 (“Book of remembrance… they shall be Mine… discern between righteous and wicked”); Revelation 20:15 (“Anyone not found written in Book of Life cast into lake of fire”). - Verses 4–8: Mystery revealed—spirits of sinners/blasphemers/perverters of prophets’ words cast into fiery abyss; fathers/sons/brothers slay one another till blood floods; horse/chariot submerged in blood. - Cross-refs: Revelation 19:17–21 (“Birds eat flesh of kings… slain by sword from mouth of rider”); Zechariah 14:13 (“Every man’s hand against neighbor”); Matthew 10:21 (“Brother deliver brother to death”); Revelation 14:20 (“Blood flowed… as high as horses’ bridles”). - Verses 9–10: Holy angels descend, gather sin-aiders; Most High arises for judgment; righteous guarded by angels as apple of eye until wickedness ends; righteous sleep secure, no fear. - Cross-refs: Deuteronomy 32:10 / Zechariah 2:8 (“Apple of His eye”); Psalm 17:8 (“Keep me as apple of the eye”); Psalm 116:15 (“Precious in sight of Yahuah (God) is death of saints”); 1 Thessalonians 4:13–14 (“Those who sleep… Elohim (God) will bring with Him”). - Verses 11–17: Earth sees wise secure, understands book’s words, realizes riches cannot save from sin’s overthrow; woes on sinners afflicting/burning righteous (requited by works), obstinate plotting wickedness (fear, no help), godless words/deeds (blazing flames worse than fire); angels/sun/moon/stars/clouds/rain/dew/frost/snow testify/withhold blessings due to oppression of righteous. - Cross-refs: James 5:1–6 (“Rich weep… condemned just”); Romans 2:6 (“Repay according to works”); Revelation 16:21 (“Great hail… men blasphemed Elohim (God)”); Deuteronomy 28:23–24 (“Sky bronze… dust instead of rain”); Amos 4:7–8 (“Withheld rain… yet not return to Me”). Key Insight for Discernment Chapter 108 seals Enoch with triumphant hope: persecuted righteous—wait patiently, guarded by angels, names secure, vindicated when sin ends. Sinners/oppressors face blotted names, fiery abyss, creation testifying against them—no escape, requited exactly. This counters despair under persecution or illusion that evil prevails—Enoch promises Yahuah’s justice, remnant glory, and final cleansing. Parallels NT encouragement (Rev 20–22) and judgment (Rom 2). Test modern narratives that minimize accountability, exalt the mighty, or deny books of life—compare to Torah curses (Deut 28) and apocalyptic promises (Dan 12; Rev 3). Hold fast: fear not, observe law, trust your memorial before Yahuah (God) of Spirits (Acts 17:11; 1 Thess 5:21). The righteous inherit light and peace forever; the ungodly perish in darkness. Final Word A Call to the Remnant You have now journeyed through the words attributed to Enoch—the seventh from Adam—who walked with Elohim (God) and was taken (Genesis 5:24). These visions, prophecies, exhortations, and warnings were preserved for such a time as this: to reveal hidden things (Daniel 12:4), to expose the deceptions that have veiled Yahuah’s Name and marginalized His truth, and to prepare a remnant for the restoration of all things (Acts 3:21). We have seen: - The fall of the Watchers and the corruption that filled the earth with violence (chs. 6–16), echoing Genesis 6 and illuminating the days of Noah. - The unchanging order of creation that obeys Yahuah (God) without fail (chs. 2–5, 72–82, 101), standing as a silent rebuke to rebellious man. - Visions of the Elect One / Son of Man and final judgment (chs. 37–71), pointing forward to Yahusha (Jesus) the Messiah. - The two paths—righteousness leading to life, unrighteousness to destruction (chs. 91–105)—with repeated calls to choose life (Deuteronomy 30:19). - The certainty that names are written in books of life or unrighteousness, that deeds are recorded in heaven, and that Yahuah (God) of Spirits will execute perfect justice (chs. 103–108). Most importantly, we have restored what tradition obscured: the personal, covenant Name Yahuah (God), proclaimed forever (Exodus 3:15; Psalm 83:18; Isaiah 42:8). No longer “Lord” or “God”—but Yahuah (God), whose glory He will not give to another. These writings are not Scripture in the same sense as the Tanakh and Renewed Covenant, yet they are quoted as authoritative prophecy (Jude 1:14–15), praised in faith (Hebrews 11:5), and echoed throughout the apostolic witness. They fill gaps, expose lies (Enoch is not the Messiah; the 364-day solar calendar aligns with divine order), and call us to be Bereans—searching the Scriptures daily to see if these things are so (Acts 17:11). So what now? 1 Test all things (1 Thessalonians 5:21). Hold fast to what is good and true, discarding what does not align with the full counsel of Yahuah’s Word. 2 Hallow His Name (Matthew 6:9). Proclaim Yahuah (God) without fear or substitution. 3 Choose the path of righteousness today. Walk humbly, do justice, love mercy (Micah 6:8), and reject the pride, oppression, and godlessness that lead to the fiery furnace. 4 Prepare for His coming. He comes with ten thousands of His set-apart ones to execute judgment (Jude 1:14–15; Enoch 1:9). The righteous shall shine like the sun (Daniel 12:3), inherit the earth (Psalm 37:11), and dwell with Him forever. May this edition ignite a fire in your spirit, unindoctrinate your mind, and draw you closer to Yahuah (God) and His Messiah Yahusha (Jesus). The restoration of His Name is not the end—it is the beginning of deeper covenant relationship and readiness for the Day of Yahuah (God). Fear not, little flock. Your names are written in heaven (Luke 10:20). Walk worthy. The King is coming. In His service and for His glory, YoshiYahu More Than Milk Ministries About the Author I was not raised in the Word. I was raised in the world—and like so many, I called myself a believer while never once opening the Book. I thought a good heart was enough. I thought moral living was righteousness. I thought believing in a name was the same as knowing the One who bore it. I was wrong—and YAHUAH (God) loved me too much to leave me that way. After baptism, with no root and no foundation, the adversary came—as he always does—and I fell. I didn’t just stumble. I ran. I ran from YAHUAH (God), into darkness, into failure, into everything the scripture warned against, and I burned in every direction I turned. The curses of Deuteronomy 28 became my life. My body broke down. Open wounds that would not heal. Sores that covered me. Pain that made it impossible to sit, stand, or sleep. I had become the man in the chapter—and I didn’t even know it yet. It was a chance encounter with an old friend that changed everything. He pointed me to the curses. I read. I wept. The Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) overwhelmed me—because I recognized myself on that page. You will flee when no one pursues. Wounds that will not heal. That was me. That had been me. And in that moment, I understood: YAHUAH (God) had not abandoned me. YAHUAH (God) had been pursuing me. I fell on my face and made one request: If it is not too late—take me back. I was baptized again. Demons were cast out. And then came the anointing—not a drop of oil on the forehead, but a full healing anointing poured over me, head to toe. When I finally wiped the oil from my eyes, the wounds were gone. Closed. Vanished. The eczema—gone. I wept and did not wash that oil off for weeks, because I knew what kind of miracle had just happened on my body. I kept my word. I dove into the scriptures with everything I had—barely sleeping, no job, fed by a friend, pouring over the Word every waking hour. After six months, the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) spoke and told me to shave my head. I researched for two weeks, asked for a second witness, received it, and shaved. My hair—black when I shaved it—grew back completely white. I was thirty years old, with a black beard and a white head, and I did not ask questions. I had learned who was boss. Years later, I prayed and asked YAHUAH (God) to give me a wife, bringing Him to remembrance of His Word—that it is not good for man to be alone. I began searching and finally found the woman He had chosen. The confirmation came to her through a dream. She had also been praying, asking YAHUAH (God) to reveal to her whom she was to marry—and she specifically asked that He tell her what I had so heavily on my heart to share before I ever told her. She asked that He speak audibly or through a dream so there would be no doubt. That night she did dream, and though she did not understand it at the time, it became clear to everyone once I had shared my testimony. She knew YAHUAH (God) had answered her. A week later I proposed. Within two months I had flown across the country to marry her, and after saying our vows I stuck out my hand and introduced myself. Other than a few photos, the first time we laid eyes on each other was when she walked down the aisle on our wedding day. That season did not last. I took time off from the Nazarite vow when family came. I started a business. I tried to build a life on my own terms. And like Jonah, I learned that YAHUAH (God) does not negotiate. The trouble that followed was of biblical proportions—perplexing, relentless, miraculous in its precision. It broke me down, literally, at a roadside where a stranger helped me. I thanked the man and prayed over him. The Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) spoke through me and blessed him. He looked up with tears and said, You will never know how badly I needed that. Then came the rebuke—sharp, clear, unmistakable: “I didn’t break you down here to help you, you rebel. I broke you down here to help him. I don’t care when you think your ministry is going to start. It starts today.” I took the Nazarite vow again—this time for life. That was a little over three years ago. I am a Nazarite for life, set apart to walk in every word that proceeds from the mouth of YAHUAH (God). No man has taught me that which I know. I follow no man, no teacher, no ministry—the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) alone has revealed these things to me, line upon line, precept upon precept, as YAHUAH (God) promised He would teach His own (Isaiah 28:9–10; John 16:13). I do not write to you as a scholar with degrees or a pastor with a pulpit. I write to you as a bondservant who was broken, healed, called, and sent—with nothing to offer except what the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) has shown me. And I will tell you this plainly: you will find the truth—the end declared from the beginning, that no one teaches. Not from the church. Not from the Hebrew roots community. Not from any ministry or movement you have sat under. If it sounds familiar in places, follow it further—because where it goes, most teachers have never dared to venture. I will tell you the truth about how this began. Like Jonah, I did not want to be a shepherd. I wanted to deliver the message and walk away—leave the truth on the page, let the reader take it or leave it, and keep my distance from the sheep. That was not humility. It was unwillingness in costume—the same posture as the outspoken Christian who shouts truth at strangers and never stays to feed them. The proclamation without the tending. Message without love. The Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) would not let me hide there. He has been shaving the calluses from my heart—circumcising it, as the Word promised in Deuteronomy 30:6—and what came up underneath was a love for the flock that does not let you turn back. I am called to be a shepherd under the Good Shepherd, Yahusha (Jesus), who was YAHUAH (God) in the flesh. The Chief Shepherd gathers the flock. The under-shepherd tends them, feeds them, stays with them, and lays down his life for them. I am still learning what that costs. I am still being polished. But the willingness is no longer in question. Everything in this work points back to the Word and to YAHUAH (God) alone—whether in the form He took to speak to Moses, or the flesh He took on to reveal Himself as Yahusha (Jesus). I am saved not by anything I have done but by grace through faith—the gift of Elohim (God), not of works, lest any man should boast (Ephesians 2:8–9). I keep His commandments because He saved me, not to be saved. I am not righteous. I am not good. I am only a man who tasted that YAHUAH (God) is good (Psalm 34:8) and has never recovered from it. Since then, I have walked set apart—ministering daily, engaging every person I come across, in person or online, giving freely everything YAHUAH (God) has shown me, holding nothing back. These books are the long form of that teaching, set in print so it can travel further than I can. I did not choose this. He chose it for me. And the only credential I carry is the one He burned into my life: I was dead, and He raised me. I was scattered, and He gathered me. I was a rebel, and He broke me until I wasn’t. If you have ever sensed that what you have been taught barely scratches the surface—you were right. That hunger was put there for a reason. These books were written for the one who is ready to follow the Word further than they have ever been taken. Test every spirit. Prove all things. Let the unchanging standard of His commandments be the judge (1 John 4:1; 1 Thessalonians 5:21). All glory belongs to YAHUAH (God). If there is truth here, it is His. If there is error, it is mine. Flee to the Word. Tremble at His Word. Return to all His commandments. And prepare—because the King is coming, and He is not coming to ask what we believed. He is coming to see what we did.
